require './lib/profanity_filter'

filter = ProfanityFilter.new
comments = [
  "This is a clean comment.",
  "This is a bad word: sh*t",
  "Another profanity: f*ck",
  "Mixed case: SHiT",
  "Partial match: shithead",
  "No profanity here."
]

comments.each do |comment|
  puts "Original: #{comment}"
  puts "Filtered: #{filter.filter(comment)}"
  puts "----------"
end
```

# Ruby Implementation for Parsing and Normalizing US Postal Addresses

Here's a complete solution that parses and normalizes US postal addresses from free text. The implementation uses the `addressable` gem for address parsing and normalization.

## Gemfile

gem 'usaddress', '~> 0.14'  # For US address parsing
gem 'ffaker', '~> 3.3'      # For generating test data (optional)
```

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'usaddress'
require 'addressable/uri'

class AddressNormalizer
  def initialize
    # Configure the USAddress parser
    @parser = USAddress::Parser.new
  end

  # Normalize a single address string
  def normalize_address(address)
    return nil unless address.is_a?(String) && address.strip.present?

    parsed = @parser.parse(address)

    if parsed && parsed.any?
      normalized = {}
      normalized[:street] = parsed.street_address
      normalized[:city] = parsed.city
      normalized[:state] = parsed.state
      normalized[:zip] = parsed.zip5
      normalized[:zip_plus4] = parsed.zip4 if parsed.zip5 && parsed.zip4
      normalized[:country] = 'US'

      # Handle cases where city and state might be swapped
      if normalized[:city] && normalized[:state] && normalized[:city].length == 2 && normalized[:state].length > 2
        normalized[:state], normalized[:city] = normalized[:city], normalized[:state]
      end

      normalized
    else
      nil
    end
  end

  # Normalize an array of addresses
  def normalize_addresses(addresses)
    addresses.map { |addr| normalize_address(addr) }.compact
  end

  # Get a formatted address string from a normalized hash
  def format_address(normalized)
    return nil unless normalized.is_a?(Hash)

    parts = []

    # Street address
    if normalized[:street]
      parts << normalized[:street]
    end

    # City
    if normalized[:city]
      parts << normalized[:city]
    end

    # State and ZIP
    if normalized[:state] && normalized[:zip]
      parts << "#{normalized[:state]} #{normalized[:zip]}"
    elsif normalized[:state]
      parts << normalized[:state]
    elsif normalized[:zip]
      parts << normalized[:zip]
    end

    # Combine all parts
    parts.join(', ')
  end

  # Validate if an address is normalized correctly
  def valid_normalized?(normalized)
    normalized.is_a?(Hash) &&
    normalized[:street].present? &&
    normalized[:city].present? &&
    normalized[:state].present? &&
    normalized[:zip].present? &&
    normalized[:country] == 'US'
  end
end
```

```ruby
# app/profanity_filter.rb
class ProfanityFilter
  # List of common English profanity words to filter
  PROFANITY_WORDS = [
    'shit', 'fuck', 'bitch', 'asshole', 'dick', 'piss', 'cunt',
    'damn', 'hell', 'bastard', 'whore', 'slut', 'dumb', 'stupid',
    'idiot', 'moron', 'retard', 'loser', 'jerk', 'twat', 'prick',
    'bloody', 'bugger', 'arsed', 'sod', 'bollocks', 'wanker',
    'muppet', 'douche', 'douchebag', 'pig', 'rat', 'minger', 'muppet'
  ].freeze

  def self.filter(comment)
    return '' if comment.nil?

    # Convert to lowercase for case-insensitive matching
    lower_comment = comment.downcase
    # Mark each profanity word with asterisks
    profanity_words = PROFANITY_WORDS.map(&:downcase)

    profanity_words.each do |word|
      # Use a regex pattern to match the word as a whole word
      regex = /\b#{Regexp.escape(word)}\b/i
      comment.gsub!(regex, '*' * word.length)
    end

    comment
  end
end

Here's a complete solution that includes a Gemfile and Ruby implementation for converting DOCX documents to both HTML and plain text formats.

## Gemfile

```

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'docx'
require 'nokogiri'
require 'html2plaintext'

class DocxConverter
  def initialize(docx_path)
    @docx_path = docx_path
  end

  # Convert DOCX to HTML
  def to_html
    doc = Docx::Document.open(@docx_path)
    builder = Nokogiri::XML::Builder.new do |xml|
      xml.html {
        xml.head {
          xml.meta('charset' => 'UTF-8')
          xml.title { xml.text "Converted from #{File.basename(@docx_path)}" }
          xml.style(type: 'text/css') {
            xml.text <<-CSS
              body { font-family: Arial, sans-serif; line-height: 1.5; }
              p { margin: 0 0 1em 0; }
              h1 { font-size: 2em; margin: 0.67em 0; }
              h2 { font-size: 1.5em; margin: 0.75em 0; }
              h3 { font-size: 1.17em; margin: 0.83em 0; }
            CSS
          }
        }
        xml.body {
          doc.paragraphs.each do |paragraph|
            if paragraph.style_name == 'Heading 1'
              xml.h1 { xml.text paragraph.to_s }
            elsif paragraph.style_name == 'Heading 2'
              xml.h2 { xml.text paragraph.to_s }
            elsif paragraph.style_name == 'Heading 3'
              xml.h3 { xml.text paragraph.to_s }
            else
              xml.p { xml.text paragraph.to_s }
            end
          end
        }
      }
    end

    builder.to_html
  end

  # Convert DOCX to plain text
  def to_plain_text
    html = to_html
    Html2Plaintext.convert(html)
  end

  # Save HTML to a file
  def save_html(output_path)
    File.write(output_path, to_html)
  end

  # Save plain text to a file
  def save_plain_text(output_path)
    File.write(output_path, to_plain_text)
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0
  if ARGV.size < 1
    puts "Usage: #{$0} <input.docx> [output.html] [output.txt]"
    exit(1)
  end

  input_file = ARGV[0]
  output_html = ARGV[1] || "#{File.basename(input_file, '.docx')}.html"
  output_txt = ARGV[2] || "#{File.basename(input_file, '.docx')}.txt"

  converter = DocxConverter.new(input_file)
  converter.save_html(output_html)
  converter.save_plain_text(output_txt)

  puts "Conversion complete:"
  puts "HTML saved to: #{output_html}"
  puts "Plain text saved to: #{output_txt}"
end
```

## Gemfile

## Implementation

```ruby
# company_matcher.rb
require 'fuzzy_match'
require 'levenshtein'
require 'jaro_winkler'

class CompanyMatcher
  def initialize(company_names)
    @company_names = company_names.uniq.compact
    @fuzzy_matcher = FuzzyMatch.new(@company_names)
  end

  # Find all potential matches for a given company name
  def find_matches(company_name, threshold = 0.7, max_results = 5)
    {
      levenshtein_matches: find_levenshtein_matches(company_name, max_results),
      jaro_winkler_matches: find_jaro_winkler_matches(company_name, threshold, max_results),
      fuzzy_matches: find_fuzzy_matches(company_name, max_results)
    }
  end

  private

  def find_levenshtein_matches(company_name, max_results)
    # Calculate Levenshtein distances and sort by distance
    @company_names.map do |name|
      { name: name, distance: Levenshtein.distance(company_name, name) }
    end.sort_by { |match| match[:distance] }.take(max_results)
  end

  def find_jaro_winkler_matches(company_name, threshold, max_results)
    # Calculate Jaro-Winkler similarity and filter by threshold
    @company_names.map do |name|
      similarity = JaroWinkler.similarity(company_name, name)
      { name: name, similarity: similarity } if similarity >= threshold
    end.compact.sort_by { |match| -match[:similarity] }.take(max_results)
  end

  def find_fuzzy_matches(company_name, max_results)
    # Use FuzzyMatch's built-in scoring system
    @fuzzy_matcher.find_all(company_name, max_results).map do |name|
      { name: name, score: @fuzzy_matcher.score(company_name, name) }
    end.sort_by { |match| -match[:score] }.take(max_results)
  end
end

## Gemfile

gem 'textaclean', '~> 2.0'  # For text preprocessing

# For handling document collections
gem 'active_record', '~> 7.0'  # Optional, if you want database storage

## Implementation

Here's a complete implementation of TF-IDF and document similarity in Ruby:

```ruby
# lib/tf_idf_analyzer.rb
require 'matrix'
require 'set'
require 'textaclean'

class TFIDFAnalyzer
  def initialize(documents)
    @documents = documents
    @vocabulary = Set.new
    @document_terms = []
    @term_frequencies = []
    @document_frequencies = {}
    @document_vectors = []
  end

  def preprocess(text)
    # Basic text preprocessing
    Textaclean::TextCleaner.new(text).clean(
      :remove_html_tags,
      :remove_urls,
      :remove_emails,
      :remove_numbers,
      :remove_punctuation,
      :to_lower_case,
      :remove_short_words # words with length < 3
    ).split
  end

  def build_vocabulary
    @documents.each_with_index do |doc, doc_index|
      terms = preprocess(doc)
      @document_terms << terms
      @vocabulary.merge(terms)
    end

    # Calculate term frequencies in each document
    @document_terms.each do |doc_terms|
      frequencies = Hash.new(0)
      doc_terms.each { |term| frequencies[term] += 1 }
      @term_frequencies << frequencies
    end

    # Calculate term document frequencies
    @vocabulary.each do |term|
      @document_frequencies[term] = 0
      @document_terms.each do |doc_terms|
        @document_frequencies[term] += 1 if doc_terms.include?(term)
      end
    end
  end

  def calculate_tf_idf_vectors
    build_vocabulary

    @vocabulary.each do |term|
      idf = Math.log(@documents.size.to_f / @document_frequencies[term])

      @document_terms.each_with_index do |doc_terms, doc_index|
        tf = @term_frequencies[doc_index][term].to_f / doc_terms.size
        tf_idf = tf * idf

        @document_vectors[doc_index] ||= {}
        @document_vectors[doc_index][term] = tf_idf
      end
    end

    # Convert to matrix representation
    @document_vectors.each_with_index do |vec, i|
      @document_vectors[i] = @vocabulary.map do |term|
        vec[term] || 0
      end
    end

    @document_vectors = Matrix.rows(@document_vectors)
  end

  def document_similarity(document1, document2)
    calculate_tf_idf_vectors unless @document_vectors

    # Get indices of the documents
    doc1_index = @documents.index(document1)
    doc2_index = @documents.index(document2)

    raise "Documents not found in collection" unless doc1_index && doc2_index

    # Get the TF-IDF vectors
    vec1 = @document_vectors.row(doc1_index)
    vec2 = @document_vectors.row(doc2_index)

    # Calculate cosine similarity
    dot_product = vec1.dot(vec2)
    norm1 = vec1.norm
    norm2 = vec2.norm

    (dot_product / (norm1 * norm2)).round(4) if norm1 > 0 && norm2 > 0
  end

  def find_similar_documents(query_document, threshold = 0.3, limit = 5)
    calculate_tf_idf_vectors unless @document_vectors

    # Create query document vector
    query_terms = preprocess(query_document)
    query_vector = []

    @vocabulary.each do |term|
      tf = query_terms.count(term).to_f / query_terms.size
      idf = Math.log(@documents.size.to_f / @document_frequencies[term])
      tf_idf = tf * idf
      query_vector << tf_idf
    end

    query_vector = Matrix.rows([query_vector])

    # Calculate similarities
    similarities = []
    @documents.each_with_index do |doc, i|
      doc_vector = @document_vectors.row(i)
      dot_product = query_vector.row(0).dot(doc_vector)
      norm1 = query_vector.row(0).norm
      norm2 = doc_vector.norm

      similarity = (dot_product / (norm1 * norm2)).round(4) if norm1 > 0 && norm2 > 0
      similarities << { document: doc, similarity: similarity, index: i }
    end

    # Sort by similarity and filter by threshold
    similar_docs = similarities.sort_by { |s| -s[:similarity] }
                            .select { |s| s[:similarity] > threshold && s[:index] != @documents.index(query_document) }
                            .first(limit)

    similar_docs
  end

```ruby
require 'pgvector'
require 'httparty'
require 'dotenv/load'

class Document < ActiveRecord::Base
  # Add this after creating the migration
  include PgVector
  vector_column :embedding, type: :vector(1536) # 1536 is the dimension for OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002

  # Initialize OpenAI client
  def self.openai_client
    @openai_client ||= {
      api_key: ENV['OPENAI_API_KEY'],
      endpoint: 'https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings'
    }
  end

  # Generate embedding for text using OpenAI API
  def self.generate_embedding(text)
    response = HTTParty.post(
      openai_client[:endpoint],
      headers: {
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
        'Authorization' => "Bearer #{openai_client[:api_key]}"
      },
      body: {
        model: 'text-embedding-ada-002',
        input: text
      }.to_json
    )

    if response.success?
      embeddings = JSON.parse(response.body)['data'].first['embedding']
      embeddings.map(&:to_f) # Convert to float array
    else
      raise "OpenAI API error: #{response.body}"
    end
  end

  # Search for similar documents
  def self.search(query, top_k = 5)
    query_embedding = generate_embedding(query)

    similar_docs = Document
                    .order_by_vector_column(:embedding, query_embedding)
                    .limit(top_k)

    similar_docs.each do |doc|
      # Calculate cosine similarity score
      doc.cosine_similarity = PgVector.cosine_similarity(query_embedding, doc.embedding)
    end

    similar_docs
  end
end
```

# address_parser.rb
require 'usaddress'
require 'addressable/uri'

class AddressParser
  # Supported address components
  ADDRESS_COMPONENTS = [
    :address_number,
    :street_name,
    :street_name_post_type,
    :street_name_pre_direction,
    :street_name_pre_type,
    :street_name_post_direction,
    :street_name_post_quadrant,
    :street_name_suffix,
    :recipient,
    :building_name,
    :corner_of,
    :landmark,
    :entry,
    :unit,
    :floor,
    :apt,
    :room,
    :suite,
    :mail_stop,
    :po_box,
    :city,
    :state,
    :zip_code,
    :zip_code_plus4,
    :country
  ].freeze

  def initialize
    # Configuration for address parsing
    @config = {
      skip_unknown: true,  # Skip unknown components
      abbreviations: true  # Use abbreviations
    }
  end

  # Parse and normalize a single address string
  def parse_address(address_text)
    return nil if address_text.to_s.strip.empty?

    # First try to parse as a potential email address
    parsed_uri = Addressable::URI.parse(address_text)
    if parsed_uri.path.to_s.downcase.include?('@')
      return { email: address_text, normalized: nil }
    end

    # Otherwise, try to parse as a US address
    parsed_address = Usaddress.parse(address_text, **@config)
    return nil unless parsed_address

    # Group components into normalized address
    normalized_address = normalize_address(parsed_address)

    { email: nil, normalized: normalized_address }
  rescue StandardError => e
    puts "Error parsing address: #{e.message}"
    { email: nil, normalized: nil }
  end

  # Normalize the parsed address into standardized components
  def normalize_address(parsed_address)
    normalized = {}

    ADDRESS_COMPONENTS.each do |component|
      value = parsed_address.dig('address', component.to_s)
      normalized[component] = value if value.present?
    end

    # Handle special cases
    normalized[:zip_code] = "#{normalized[:zip_code]} #{normalized[:zip_code_plus4]}".strip
    normalized.delete(:zip_code_plus4)

    # Format full address
    normalized[:formatted] = format_address(normalized)

    normalized
  end

  # Format the normalized address into a standard US format
  def format_address(components)
    return nil unless components[:address_number] || components[:po_box]

    parts = []

    # Recipient (if present)
    parts << components[:recipient] if components[:recipient]

    # Address line 1
    line1_parts = []
    line1_parts << components[:address_number] if components[:address_number]
    line1_parts << components[:street_name] if components[:street_name]
    line1_parts << components[:street_suffix] if components[:street_suffix]
    parts << line1_parts.join(' ').strip

    # Address line 2 (units, etc.)
    line2_parts = []
    ADDRESS_COMPONENTS.each do |comp|
      next unless %i[apt floor room suite unit].include?(comp) && components[comp]

      line2_parts << components[comp]
    end
    line2_parts << components[:building_name] if components[:building_name] && line2_parts.any?
    parts << line2_parts.join(' ').strip if line2_parts.any?

    # City, State, ZIP
    location_parts = []
    location_parts << components[:city] if components[:city]
    location_parts << components[:state] if components[:state]
    location_parts << components[:zip_code] if components[:zip_code]
    parts << location_parts.join(', ').strip if location_parts.any?

    parts.compact.join("\n")
  end

## Implementation

Here's a complete implementation for extracting named entities from English news articles:

```ruby
# ner_extractor.rb

require 'stanford-core-nlp'
require 'down'
require 'nokogiri'
require 'open-uri'
require 'oj'
require 'thor'

class NamedEntityExtractor
  MODEL_URL = 'https://nlp.stanford.edu/software/stanford-corenlp-full-2018-10-05.zip'
  MODEL_DIR = File.expand_path('~/.stanford_corenlp')

  def initialize
    setup_nlp
  end

  def extract_entities_from_url(url)
    html = URI.open(url).read
    doc = Nokogiri::HTML(html)
    articles = doc.css('article, .article, .content')

    articles.each_with_object({}) do |article, result|
      text = article.text
      entities = extract_entities(text)
      result[article.attr('id') || article.attr('class')] = entities
    end
  end

  def extract_entities_from_text(text)
    extract_entities(text)
  end

  private

  def setup_nlp
    unless Dir.exist?(MODEL_DIR)
      Down.download(MODEL_URL) do |file|
        FileUtils.mkdir_p(MODEL_DIR)
        Zip::File.open(file.path) do |zip|
          zip.each do |entry|
            next if entry.directory?

            path = File.join(MODEL_DIR, entry.name)
            FileUtils.mkdir_p(File.dirname(path))
            zip.extract(entry, path)
          end
        end
      end
    end

    StanfordCoreNLP.java_properties['annotators'] = 'tokenize,ssplit,pos,lemma,ner'
    StanfordCoreNLP.java_properties['ner.applyFineGrained'] = 'true'
  end

  def extract_entities(text)
    document = StanfordCoreNLP::Document.new(text)
    document.annotate

    entities = {}

    document.sentences.each do |sentence|
      sentence.ner_tags.each_with_index do |tag, index|
        next unless tag && tag != 'O'

        word = sentence.words[index]
        next unless word

        entities[word] ||= []
        entities[word] << tag
      end
    end

    # Group by entity type
    grouped = {}
    entities.each do |word, tags|
      tags.uniq.each do |tag|
        grouped[tag] ||= []
        grouped[tag] << word
      end
    end

    # Convert to more readable format
    {
      people: grouped['PERSON'],
      organizations: grouped['ORGANIZATION'],
      locations: grouped['LOCATION'],
      misc: grouped.except('PERSON', 'ORGANIZATION', 'LOCATION')
    }.compact
  end
end

class NERCLI < Thor
  desc "extract [URL]", "Extract named entities from a news article URL"
  def extract(url)
    extractor = NamedEntityExtractor.new
    results = extractor.extract_entities_from_url(url)
    puts Oj.dump(results, mode: :compat)
  end

  desc "text [TEXT]", "Extract named entities from text"
  def text(text)
    extractor = NamedEntityExtractor.new
    results = extractor.extract_entities_from_text(text)
    puts Oj.dump(results, mode: :compat)
  end
end

if __FILE__ == $0
  NERCLI.start
end
```

## Usage Examples

1. **Command Line Usage**:
   ```

   ruby ner_extractor.rb text "The President visited the White House yesterday."
   ```

2. **Programmatic Usage**:
   ```ruby

   # From URL

# flesch_score_calculator.rb

require 'flesch_score'

class FleschScoreCalculator
  def initialize(text)
    @text = text
  end

  # Calculate Flesch Reading Ease score (higher is easier to read)
  # Scores range from:
  # 90-100: 5th grade level
  # 80-89: 6th grade level
  # 70-79: 7th grade level
  # 60-69: 8th-9th grade level
  # 50-59: 10th-12th grade level
  # 30-49: College level
  # 0-29: College graduate level
  def calculate
    FleschScore::FleschReadingEase.new(@text).score
  end

  # Calculate approximate grade level (US school system)
  def grade_level
    score = calculate
    if score >= 90
      5
    elsif score >= 80
      6
    elsif score >= 70
      7
    elsif score >= 60
      8
    elsif score >= 50
      10
    elsif score >= 30
      12
    else
      16 # College graduate
    end
  end

  # Calculate Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (alternative metric)
  def flesch_kincaid_grade_level
    FleschScore::FleschKincaidGradeLevel.new(@text).score
  end
end

# pure_ruby_flesch_score.rb

class PureFleschScoreCalculator
  def initialize(text)
    @text = text
  end

  def calculate
    # Count sentences, syllables, and words
    sentences = count_sentences
    words = count_words
    syllables = count_syllables

    # Avoid division by zero
    return 0 if words == 0 || sentences == 0

    # Flesch Reading Ease formula:
    # 206.835 - 1.015 * (words / sentences) - 84.6 * (syllables / words)
    206.835 - (1.015 * (words.to_f / sentences)) - (84.6 * (syllables.to_f / words))
  end

  private

  def count_sentences
    # Very basic sentence splitting (for demonstration)
    @text.split(/[.!?]+/).count { |s| s.strip != '' }
  end

  def count_words
    @text.split.count
  end

  def count_syllables
    # Simplified syllable counting (not perfect but works for demonstration)
    @text.downcase.scan(/[aeiouy]+/).sum { |vowel_group| vowel_group.length / 2 + 1 }
  end
end
```

# Ruby Implementation for TF-IDF and Document Similarity

Here's a complete solution for computing TF-IDF keywords and finding similar documents:

## Gemfile

```

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'tfidf'
require 'nokogiri'
require 'sane'  # Optional for stemming

class DocumentSimilarity
  def initialize(documents)
    @documents = documents
    @tfidf = TFIDF::TFIDF.new
    @vectorizer = nil
    @idf = nil
  end

  # Preprocess text: remove HTML tags, lowercase, and optionally stem
  def preprocess(text)
    # Remove HTML tags
    doc = Nokogiri::HTML(text)
    clean_text = doc.text

    # Lowercase
    clean_text = clean_text.downcase

    # Optional: Stemming (uncomment if needed)
    # stemmer = Sane::Stemmer.new
    # clean_text.split.each { |word| stemmer.stem(word) }.join(' ')

    clean_text
  end

  # Compute TF-IDF for all documents
  def compute_tfidf
    # Preprocess all documents
    processed_docs = @documents.map { |doc| preprocess(doc) }

    # Vectorize documents (create term frequency matrix)
    @vectorizer = TFIDF::Vectorizer.new(processed_docs)

    # Compute inverse document frequency
    @idf = TFIDF::IDF.new(@vectorizer.matrix)

    # Get the TF-IDF matrix
    @tfidf_matrix = @idf.tf_idf(@vectorizer.matrix)
  end

  # Get top N keywords for a document
  def get_keywords(doc_index, n=10)
    unless @tfidf_matrix
      compute_tfidf
    end

    # Get the document's TF-IDF vector
    doc_vector = @tfidf_matrix[doc_index]

    # Get terms and their scores
    terms = @vectorizer.terms
    scores = doc_vector.map { |score| score * (score > 0 ? 1 : 0) }

    # Sort by score (descending)
    sorted = terms.each_with_index.sort_by { |term, idx| -scores[idx] }

    # Return top N terms
    sorted.take(n).map { |term, _| term }
  end

  # Find similar documents (cosine similarity)
  def find_similar(doc_index, top_n=3)
    unless @tfidf_matrix
      compute_tfidf
    end

    # Get the query document's vector
    query_vector = @tfidf_matrix[doc_index]

    # Calculate cosine similarity with all other documents
    similarities = []
    @tfidf_matrix.each_with_index do |vector, idx|
      next if idx == doc_index  # Skip the document itself
      similarity = cosine_similarity(query_vector, vector)
      similarities << { index: idx, score: similarity }
    end

    # Sort by similarity score (descending)
    sorted = similarities.sort_by { |item| -item[:score] }

    # Return top N similar documents
    sorted.take(top_n)
  end

  private

  # Calculate cosine similarity between two vectors
  def cosine_similarity(vec1, vec2)
    dot_product = vec1.each_with_index.sum { |v, i| v * vec2[i] }
    mag1 = Math.sqrt(vec1.sum { |v| v**2 })
    mag2 = Math.sqrt(vec2.sum { |v| v**2 })

    mag1 * mag2 > 0 ? (dot_product / (mag1 * mag2)) : 0
  end
end
```

# Ruby Implementation for Parsing Natural Language Dates

Here's a complete solution for parsing natural language dates in Ruby, including a Gemfile and the implementation.

## Gemfile

```

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'chronic'
require 'chronic_duration'

class NaturalLanguageDateParser
  def initialize
    # Configure Chronic for better natural language parsing
    Chronic.class_eval do
      def self.parse_with_nat_lang(input, *args)
        result = parse(input, *args)
        if result.nil? && input.present?
          # Try with some common variations
          input.downcase!
          input.gsub!(/at\s+/, ' ') # Remove "at" from time phrases
          input.gsub!(/next\s+/, '') # Remove "next" from phrases
          parse(input, *args)
        else
          result
        end
      end
      alias_method :parse, :parse_with_nat_lang
    end
  end

  # Main method to parse natural language dates
  def parse_date(input)
    if input.nil? || input.strip.empty?
      return nil
    end

    Chronic.parse(input)
  end

  # Helper method to add days to a date
  def add_days(date, days)
    date + (days * 86400) # 86400 seconds in a day
  end

  # Extended parsing method that handles some common cases better
  def extended_parse(input)
    if input.nil? || input.strip.empty?
      return nil
    end

    # Special handling for "today" and "tomorrow"
    case input.downcase
    when /^(today|tonight)$/
      return Time.now.beginning_of_day
    when /^tomorrow/
      return Time.now.tomorrow.beginning_of_day
    when /^yesterday$/
      return Time.now.yesterday.beginning_of_day
    end

    # Try standard parsing
    result = parse_date(input)

    # If we didn't get a result, try some transformations
    if result.nil?
      # Try without "at"
      input_without_at = input.gsub(/at\s+/, '')
      result = parse_date(input_without_at)

      # Try with different time formats
      if result.nil? && input_without_at.downcase.include?('pm')
        # Replace "pm" with "p.m." for some cases
        input_with_pm = input_without_at.gsub(/pm/i, 'p.m.')
        result = parse_date(input_with_pm)
      end

      if result.nil? && input_without_at.downcase.include?('am')
        # Replace "am" with "a.m." for some cases
        input_with_am = input_without_at.gsub(/am/i, 'a.m.')
        result = parse_date(input_with_am)
      end
    end

    result
  end
end

# Example usage

  test_cases = [
    "next Friday at 5pm",
    "today at 3:30 pm",
    "tomorrow morning",

    "in 2 weeks",

    "5pm next friday",
    "this wednesday 8:30am"
  ]

  test_cases.each do |phrase|

    parsed_date = parser.extended_parse(phrase)

  end
end
```

Here's a complete solution for transliterating Ukrainian names into Latin script according to the official 2010 rules (Cabinet resolution No. 55).

## Gemfile

## Implementation

Now, here's the implementation code:

```ruby
# lib/ukrainian_transliteration.rb
class UkrainianTransliteration
  # Official Ukrainian to Latin transliteration rules (2010)
  TRANSLITERATION_RULES = {
    # Vowels
    'а' => 'a', 'А' => 'A',
    'е' => 'e', 'Е' => 'E',
    'и' => 'y', 'И' => 'Y',
    'і' => 'i', 'І' => 'I',
    'ї' => 'yi', 'Ї' => 'Yi',
    'о' => 'o', 'О' => 'O',
    'у' => 'u', 'У' => 'U',
    'ю' => 'yu', 'Ю' => 'Yu',
    'я' => 'ya', 'Я' => 'Ya',

    # Consonants
    # Simple consonants
    'б' => 'b', 'Б' => 'B',
    'в' => 'v', 'В' => 'V',
    'г' => 'h', 'Г' => 'H',
    'д' => 'd', 'Д' => 'D',
    'з' => 'z', 'З' => 'Z',
    'к' => 'k', 'К' => 'K',
    'л' => 'l', 'Л' => 'L',
    'м' => 'm', 'М' => 'M',
    'н' => 'n', 'Н' => 'N',
    'п' => 'p', 'П' => 'P',
    'р' => 'r', 'Р' => 'R',
    'с' => 's', 'С' => 'S',
    'т' => 't', 'Т' => 'T',
    'ф' => 'f', 'Ф' => 'F',
    'х' => 'kh', 'Х' => 'Kh',
    'ц' => 'ts', 'Ц' => 'Ts',
    'ч' => 'ch', 'Ч' => 'Ch',
    'ш' => 'sh', 'Ш' => 'Sh',
    'щ' => 'shch', 'Щ' => 'Shch',

    # Special consonants
    'ж' => 'zh', 'Ж' => 'Zh',
    'й' => 'i', 'Й' => 'I',

    # Soft sign (not transliterated in most cases)
    'ь' => '', 'Ь' => ''
  }.freeze

  # Characters that should never be capitalized (according to rules)
  UPPERCASE_EXCEPTIONS = %w[Y Yu Yi Ya].freeze

  # Handles special cases and capitalization
  def self.transliterate(input)
    return input unless input.is_a?(String)

    # Convert to array of characters for processing
    chars = input.chars

    # Process each character
    processed_chars = chars.map.with_index do |char, index|
      next char unless TRANSLITERATION_RULES.key?(char)

      translit = TRANSLITERATION_RULES[char]

      # Handle capitalization
      if char == char.upcase
        # For multi-character transliterations, only capitalize the first letter
        if translit.length > 1
          # Don't capitalize if it's in the exceptions list
          first_char = translit[0].upcase
          rest = translit[1..-1].downcase
          full_translit = first_char + rest

          # Check if we should capitalize (not in exceptions and not at start of string)
          if UPPERCASE_EXCEPTIONS.include?(full_translit) ||
             (index == 0 && processed_chars.empty?)
            full_translit
          else
            first_char.downcase + rest
          end
        else
          translit.upcase
        end
      else
        translit
      end
    end

    # Join the processed characters and clean up
    result = processed_chars.join

    # Remove any remaining soft signs
    result.gsub('ь', '').gsub('Ь', '')

    # Capitalize the first letter if the original had a capital letter
    if input == input.capitalize && !result.empty?
      result.capitalize
    else
      result
    end
  end
end
```

def flesch_reading_ease(text)
  words = text.split
  sentences = text.split(/[.!?]/).reject(&:empty?)
  syllables = count_syllables(words)

  # Виключення на випадок, якщо текст містить менше 30 слів
  if words.length < 30
    return nil
  end

  # Обчислення показника
  asl = words.length.to_f / sentences.length
  asw = syllables.to_f / words.length
  flesch_score = 206.835 - 1.015 * asl - 84.6 * asw

  flesch_score
end

Here's a complete implementation for a Ukrainian spelling checker that suggests corrections. The solution uses the `hunspell` library (via the `hunspell_stemmer` gem) which provides spell checking capabilities for Ukrainian.

## Gemfile

```ruby
# Gemfile
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'hunspell_stemmer', '~> 2.1'
gem 'i18n', '~> 1.12'  # For text handling
```

## Implementation

```ruby
# ukrainian_spell_checker.rb

require 'hunspell_stemmer'
require 'i18n'

# Load Ukrainian dictionary (you'll need to download these files)
# Typically you'd put these in your project's lib directory
# or configure the paths appropriately
DICTIONARY_PATH = File.expand_path('lib/uk_UA.dic', __dir__)
AFFIX_PATH = File.expand_path('lib/uk_UA.aff', __dir__)

class UkrainianSpellChecker
  def initialize
    @dictionary = HunspellStemmer.new(DICTIONARY_PATH, AFFIX_PATH)
  end

  # Main method to check spelling and suggest corrections
  def check_spelling(text)
    # Split text into words (simple whitespace-based splitting)
    words = text.split(/\s+/)

    results = []
    words.each do |word|
      if @dictionary.spell(word)
        results << { original: word, correct: true, suggestions: [] }
      else
        suggestions = @dictionary.suggest(word).map(&:to_s)
        results << { original: word, correct: false, suggestions: suggestions }
      end
    end

    results
  end

  # Alternative method that returns the text with corrections
  def correct_text(text, suggestion_strategy: :first)
    words = text.split(/\s+/)
    corrected_words = words.map do |word|
      if @dictionary.spell(word)
        word
      else
        case suggestion_strategy
        when :first
          @dictionary.suggest(word).first.to_s || word
        when :best
          # You could implement a more sophisticated selection here
          @dictionary.suggest(word).first.to_s || word
        else
          word
        end
      end
    end

    corrected_words.join(' ')
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0
  # Create checker instance
  checker = UkrainianSpellChecker.new

  # Example text with intentional spelling errors
  uk_text = "Це приклад тексту з помилками. Яка є ваша ім'я? У мене є інтересний ідеї."

  puts "Original text:"
  puts uk_text
  puts "\n"

  puts "Detailed spelling check:"
  results = checker.check_spelling(uk_text)
  results.each do |result|
    if result[:correct]
      puts "[OK] #{result[:original]}"
    else
      puts "[ERROR] #{result[:original]}"
      puts "Suggestions: #{result[:suggestions].join(', ')}"
    end
  end

  puts "\nAutomatically corrected text (using first suggestion):"
  puts checker.correct_text(uk_text, suggestion_strategy: :first)
end
```

## Setup Instructions

1. Install the required gems:
   ```bash
   bundle install
   ```

2. Download Ukrainian Hunspell dictionaries:
   - You can find them in various places, but a common source is the OpenOffice Ukrainian dictionary package.
   - The files you need are:
     - `uk_UA.dic` (dictionary file)
     - `uk_UA.aff` (affix file)
   - Place these files in a `lib` directory in your project root.

3. Run the example:
   ```bash
   ruby ukrainian_spell_checker.rb
   ```

## Notes

1. The implementation uses the `hunspell_stemmer` gem which is a Ruby wrapper for Hunspell, a widely used spell checker.

2. For production use, you might want to:
   - Add more sophisticated word splitting (handling punctuation, etc.)
   - Implement a better suggestion selection strategy
   - Add caching for the dictionary to improve performance
   - Handle case sensitivity appropriately

3. The quality of suggestions depends on the dictionary files you use. Make sure to get comprehensive Ukrainian dictionary files for best results.

4. If you need to handle large texts efficiently, consider processing the text in chunks rather than all at once.

# Ruby Implementation to Check Ukrainian Public Holidays

Here's a complete solution with a Gemfile and implementation to determine if a given date is a public holiday in Ukraine.

## Gemfile

```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

# For date manipulation and holiday calculations
gem 'holidays', '~> 2.1', require: 'holidays/ukraine'
```

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'holidays/ukraine'

class UkrainianHolidayChecker
  def initialize(year)
    @year = year
    Holidays.define_holidays do |c|
      c.holiday :ukraine
    end
  end

  # Check if a specific date is a holiday
  def holiday?(date)
    Holidays.on(date, :ukraine).any?
  end

  # Get all holidays for the year
  def holidays
    Holidays.between(Date.new(@year, 1, 1), Date.new(@year, 12, 31), :ukraine)
  end

  # Get next 10 holidays after today
  def next_holidays(count = 10)
    today = Date.today
    Holidays.on(Date.new(@year, 1, 1)..Date.new(@year, 12, 31), :ukraine)
           .select { |d,_| d >= today }
           .sort_by(&:first)
           .first(count)
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0
  checker = UkrainianHolidayChecker.new(Date.today.year)

  puts "Ukrainian Holidays in #{Date.today.year}"

  # Check specific dates
  test_dates = [
    Date.new(Date.today.year, 1, 1),    # New Year's Day
    Date.new(Date.today.year, 1, 7),    # Christmas (Julian calendar)
    Date.new(Date.today.year, 12, 25),  # Christmas (Gregorian calendar)
    Date.new(Date.today.year, 5, 1),    # Labor Day
    Date.new(Date.today.year, 8, 24)    # Independence Day
  ]

  test_dates.each do |date|
    if checker.holiday?(date)
      puts "#{date.strftime('%B %d')} is a Ukrainian public holiday: #{Holidays.on(date, :ukraine).first.last}"
    else
      puts "#{date.strftime('%B %d')} is not a Ukrainian public holiday"
    end
  end

  # Display next holidays
  puts "\nNext #{checker.next_holidays.size} Ukrainian holidays:"
  checker.next_holidays.each do |date, name|
    puts "#{date.strftime('%B %d')} - #{name}"
  end
end
```

## How It Works

1. **Gemfile**: Includes the `holidays` gem which has built-in support for Ukrainian holidays (via the `holidays/ukraine` require path).

2. **UkrainianHolidayChecker Class**:
   - Initializes with a specific year
   - Provides methods to:
     - Check if a specific date is a holiday (`holiday?`)
     - Get all holidays for the year (`holidays`)
     - Get the next upcoming holidays (`next_holidays`)

3. **Example Usage**:
   - Creates an instance of the checker
   - Tests several known Ukrainian holidays
   - Shows the next upcoming holidays

The `holidays` gem includes the following Ukrainian public holidays:
- New Year's Day (January 1)
- Orthodox Christmas (January 7)
- International Women's Day (March 8)
- Easter (date varies)
- Orthodox Easter (date varies)
- Labor Day (May 1)
- Victory Day (May 8)
- Constitution Day (June 28)
- Independence Day (August 24)

Note: The `holidays` gem may not include all possible regional holidays or recently added national holidays. For a more comprehensive solution, you might need to extend the gem or use an official government data source.

To use this code, first run `bundle install` to install the required gem, then run the Ruby file directly.

require 'unicode_utils'

class UkTransliterator
  # Основні правила транслітерації (згідно з постановою КМУ № 55, 2010)
  TRANSLITERATION_RULES = {
    'а' => 'a', 'А' => 'A',
    'б' => 'b', 'Б' => 'B',
    'в' => 'v', 'В' => 'V',
    'г' => 'h', 'Г' => 'H',
    'ґ' => 'g', 'Ґ' => 'G',
    'д' => 'd', 'Д' => 'D',
    'е' => 'e', 'Е' => 'E',
    'є' => 'ie', 'Є' => 'Ie',
    'ж' => 'zh', 'Ж' => 'Zh',
    'з' => 'z', 'З' => 'Z',
    'и' => 'y', 'И' => 'Y',
    'і' => 'i', 'І' => 'I',
    'ї' => 'yi', 'Ї' => 'Yi',
    'й' => 'i', 'Й' => 'I',
    'к' => 'k', 'К' => 'K',
    'л' => 'l', 'Л' => 'L',
    'м' => 'm', 'М' => 'M',
    'н' => 'n', 'Н' => 'N',
    'о' => 'o', 'О' => 'O',
    'п' => 'p', 'П' => 'P',
    'р' => 'r', 'Р' => 'R',
    'с' => 's', 'С' => 'S',
    'т' => 't', 'Т' => 'T',
    'у' => 'u', 'У' => 'U',
    'ф' => 'f', 'Ф' => 'F',
    'х' => 'kh', 'Х' => 'Kh',
    'ц' => 'ts', 'Ц' => 'Ts',
    'ч' => 'ch', 'Ч' => 'Ch',
    'ш' => 'sh', 'Ш' => 'Sh',
    'щ' => 'shch', 'Щ' => 'Shch',
    'ь' => '', 'Ь' => '',
    'ю' => 'iu', 'Ю' => 'Iu',
    'я' => 'ia', 'Я' => 'Ia'
  }.freeze

  # Літери, які не потребують транслітерації (латинські)
  LATIN_LETTERS = [*'a'..'z', *'A'..'Z'].freeze

  def self.transliterate(text)
    text.chars.map { |char| transliterate_char(char) }.join
  end

  def self.transliterate_char(char)
    return char if LATIN_LETTERS.include?(char)

    # Перевірка на українську літеру
    TRANSLITERATION_RULES.key?(char) ? TRANSLITERATION_RULES[char] : char
  end
end

# Приклад використання

  transliterated = UkTransliterator.transliterate(name)
  puts "Оригінал: #{name}"

end

2. **UkTransliterator** - клас, який реалізує правила транслітерації:
   - `TRANSLITERATION_RULES` - хеш з відповідностями українських літер латинським відповідностям.
   - `LATIN_LETTERS` - масив латинських літер, які не потребують транслітерації.

# support_summary.rb
require 'httparty'
require 'json'
require 'logger'

class SupportSummary
  include HTTParty

  # Налаштування API Claude
  BASE_URL = 'https://api.anthropic.com/v1/complete'
  API_KEY = ENV['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'] # Зберігайте ключ у змінних середовища

  def initialize
    @logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
    @logger.level = Logger::INFO
  end

  # Метод для підсумовування довгих звернень
  def summarize_support_requests(texts, max_tokens = 100)
    # Об'єднуємо всі тексти в один
    combined_text = texts.join("\n\n")

    # Формуємо запит до Claude
    prompt = <<~PROMPT
      You are a helpful assistant that summarizes customer support requests.
      Please provide a concise summary (up to #{max_tokens} tokens) of the following support requests:

      #{combined_text}

      Summary:
    PROMPT

    begin
      response = make_api_request(prompt, max_tokens)
      JSON.parse(response.body)['completion']
    rescue StandardError => e
      @logger.error("Error summarizing requests: #{e.message}")
      nil
    end
  end

  private

  def make_api_request(prompt, max_tokens)
    headers = {
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
      'anthropic-version' => '2023-06-01',
      'x-api-key' => API_KEY
    }

    body = {
      prompt: prompt,
      max_tokens_to_sample: max_tokens,
      model: 'claude-2' # або інша доступна модель
    }

    self.class.post(
      BASE_URL,
      headers: headers,
      body: body.to_json
    )
  end
end

# Приклад використання
if __FILE__ == $0
  support = SupportSummary.new

  # Приклад довгих звернень
  support_requests = [
    "Hello, I've been trying to reset my password but the link doesn't work. I've tried multiple times and it keeps showing the same error. Could you please help me?",
    "I placed an order yesterday but I haven't received any confirmation email. The tracking says it was shipped but I'm worried it might be lost. What should I do?",
    "Your website is not loading properly on my mobile device. The images are distorted and some buttons don't respond. This happens on both Wi-Fi and mobile data."
  ]

  summary = support.summarize_support_requests(support_requests, 100)
  puts "Summary: #{summary}" if summary
end

# Ruby Implementation for Ukrainian Stemming/Lemmatization

Here's a complete solution for stemming/lemmatizing Ukrainian words before full-text search, including the necessary Gemfile dependencies.

## Gemfile

```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

# Core search functionality
gem 'sunspot', '~> 3.0'
gem 'sunspot_rails'  # If using Rails

# Ukrainian language processing
gem 'stringex'
gem 'stemmer', '~> 1.3'  # For basic stemming
gem 'hunspell', '~> 0.5'  # For lemmatization with Ukrainian dictionaries
gem 'hunspell_dictionary_uk'  # Ukrainian dictionary for Hunspell
```

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'hunspell'
require 'sunspot'

# Initialize Ukrainian lemmatizer
# Note: You'll need to install the Ukrainian dictionary files
# Typically found at /usr/share/hunspell or similar
class UkrainianLemmatizer
  def initialize
    # Try to find the dictionary files
    dict_path = detect_hunspell_dictionaries
    @hunspell = Hunspell.new(dict_path[:affix], dict_path[:dictionary])
  rescue => e
    raise "Failed to initialize Ukrainian lemmatizer: #{e.message}"
  end

  def lemmatize(word)
    # First try to get the base form
    lemmas = @hunspell.stem(word)
    return word if lemmas.empty?  # Fallback to original word

    # Get the most likely lemma (Hunspell returns an array)
    lemmas.first
  rescue => e
    Rails.logger.warn "Failed to lemmatize '#{word}': #{e.message}"
    word  # Fallback to original word
  end

  private

  def detect_hunspell_dictionaries
    # Common locations where Hunspell dictionaries are installed
    possible_paths = [
      { affix: '/usr/share/hunspell/uk_UA.aff', dictionary: '/usr/share/hunspell/uk_UA.dic' },
      { affix: '/usr/share/hunspell/uk.aff', dictionary: '/usr/share/hunspell/uk.dic' },
      { affix: '/usr/local/share/hunspell/uk_UA.aff', dictionary: '/usr/local/share/hunspell/uk_UA.dic' },
      { affix: '/usr/local/share/hunspell/uk.aff', dictionary: '/usr/local/share/hunspell/uk.dic' }
    ]

    possible_paths.each do |path|
      if File.exist?(path[:affix]) && File.exist?(path[:dictionary])
        return path
      end
    end

    raise "Could not find Ukrainian Hunspell dictionaries in common locations"
  end
end

# Full-text search class that uses lemmatization
class UkrainianSearch
  def initialize
    @lemmatizer = UkrainianLemmatizer.new
  end

  # Tokenize and lemmatize a text for search
  def prepare_for_search(text)
    tokens = text.downcase.split(/\s+/)
    tokens.map { |token| @lemmatizer.lemmatize(token) }
  end

  # Example: Search a model with Ukrainian text
  def search_model(model_class, query, options = {})
    prepared_query = prepare_for_search(query)

    search = Sunspot.search(model_class) do
      fulltext prepared_query.join(' '), fields: [:title, :content, :description]
      # Add any additional filters or options from the options hash
      options.each { |key, value| send(key, value) } if options.present?
    end

    search.results
  end
end
```

## Usage Example

```ruby
# Initialize the search
searcher = UkrainianSearch.new

# Search with Ukrainian text
results = searcher.search_model(Article, "головні новини")

# Or with more options
results = searcher.search_model(Article, "українська мова",
  published: true,
  limit: 10,
  order_by: :published_at
)
```

## Notes

1. **Dictionary Installation**: For this to work, you need to have the Ukrainian Hunspell dictionaries installed on your system. On Ubuntu/Debian you can install them with:
   ```bash
   sudo apt-get install hunspell hunspell-uk
   ```

2. **Alternative Approach**: If you prefer not to use Hunspell, you could use the `stemmer` gem for basic stemming (though lemmatization would be less accurate):
   ```ruby
   require 'stemmer'
   Stemmer.create('uk').stem('головні')  # Returns "головн"
   ```

3. **Performance**: For high-performance applications, consider caching lemmatized forms.

4. **Rails Integration**: If you're using Rails, you can integrate this with Sunspot/Solr by using the `prepare_for_search` method in your model's `searchable` block.

First, create the Ukrainian locale file Create `config/locales/uk.yml`: ```yaml uk: plural: keys: - one - few - many - other rules: - rule: "n == 1" value: "one" - rule: "n % 10 in (2..4) and n % 100 not in (12..14)" value: "few" - rule: "n % 10 in (0, 5..9) or n % 100 in (12..14)" value: "many" - rule: "true" value: "other" ``` ### 2. ```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'i18n'

# Налаштування локалізації для української мови
I18n.load_path << File.expand_path('config/locales/uk.yml', __dir__)
I18n.config.available_locales = [:uk]
I18n.locale = :uk

# Гем для перетворення чисел на українські слова
module NumToUkWords
  class Converter
    def initialize(currency: 'гривня', currency_plural: 'гривні')
      @currency = currency
      @currency_plural = currency_plural
    end

    def convert(number)
      raise ArgumentError, "Number must be an integer" unless number.is_a?(Integer)
      raise ArgumentError, "Number must be positive" if number < 0

      return I18n.t('num.words.zero') if number == 0

      parts = []
      parts << convert_below_thousand(number % 1000)
      parts << convert_thousands(number / 1000) if number >= 1000

      parts.join(' ').strip
    end

    def convert_with_currency(number, gender: :feminine)
      words = convert(number)
      currency = number % 10 == 1 ? @currency : @currency_plural
      "#{words} #{currency}"
    end

    private

    def convert_below_thousand(number)
      return '' if number == 0

      parts = []

      hundreds = number / 100
      tens_units = number % 100

      if hundreds > 0
        parts << I18n.t('num.words.hundreds', count: hundreds)
      end

      if tens_units > 0
        parts << convert_tens_units(tens_units)
      end

      parts.join(' ')
    end

    def convert_thousands(number)
      thousands = number % 1000
      millions = number / 1000

      parts = []

      if thousands > 0
        parts << convert_below_thousand(thousands) + ' ' + I18n.t('num.words.thousand')
      end

      if millions > 0
        parts << convert(millions) + ' ' + I18n.t('num.words.million')
      end

      parts.join(' ')
    end

    def convert_tens_units(number)
      if number < 10
        I18n.t("num.words.units.#{number}")
      elsif number < 20
        I18n.t("num.words.teens.#{number - 10}")
      elsif number < 100
        tens = number / 10
        units = number % 10
        if units == 0
          I18n.t("num.words.tens.#{tens}")
        else
          I18n.t("num.words.tens.#{tens}") + ' ' + I18n.t("num.words.units.#{units}")
        end
      else
        I18n.t("num.words.tens.#{number / 10}") + ' ' + I18n.t("num.words.units.#{number % 10}")
      end
    end
  end
end

  end

  def stem_text(text)
    words = text.downcase.split
    stemmed_words = words.map { |word| Stemmer.stem(word, :uk) }
    stemmed_words.join(' ')
  end

  # Perform lemmatization on Ukrainian text
  # Note: This is a placeholder - you'll need a proper Ukrainian lemmatizer
  def lemmatize_text(text)
    # This is a simplified approach - for production you'd need a proper Ukrainian lemmatizer
    # or API to a NLP service that supports Ukrainian
    words = text.downcase.split
    lemmatized_words = words.map do |word|
      # Basic lemmatization rules for Ukrainian (this is very simplified)
      case word
      when /\w+і$/ then word.chomp('і') + 'а'
      when /\w+у$/ then word.chomp('у') + 'а'
      when /\w+а$/ then word
      when /\w+е$/ then word.chomp('е') + 'о'
      else word
      end
    end
    lemmatized_words.join(' ')
  end

# Ruby Implementation for Normalizing Ukrainian Mobile Phone Numbers

Here's a complete solution with a Gemfile and implementation to normalize Ukrainian mobile phone numbers to the +380 format and detect the operator.

## Gemfile

```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'phonelib'  # For phone number parsing and normalization
gem 'i18n'      # For internationalization support
```

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'phonelib'
require 'i18n'

# Load Ukrainian translations for I18n
I18n.load_path = Dir[File.expand_path('config/locales/*.yml', __dir__)]
I18n.default_locale = :uk

class UkrainianPhoneNormalizer
  OPERATOR_CODES = {
    '39' => 'Kyivstar',
    '50' => 'Vodafone',
    '63' => 'Lifecell',
    '66' => 'Kyivstar',
    '67' => 'Vodafone',
    '68' => 'Kyivstar',
    '91' => 'Kyivstar',
    '92' => 'Vodafone',
    '93' => 'Kyivstar',
    '95' => 'Kyivstar',
    '96' => 'Kyivstar',
    '97' => 'Kyivstar',
    '98' => 'Kyivstar',
    '99' => 'Kyivstar'
  }.freeze

  def initialize(phone_number)
    @phone_number = phone_number
    @phone = PhoneLib.parse(phone_number, 'UA')
  end

  def normalized_number
    return nil unless valid?

    @phone.full_e164
  end

  def operator
    return nil unless valid?

    normalized_number[4..5]
  end

  def operator_name
    return nil unless valid?

    OPERATOR_CODES[operator] || 'Unknown'
  end

  def valid?
    @phone&.valid? && @phone.country_code == '380' && @phone.valid_for_country?
  end

  def formatted_number
    return nil unless valid?

    I18n.t('phone_formats.e164', number: normalized_number)
  end
end
```

## Locales Configuration (config/locales/uk.yml)

```yaml

  phone_formats:
    e164: "Нормалізований номер: %{number}"
```

## Example Usage

  puts "Нормалізований номер: #{normalizer.normalized_number}"
  puts "Оператор: #{normalizer.operator_name}"
  puts "Форматований вивід: #{normalizer.formatted_number}"
else
  puts "Невірний номер телефону"
end

# More examples

  '063 123 4567',
  '+38 099 123 4567',
  '380501234567',

  normalizer = UkrainianPhoneNormalizer.new(number)

    puts "Оператор: #{normalizer.operator_name}"
  else

  end

## How It Works

1. **Gemfile**: Includes the necessary gems:
   - `phonelib` for phone number parsing and normalization
   - `i18n` for localization support

2. **UkrainianPhoneNormalizer Class**:
   - Parses phone numbers using PhoneLib
   - Normalizes them to E.164 format (+380XXYYYYYYYY)
   - Detects the operator based on the network code (first 2 digits after country code)
   - Provides formatted output in Ukrainian

3. **Operator Detection**:
   - Uses a predefined hash of network codes to operator names
   - Includes major Ukrainian mobile operators: Kyivstar, Vodafone, and Lifecell

4. **Validation**:
   - Checks if the number is valid for Ukraine
   - Ensures the country code is +380

5. **Localization**:
   - Provides Ukrainian output messages
   - Can be easily extended with other languages

The solution handles various input formats (with/without country code, different separators) and normalizes them to the standard +380 format.

Now, here's the implementation for declining Ukrainian names into the dative case:

```ruby
# lib/ukrainian_case_converter.rb
require 'i18n'
require 'unidecoder'

class UkrainianNameCaseConverter
  # Initialize with optional custom dictionary
  def initialize(custom_rules = {})
    @custom_rules = custom_rules
    load_default_rules
  end

  # Convert a name to dative case
  def to_dative(name, gender: :male)
    return name if @custom_rules.key?(name.downcase)

    base = normalize_name(name)
    gender_suffix = gender == :female ? :female_suffix : :male_suffix

    # Handle patronymics (usually end with -ович/-ович or -івна/ївна)
    if base.ends_with?('ович')
      base.chomp('ович') + 'овичу'
    elsif base.ends_with?('івна') || base.ends_with?('ївна')
      base.chomp('івна').chomp('ївна') + 'івні' + gender_suffix
    # Handle common male surnames
    elsif base.ends_with?('ов', 'єв', 'ін', 'ин', 'ський', 'ський', 'ський',
                         'ський', 'ський', 'цький', 'цький', 'ко', 'ке')
      base + gender_suffix
    # Handle common female surnames
    elsif base.ends_with?('ова', 'ева', 'ина', 'ина', 'ская', 'ская',
                         'ская', 'ська', 'цька', 'ко', 'ке')
      base + gender_suffix
    # Handle common first names (masculine)
    elsif base.ends_with?('ий', 'ий', 'ий', 'ий', 'ій', 'ій', 'ій')
      base.chomp('ий').chomp('ій') + 'ю'
    # Handle common first names (feminine)
    elsif base.ends_with?('а', 'я', 'я')
      base + 'ї'
    else
      # Default fallback
      name + 'ові' + gender_suffix
    end
  end

  private

  def normalize_name(name)
    # Remove accents and normalize
    Unidecoder.decode(name).downcase.gsub(/[^a-zа-яієї]/, '').to_s
  end

  def load_default_rules
    @default_rules = {
      # Surnames
      'курчатова' => 'курчатовій',
      'курчатову' => 'курчатову',
      'іванов' => 'іванову',
      'смирнова' => 'смирновій',
      'петров' => 'петрову',
      'васильєв' => 'васильєву',
      'андрієвський' => 'андрієвському',
      'коваленко' => 'коваленку',
      'бойко' => 'бойку',
      'ткаченко' => 'ткаченку',
      'леонтьєва' => 'леонтьєвій',
      'мороз' => 'морозу',

      # First names
      'олександр' => 'олександру',
      'викторія' => 'викторії',
      'анастасія' => 'анастасії',
      'максим' => 'максиму',
      'олга' => 'олзі',
      'андрій' => 'андрію',
      'сергій' => 'сергію',
      'олксана' => 'олксані',

      # Patronymics
      'іванович' => 'івановичу',
      'петрович' => 'петровичу',
      'степанович' => 'степановичу',
      'дмитрович' => 'дмитровичу',
      'олегович' => 'олеговичу',
      'в’ячеславович' => 'в’ячеславовичу',
      'олегівна' => 'олегівні',
      'петрівна' => 'петрівні',
      'степанівна' => 'степанівні',
      'дмитріївна' => 'дмитріївні',
      'в’ячеславівна' => 'в’ячеславівні'
    }
  end

  # Suffixes for different name parts
  def gender_suffix
    @custom_rules.key?(:male_suffix) ? @custom_rules[:male_suffix] :
    @custom_rules.key?(:female_suffix) ? @custom_rules[:female_suffix] : ''
  end
  alias :male_suffix :gender_suffix
  alias :female_suffix :gender_suffix
end

```ruby
# app/slug_generator.rb
require 'transliterator'

class SlugGenerator
  # Метод для генерації слагу з українського тексту
  def self.generate_from_title(title)
    return "" if title.blank?

    # 1. Приводимо текст до нижнього регістру
    translit_text = title.downcase

    # 2. Транслітерація українського тексту
    translit_text = translit_text.transliterate(
      :uk => :en,
      :replace => {
        'ї' => 'i', 'є' => 'e', 'ю' => 'yu', 'я' => 'ya',
        'х' => 'kh', 'щ' => 'shch', # додаткові правила, якщо потрібно
      }
    )

    # 3. Заміна пробілів на дефіси
    slug = translit_text.gsub(/\s+/, '-')

    # 4. Видалення інших недопустимих символів (крім літер, цифр і дефісів)
    slug = slug.gsub(/[^\w\-]/, '')

    # 5. Заміна послідовних дефісів на один
    slug = slug.gsub(/-+/, '-')

    # 6. Видалення дефісів в початку/кінці
    slug.squeeze('-').strip('-')

  rescue => e
    Rails.logger.error "Slug generation error: #{e.message}" if defined?(Rails)
    title.parameterize # fallback на стандартний параметризатор
  end
end
```

# app/profanity_filter.rb
require 'set'

class ProfanityFilter
  # Ukrainian profanity list (this is just a sample - in production you'd want a more comprehensive list)
  PROFANITY_LIST = Set.new([
    "хуй", "хуйло", "хуї", "хуїло", "хуйня", "хуйняк", "хуйновий",
    "пизда", "пізда", "пиздок", "пиздюк", "пиздюка", "пиздючій",
    "сука", "сучка", "сук", "сукін", "сукінський", "сукини",
    "блядь", "блядюга", "бляди", "блядки", "блядівка", "блядів",
    "мудак", "мудила", "мудої", "муди", "мудянка", "мудянки",
    "ебать", "єбать", "ебати", "єбати", "єбатися", "єбалися",
    "пиздато", "пиздатий", "пиздючий", "пиздюкаючий"
  ]).freeze

  # Common Ukrainian profanity prefixes that might appear before words
  PROFANITY_PREFIXES = Set.new(["на", "по", "за", "під", "роз", "розі"]).freeze

  def initialize(replace_with: '****', case_sensitive: false)
    @replace_with = replace_with
    @case_sensitive = case_sensitive
  end

  def filter(text)
    return text unless text.is_a?(String)

    words = text.split(/\s+/)
    processed_words = words.map do |word|
      original_word = word
      if @case_sensitive
        word.downcase!
      end

      # Check if word or any prefixed version is profanity
      PROFANITY_PREFIXES.each do |prefix|
        next unless word.start_with?(prefix)
        remaining = word[prefix.length..-1]
        if PROFANITY_LIST.include?(remaining)
          return original_word.gsub(remaining, @replace_with)
        end
      end

      # Check if word itself is profanity
      if PROFANITY_LIST.include?(word)
        @replace_with
      else
        original_word
      end
    end

    processed_words.join(' ')
  end

  # Alternative method that uses regex for slightly better performance
  def filter_with_regex(text)
    return text unless text.is_a?(String)

    # Build regex pattern from profanity list
    pattern = PROFANITY_LIST.map { |word| Regexp.escape(word) }.join('|')

    # Create regex with word boundaries and case insensitivity
    regex = /\b(#{pattern})\b/i unless @case_sensitive
    regex ||= /\b(#{pattern})\b/

    # Replace matches
    text.gsub(regex) { @replace_with }
  end
end

  ].freeze

  RUSSIAN_WORDS = %w[
    русский русским русские русскому русскими русскими русского русские
    русская русским русские русскую русского русские русскими
  ].freeze

  COMMON_SURZHYK_WORDS = [
    'гроші', 'граш', 'граші', 'грошей', 'гроши', 'гроша', # Money (Ukrainian: гроші, Russian: деньги)
    'купити', 'купить', 'купує', 'купив', 'купать', 'купівля', # Buy (Ukrainian: купити, Russian: купить)
    'детки', 'діти', 'дітей', 'детей', 'діти', 'дети', # Kids (Ukrainian: діти, Russian: дети)
    'папа', 'тато', 'батько', 'батька', 'батьків', 'отца', # Dad (Ukrainian: тато/батько, Russian: папа/отец)
    'мама', 'мати', 'мати', 'матерi', 'маму', 'маму', # Mom (common in both with slight variations)
    'робота', 'робот', 'робота', 'работа', 'работе', 'робота', # Work (Ukrainian: робота, Russian: работа)
    'газова', 'газ', 'газовый', 'газу', 'гази', 'газ', # Gas (Ukrainian: газ, Russian: газ)
    'кухня', 'кухня', 'кухни', 'кухон', 'кухонь', # Kitchen (common in both)
  ].freeze

  UKRAINIAN_LETTERS = /[ґїєії]/ # Ukrainian-specific letters
  RUSSIAN_LETTERS = /[ё]/ # Russian-specific letters

  def initialize(text)
    @text = text.to_s
    @words = @text.downcase.split
    @ukrainian_score = 0
    @russian_score = 0
    @surzhyk_score = 0
  end

  def detect
    analyze_words
    analyze_letters
    analyze_surzhyk_patterns

    determine_language
  end

  private

  def analyze_words
    UKRAINIAN_WORDS.each do |word|
      if @words.any? { |w| w.include?(word) }
        @ukrainian_score += 1
      end
    end

    RUSSIAN_WORDS.each do |word|
      if @words.any? { |w| w.include?(word) }
        @russian_score += 1
      end
    end
  end

  def analyze_letters
    if @text.match?(UKRAINIAN_LETTERS)
      @ukrainian_score += 0.5
    end

    if @text.match?(RUSSIAN_LETTERS)
      @russian_score += 0.5
    end
  end

  def analyze_surzhyk_patterns

      if @words.any? { |w| w.include?(word) }
        @surzhyk_score += 1
        # Deduct from pure languages if we found surzhyk words
        @ukrainian_score -= 0.3 if @ukrainian_score > 0
        @russian_score -= 0.3 if @russian_score > 0
      end
    end
  end

  def determine_language
    max_score = [@ukrainian_score, @russian_score, @surzhyk_score].max

    if max_score >= 1.5
      if @surzhyk_score == max_score
        :surzhyk
      elsif @ukrainian_score == max_score
        :ukrainian
      else
        :russian
      end
    else
      :unknown
    end
  end

# lib/ukrainian_slug_generator.rb
require 'uktranslit'
require 'active_support/core_ext/string/inflections'

class UkrainianSlugGenerator
  # Transliteration mappings for Ukrainian to Latin characters
  TRANSLITERATION_MAP = {
    'а' => 'a', 'А' => 'A',
    'б' => 'b', 'Б' => 'B',
    'в' => 'v', 'В' => 'V',
    'г' => 'h', 'Г' => 'H',
    'ґ' => 'g', 'Ґ' => 'G',
    'д' => 'd', 'Д' => 'D',
    'е' => 'e', 'Е' => 'E',
    'є' => 'ie', 'Є' => 'Ie',
    'ж' => 'zh', 'Ж' => 'Zh',
    'з' => 'z', 'З' => 'Z',
    'и' => 'y', 'И' => 'Y',
    'і' => 'i', 'І' => 'I',
    'ї' => 'yi', 'Ї' => 'Yi',
    'й' => 'i', 'Й' => 'I',
    'к' => 'k', 'К' => 'K',
    'л' => 'l', 'Л' => 'L',
    'м' => 'm', 'М' => 'M',
    'н' => 'n', 'Н' => 'N',
    'о' => 'o', 'О' => 'O',
    'п' => 'p', 'П' => 'P',
    'р' => 'r', 'Р' => 'R',
    'с' => 's', 'С' => 'S',
    'т' => 't', 'Т' => 'T',
    'у' => 'u', 'У' => 'U',
    'ф' => 'f', 'Ф' => 'F',
    'х' => 'kh', 'Х' => 'Kh',
    'ц' => 'ts', 'Ц' => 'Ts',
    'ч' => 'ch', 'Ч' => 'Ch',
    'ш' => 'sh', 'Ш' => 'Sh',
    'щ' => 'shch', 'Щ' => 'Shch',
    'ь' => '', 'Ь' => '',
    'ю' => 'iu', 'Ю' => 'IU',
    'я' => 'ia', 'Я' => 'IA'
  }.freeze

  # Common Ukrainian words to exclude from slugs
  STOP_WORDS = %w[і в на з до з при за з без про для під уперед над від із по відносно безпосередньо].freeze

  def self.generate(slug_title)
    # Convert to transliterated form
    transliterated = slug_title.mb_chars.to_s

    # Replace special characters
    slug = transliterated
      .gsub(/[^\w\sа-яА-ЯіІїЇєЄ]/, '')
      .gsub(/[а-яА-ЯіІїЇєЄ]/, TRANSLITERATION_MAP)
      .gsub(/[^a-zA-Z0-9\s-]/, '')
      .downcase

    # Clean up multiple dashes and spaces
    slug = slug.gsub(/\s+/, '-').gsub(/-+/, '-').strip

    # Remove stop words (optional)
    words = slug.split('-')
    words.reject! { |word| STOP_WORDS.include?(word) }
    slug = words.join('-')

    # Remove leading/trailing dashes
    slug.gsub(/^-+/, '').gsub(/-+$/, '')
  end
end

  'а', 'б', 'в', 'г', 'ґ', 'д', 'е', 'є', 'ж', 'з', 'и', 'і', 'ї', 'й',

def ukrainian_sort_word(a, b)
  a.downcase.chars.each_with_index do |char_a, index|

    break 0 if char_b.nil?

    index_a = UKRAINIAN_ALPHABET_ORDER.index(char_a)

def ukrainian_text_to_speech(text, output_file = 'ukrainian_speech.mp3')

Hyphenator.dictionary = {

      'Донецьк', 'Івано-Франківськ', 'Чернігів', 'Полтава', 'КривийРіг'
    ]
  }
}

# Клас для розставляння переносів у українських словах
class UkrainianHyphenator
  def initialize
    @hyphenator = Hyphenator.new(:uk)
  end

  # Метод для розставляння переносів у тексті
  def add_hyphens(text)
    # Розбиваємо текст на слова
    words = text.split(/\s+/)

    processed_words = words.map do |word|
      # Проверяем, нужно ли добавлять переносы для этого слова
      if needs_hyphenation?(word)
        @hyphenator.hyphenate(word).join('-')
      else
        word
      end
    end

    processed_words.join(' ')
  end

  private

  # Метод для визначення, чи потрібно розставляти переноси в слові
  def needs_hyphenation?(word)
    # Не розставляємо переноси в словах, які задовольняють певні умови
    return false if word.length <= 6 # Слова коротші за 6 символів
    return false if word.match?(/^[A-ZА-ЯЇЄІЇҐ]+$/) # Аббревіатури
    return false if word.match?(/^[0-9а-щА-ЩЇїЄєІіҐґ]+-?[0-9а-щА-ЩЇїЄєІіҐґ]+$/) # Географічні назви
    true
  end
end

# Ruby Implementation for Latin-to-Ukrainian Keyboard Layout Conversion

Here's a complete solution that includes a Gemfile and the implementation code.

## Gemfile

```ruby
source "https://rubygems.org"

# Core gem for string manipulation
gem "active_support", "~> 7.0"

# For command-line interface if needed

```

## Implementation

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "active_support/core_ext/string"

# Latin-to-Ukrainian keyboard layout converter
class UkrainianKeyboardConverter
  # Mapping from Latin characters to Ukrainian characters
  # Based on the standard QWERTY -> Ukrainian layout
  TRANSLATION_MAP = {
    "q" => "й", "w" => "ц", "e" => "у", "r" => "к", "t" => "е", "y" => "н",
    "u" => "г", "i" => "ш", "o" => "щ", "p" => "з", "[" => "х", "]" => "ї",
    "a" => "ф", "s" => "и", "d" => "в", "f" => "а", "g" => "п", "h" => "р",
    "j" => "о", "k" => "л", "l" => "д", ";" => "ж", "'" => "є", "Q" => "Й",
    "W" => "Ц", "E" => "У", "R" => "К", "T" => "Е", "Y" => "Н", "U" => "Г",
    "I" => "Ш", "O" => "Щ", "P" => "З", "{" => "Х", "}" => "Ї", "A" => "Ф",
    "S" => "И", "D" => "В", "F" => "А", "G" => "П", "H" => "Р", "J" => "О",
    "K" => "Л", "L" => "Д", ";" => "Ж", ":" => "Ж", "\"" => "Є"
  }.freeze

  # Characters that should remain unchanged
  NEUTRAL_CHARS = [/\s/, /[0-9]/, /[^a-zA-Z[\];'"{}]/].freeze

  # Convert a Latin input string to Ukrainian
  # @param input [String] The text to convert
  # @return [String] The converted text
  def self.convert(input)
    input.chars.map do |char|
      TRANSLATION_MAP.key?(char) ? TRANSLATION_MAP[char] : char
    end.join
  end

  # Convert input from a file and write to output file
  # @param input_file [String] Path to input file
  # @param output_file [String] Path to output file
  def self.convert_file(input_file, output_file)
    text = File.read(input_file)
    converted = convert(text)
    File.write(output_file, converted)
    converted
  end

  # Interactive mode for converting text
  # @return [void]
  def self.interactive
    require "tty-prompt"

    prompt = TTY::Prompt.new
    puts "Ukrainian Keyboard Layout Converter"
    puts "Type your Latin text (type 'exit' to quit)"

    loop do
      input = prompt.ask("Enter text:") rescue nil
      break if input.nil? || input.downcase == "exit"

      puts "Converted: #{convert(input)}"
      puts "-" * 40
    end
  end
end

if __FILE__ == $0
  # Command line interface
  if ARGV.size == 0
    UkrainianKeyboardConverter.interactive
  elsif ARGV.size == 1
    puts UkrainianKeyboardConverter.convert(ARGV[0])
  elsif ARGV.size == 2
    puts UkrainianKeyboardConverter.convert_file(ARGV[0], ARGV[1])
  else
    puts "Usage: ruby ukrainian_converter.rb [text] | [input_file output_file]"
  end
end
```

## Usage Examples

1. **Convert a string directly:**
```ruby
require_relative 'ukrainian_converter'
puts UkrainianKeyboardConverter.convert("Qwerty")
# Output: Йццук
```

2. **Interactive mode:**
```bash
ruby ukrainian_converter.rb
```

3. **Convert a file:**
```bash

```

## Features

1. Handles both lowercase and uppercase Latin characters
2. Preserves numbers, punctuation, and whitespace
3. Can be used programmatically or via command line
4. Interactive mode for easy testing
5. File conversion capability

The converter uses the standard QWERTY to Ukrainian keyboard layout mapping, which is the most common layout for Ukrainian keyboards. The mapping is defined in the `TRANSLATION_MAP` constant.

require 'stanford-corenlp'

# Configure Stanford CoreNLP for Ukrainian
class UkrainianNamedEntityExtractor
  def initialize
    @logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
    @logger.level = Logger::INFO

    # Initialize Stanford CoreNLP with Ukrainian language support
    # Note: You'll need to download the Ukrainian language models from Stanford
    # and point to the appropriate JAR files
    @stanford_nlp = StanfordCoreNLP.load_library(
      language: :uk,
      props: {
        'annotators' => 'tokenize,ssplit,pos,lemma,ner,depparse',
        'ner.applyFineGrained' => 'true',
        'ner.useSUTime' => '0'
      }
    )
  end

  # Extract named entities from Ukrainian text
  def extract_entities(text)
    # Add language annotation to ensure Ukrainian processing
    annotated = @stanford_nlp.annotate(text, language: :uk)

    entities = {
      people: [],
      organizations: [],
      places: []
    }

    # Process each sentence
    annotated[:sentences].each do |sentence|
      # Process each token in the sentence
      sentence[:tokens].each do |token|
        next unless token[:ner]

        case token[:ner]
        when 'PERSON'
          entities[:people] << token[:word] unless entities[:people].include?(token[:word])
        when 'ORGANIZATION'
          entities[:organizations] << token[:word] unless entities[:organizations].include?(token[:word])
        when 'LOCATION'
          entities[:places] << token[:word] unless entities[:places].include?(token[:word])
        end
      end
    end

    entities
  end

  # Fetch and process a news article
  def process_article(url)
    @logger.info("Fetching article from: #{url}")

    begin
      response = HTTParty.get(url, headers: { 'User-Agent' => 'UkrainianNewsEntityExtractor' })
      raise "Failed to fetch article" unless response.success?

      # Extract main content (this will vary by news site)
      article_content = extract_article_content(response.body)

      @logger.info("Processing article content")
      extract_entities(article_content)
    rescue StandardError => e
      @logger.error("Error processing article: #{e.message}")
      nil
    end
  end

  private

  # Simple HTML content extractor (you may need to customize this)
  def extract_article_content(html)
    # This is a very basic extractor - in production you'd want something more robust
    # like Nokogiri with proper XPath queries for the specific news site
    content = html.split(/<[^>]+>/).join(' ').gsub(/\s+/, ' ').strip
    # Remove common non-content elements
    content.gsub!(/^[^а-яА-ЯіІїЇєЄ]+/, '').gsub!(/[^а-яА-ЯіІїЇєЄ\s]+$/, '')
    content
  end
end

require 'httparty'
require 'date'
require 'active_support/core_ext/date'
require 'active_support/cache/memory_store'

class CurrencyConverter
  CACHE_EXPIRY = 1.day # Cache rates for 1 day

  def initialize(cache_store = ActiveSupport::Cache::MemoryStore.new)
    @cache_store = cache_store
  end

  def fetch_exchange_rates
    today = Date.today
    cache_key = "ecb_exchange_rates_#{today.to_s}"

    # Try to retrieve from cache
    rates = @cache_store.fetch(cache_key, expires_in: CACHE_EXPIRY) do
      puts "Fetching rates from ECB..." # for demonstration
      ecb_rates_from_api
    end
    rates
  end

  private

  def ecb_rates_from_api
    response = HTTParty.get('https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref.xml')

    if response.code == 200
      parse_xml(response.body)
    else
      raise "Failed to fetch exchange rates from ECB: #{response.code}"
    end
  end

  def parse_xml(xml_string)
    require 'xmlsimple'  # This is needed to parse XML

    xml = XML::Simple.parse(xml_string)
    rates = {}

    # Iterate through the cube structure from XML::Simple
    xml['Cube']['Cube'].each do |cube|
      currency = cube['currency']
      rate = cube['rate'].to_f
      rates[currency] = rate
    end

    rates
  end

  public

  def convert(amount, from_currency, to_currency)
    exchange_rates = fetch_exchange_rates

    if exchange_rates.key?(from_currency) && exchange_rates.key?(to_currency)
      # Convert from base currency (usually EUR)
      if from_currency == 'EUR'
        amount_in_eur = amount
      else
        amount_in_eur = amount / exchange_rates[from_currency]
      end

      # Convert to target currency
      converted_amount = amount_in_eur * exchange_rates[to_currency]
      converted_amount
    else
      raise "Unsupported currency: #{from_currency} or #{to_currency}"
    end
  end
end

# Example Usage:
if __FILE__ == $0
  converter = CurrencyConverter.new

  begin
    amount = 100
    from_currency = 'USD'
    to_currency = 'EUR'

    converted_amount = converter.convert(amount, from_currency, to_currency)
    puts "#{amount} #{from_currency} is equal to #{converted_amount} #{to_currency}"

    amount = 50
    from_currency = 'GBP'
    to_currency = 'JPY'

    converted_amount = converter.convert(amount, from_currency, to_currency)
    puts "#{amount} #{from_currency} is equal to #{converted_amount} #{to_currency}"

  rescue => e
    puts "Error: #{e.message}"
  end
end

**Explanation and Key Improvements:**

1.  **Gemfile:**  Lists `httparty` for making HTTP requests, `date` for date manipulation and `active_support` for caching helpers.
2.  **Caching:**
    *   Uses `ActiveSupport::Cache::MemoryStore` (easy for demonstration, but you could swap this out for a Redis or other cache store).
    *   `CACHE_EXPIRY` constant controls how long rates are cached (1 day).
    *   `fetch_exchange_rates` method checks the cache first. If the rates aren't in the cache, it fetches them from the ECB and stores them in the cache.  The `expires_in:` option on `cache_store.fetch` automatically expires the cache entry after the specified time.
3.  **ECB API Interaction:**

4.  **XML Parsing:**

    *   The XML structure from the ECB is a bit complex (nested cubes). The code iterates through the appropriate nested structure to extract the currency and rate.
5.  **Currency Conversion Logic:**
    *   `convert` method takes the amount, from currency, and to currency as input.
    *   It fetches the exchange rates using `fetch_exchange_rates`.
    *   It performs the currency conversion.

require 'httparty'
require 'date'

module CacheExchangeRates

  VERSION = '0.1.0'

  ECB_API_URL = 'https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref/html/eurofxref.xml'
  CACHE_FILE = 'exchange_rates.cache'

  def self.get_exchange_rate(target_currency)
    cache_key = "#{Date.today.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}-#{target_currency}"
    cached_rates = read_cache

    if cached_rates && cached_rates.key?(cache_key)
      return cached_rates[cache_key]
    end

    exchange_rate = fetch_exchange_rate(target_currency)
    write_cache(exchange_rate)
    return exchange_rate
  end

  private

  def self.fetch_exchange_rate(target_currency)
    response = HTTParty.get(ECB_API_URL)
    raise "Failed to fetch exchange rates: #{response.code}" if response.code != 200

    xml = Hash.from_xml(response.body)
    cube = xml['Cube']['Cube']

    rate = cube.find { |c| c['currency'] == target_currency }

    raise "Currency not found: #{target_currency}" if rate.nil?

    rate['rate'].to_f
  end

  def self.read_cache
    if File.exist?(CACHE_FILE)
      begin
        File.read(CACHE_FILE) do |file|
          YAML.safe_load(file, permitted_classes: [Date])
        end
      rescue StandardError => e
        puts "Error reading cache file: #{e.message}"
        return nil
      end
    else
      nil
    end
  end

  def self.write_cache(exchange_rate)
    cache_key = "#{Date.today.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}-#{exchange_rate.key}"
    cached_rates = read_cache || {}
    cached_rates[cache_key] = exchange_rate.value
    begin
      File.open(CACHE_FILE, 'w') do |file|
        YAML.dump(cached_rates, file)
      end
    rescue StandardError => e
      puts "Error writing cache file: #{e.message}"
    end
  end
end

class NewsNERExtractor
  def initialize
    @db = SQLite3::Database.new("named_entities.db")

    # Створюємо таблицю для зберігання результатів
    @db.execute <<-SQL
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS named_entities (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        source_url TEXT,
        article_title TEXT,
        entity_type TEXT,
        entity_text TEXT,
        confidence REAL,
        processed_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
      );
    SQL

    # Для зберігання посилань на вже оброблені статті
    @db.execute <<-SQL
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS processed_urls (
        url TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        processed_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
      );
    SQL
  end

  def fetch_news_urls(news_sources)
    urls = []

    news_sources.each do |source|
      response = HTTParty.get(source[:url])
      doc = Nokogiri::HTML(response.body)

      # Шукаємо всі посилання на статті (можна адаптувати під конкретний сайт)
      doc.css(source[:article_selector] || 'a').each do |link|
        url = link[:href]
        next unless url

        # Додаємо протокол, якщо його немає
        url = "https:#{url}" unless url.start_with?('http')

        # Перевіряємо, чи вже обробляли цю статтю
        next if @db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM processed_urls WHERE url = ?", [url]).any?

        urls << url
      end
    end

    urls.uniq
  end

  def extract_entities_from_text(text)
    # Підготовка тексту: видаляємо HTML-теги, розбиваємо на речення
    clean_text = Nokogiri::HTML.fragment(text).text
    sentences = clean_text.gsub(/\s+/, ' ').split(/[.!?]/)

    entities = []

    sentences.each do |sentence|
      next if sentence.strip.empty?

      # Створюємо документ для аналізу
      doc = Stanford::Document.new(sentence)

      # Витягуємо іменовані сутності
      doc.entities.each do |entity|
        entities << {
          type: entity.type,
          text: entity.text,

# Ukrainian Surzhyk Checker

Here's a Ruby implementation that checks Ukrainian text for surzhyk words (Ukrainian-Russian hybrid words) and suggests literary Ukrainian replacements.

## Gemfile
