require 'httparty'
require 'json'
require 'dotenv/load'

class KyivstarSMS
  include HTTParty
  
  # Configure HTTParty
  default_timeout 30
  
  def initialize(api_key, base_url = 'https://api.kyivstar.ua')
    @api_key = api_key
    @base_url = base_url
    self.class.base_uri(@base_url)
  end
  
  # Send SMS message
  def send_sms(to, message, from = nil)
    # Validate required parameters
    raise ArgumentError, 'Recipient phone number is required' if to.nil? || to.empty?
    raise ArgumentError, 'Message content is required' if message.nil? || message.empty?
    
    # Prepare request payload
    payload = {
      to: to,
      text: message
    }
    
    # Add sender ID if provided
    payload[:from] = from if from && !from.empty?
    
    # Make API request
    response = self.class.post(
      '/sms/send',
      headers: {
        'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@api_key}",
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
      },
      body: payload.to_json
    )
    
    # Handle response
    case response.code
    when 200..201
      handle_success(response)
    when 400
      handle_bad_request(response)
    when 401
      handle_unauthorized(response)
    when 403
      handle_forbidden(response)
    when 429
      handle_rate_limit(response)
    else
      handle_error(response)
    end
  end
  
  # Send multiple SMS messages
  def send_bulk_sms(recipients, message, from = nil)
    raise ArgumentError, 'Recipient list is required' if recipients.nil? || recipients.empty?
    raise ArgumentError, 'Message content is required' if message.nil? || message.empty?
    
    # Prepare request payload
    payload = {
      messages: recipients.map do |recipient|
        msg_data = { to: recipient, text: message }
        msg_data[:from] = from if from && !from.empty?
        msg_data
      end
    }
    
    # Make API request
    response = self.class.post(
      '/sms/send/bulk',
      headers: {
        'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@api_key}",
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
      },
      body: payload.to_json
    )
    
    # Handle response
    case response.code
    when 200..201
      handle_success(response)
    when 400
      handle_bad_request(response)
    when 401
      handle_unauthorized(response)
    when 403
      handle_forbidden(response)
    when 429
      handle_rate_limit(response)
    else
      handle_error(response)
    end
  end
  
  private
  
  def handle_success(response)
    response_data = JSON.parse(response.body)
    {
      success: true,
      message_id: response_data['messageId'],
      status: response_data['status'],
      response: response_data
    }
  end
  
  def handle_bad_request(response)
    error_data = JSON.parse(response.body)
    {
      success: false,
      error: 'Bad Request',
      message: error_data['message'],
      code: response.code
    }
  end
  
  def handle_unauthorized(response)
    {
      success: false,
      error: 'Unauthorized',
      message: 'Invalid API key provided',
      code: response.code
    }
  end
  
  def handle_forbidden(response)
    error_data = JSON.parse(response.body)
    {
      success: false,
      error: 'Forbidden',
      message: error_data['message'],
      code: response.code
    }
  end
  
  def handle_rate_limit(response)
    {
      success: false,
      error: 'Rate Limit Exceeded',
      message: 'Too many requests. Please try again later.',
      code: response.code
    }
  end
  
  def handle_error(response)
    {
      success: false,
      error: 'API Error',
      message: "HTTP #{response.code}: #{response.body}",
      code: response.code
    }
  end
end

require 'httparty'
require 'json'

class ViberMessageSender
  include HTTParty

  def initialize(api_key, base_url = 'https://viber.infobip.com')
    @base_url = base_url
    @api_key = api_key
    @headers = {
      'Authorization' => "App #{@api_key}",
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
      'Accept' => 'application/json'
    }
  end

  def send_viber_message(to_number, message_text, sender_name = 'Infobip')
    # Ensure the phone number is in international format for Ukraine
    formatted_number = format_phone_number(to_number)
    
    # Build the message payload
    payload = {
      "from" => sender_name,
      "to" => {
        "phoneNumber" => formatted_number
      },
      "message" => {
        "text" => message_text
      }
    }

    # Send the message
    response = self.class.post(
      "#{@base_url}/viber/1/message/text",
      headers: @headers,
      body: payload.to_json
    )

    handle_response(response)
  end

  private

  def format_phone_number(phone_number)
    # Remove any non-digit characters
    digits_only = phone_number.gsub(/\D/, '')
    
    # Handle Ukrainian numbers (380 prefix)
    if digits_only.start_with?('380')
      digits_only
    elsif digits_only.start_with?('0')
      # Convert 0xxxxxxxxx to 380xxxxxxxxx
      "380#{digits_only[1..-1]}"
    else
      # Assume it's already in international format
      digits_only
    end
  end

  def handle_response(response)
    case response.code
    when 200..299
      puts "✅ Message sent successfully!"
      puts "Response: #{response.body}"
      { success: true, response: response.parsed_response }
    when 400
      puts "❌ Bad Request: #{response.body}"
      { success: false, error: 'Bad Request', response: response.parsed_response }
    when 401
      puts "❌ Unauthorized: Invalid API key"
      { success: false, error: 'Unauthorized', response: response.parsed_response }
    when 403
      puts "❌ Forbidden: Insufficient permissions"
      { success: false, error: 'Forbidden', response: response.parsed_response }
    when 429
      puts "❌ Rate Limited: Too many requests"
      { success: false, error: 'Rate Limited', response: response.parsed_response }
    when 500..599
      puts "❌ Server Error: #{response.body}"
      { success: false, error: 'Server Error', response: response.parsed_response }
    else
      puts "❌ Unexpected error: #{response.code} - #{response.body}"
      { success: false, error: "Unexpected error: #{response.code}", response: response.parsed_response }
    end
  end
end

require 'httparty'

class VodafoneUkraineMessenger
  include HTTParty
  
  # Configure HTTParty
  default_timeout 30
  headers 'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
  
  def initialize(api_key, logger = nil)
    @api_key = api_key
    @logger = logger || Logger.new(STDOUT)
    @base_url = 'https://api.vodafone.ua'
  end
  
  # Send SMS message
  def send_sms(to, message, sender = nil)
    endpoint = '/sms/send'
    
    payload = {
      to: to,
      text: message,
      sender: sender
    }.delete_if { |_, v| v.nil? || v.empty? }
    
    response = make_request(endpoint, payload)
    
    if response.success?
      @logger.info("SMS sent successfully to #{to}")
      response.parsed_response
    else
      @logger.error("Failed to send SMS to #{to}: #{response.body}")
      raise "SMS sending failed: #{response.body}"
    end
  end
  
  # Send Viber message
  def send_viber(to, message, sender = nil, viber_options = {})
    endpoint = '/viber/send'
    
    payload = {
      to: to,
      text: message,
      sender: sender,
      viber_options: viber_options
    }.delete_if { |_, v| v.nil? || v.empty? }
    
    response = make_request(endpoint, payload)
    
    if response.success?
      @logger.info("Viber message sent successfully to #{to}")
      response.parsed_response
    else
      @logger.error("Failed to send Viber message to #{to}: #{response.body}")
      raise "Viber message sending failed: #{response.body}"
    end
  end
  
  # Send both SMS and Viber
  def send_both(to, sms_message, viber_message, sender = nil)
    results = {}
    
    begin
      results[:sms] = send_sms(to, sms_message, sender)
    rescue => e
      results[:sms] = { error: e.message }
    end
    
    begin
      results[:viber] = send_viber(to, viber_message, sender)
    rescue => e
      results[:viber] = { error: e.message }
    end
    
    results
  end
  
  private
  
  def make_request(endpoint, payload)
    # Add authentication header
    headers = {
      'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@api_key}",
      'Accept' => 'application/json'
    }
    
    # Make the HTTP request
    self.class.post(
      "#{@base_url}#{endpoint}",
      headers: headers,
      body: payload.to_json
    )
  end
end

require 'httparty'
require 'json'

class LifecellSMS
  include HTTParty
  
  # Configure default options for HTTParty
  default_timeout 30
  headers 'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
  
  def initialize(api_key, base_url = 'https://api.lifecell.ua')
    @api_key = api_key
    @base_url = base_url
    @headers = {
      'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@api_key}",
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
    }
  end
  
  # Send one-time password to a phone number
  def send_otp(phone_number, otp, message_template = nil)
    # Validate phone number format
    unless valid_phone_number?(phone_number)
      raise ArgumentError, "Invalid phone number format"
    end
    
    # Prepare message template
    message = message_template || "Your one-time password is: #{otp}"
    
    # Prepare request data
    data = {
      to: phone_number,
      message: message,
      type: 'otp'
    }
    
    begin
      response = self.class.post(
        "#{@base_url}/sms/send",
        headers: @headers,
        body: data.to_json
      )
      
      # Parse response
      result = JSON.parse(response.body)
      
      if response.success?
        {
          success: true,
          message_id: result['message_id'],
          status: result['status']
        }
      else
        {
          success: false,
          error: result['error'] || response.body,
          status_code: response.code
        }
      end
    rescue JSON::ParserError => e
      {
        success: false,
        error: "Failed to parse response: #{e.message}"
      }
    rescue => e
      {
        success: false,
        error: "Network error: #{e.message}"
      }
    end
  end
  
  # Validate phone number format (basic validation)
  def valid_phone_number?(phone_number)
    # Remove non-digit characters
    digits_only = phone_number.gsub(/\D/, '')
    
    # Check if it's a valid Ukrainian phone number format
    # Accepts formats: +380XXXXXXXXX, 380XXXXXXXXX, 0XXXXXXXXX
    return false if digits_only.length < 9 || digits_only.length > 12
    
    # For Ukrainian numbers, check if it starts with 380 or 0
    if digits_only.start_with?('380')
      digits_only.length == 12
    elsif digits_only.start_with?('0')
      digits_only.length == 10
    else
      false
    end
  end
  
  # Send OTP with automatic generation
  def send_otp_auto(phone_number, length = 6, message_template = nil)
    # Generate OTP
    otp = generate_otp(length)
    
    # Send OTP
    send_otp(phone_number, otp, message_template)
  end
  
  # Generate random OTP
  def generate_otp(length = 6)
    (0..length-1).map { rand(0..9).to_s }.join
  end
  
  # Check message status
  def check_status(message_id)
    begin
      response = self.class.get(
        "#{@base_url}/sms/status/#{message_id}",
        headers: @headers
      )
      
      result = JSON.parse(response.body)
      
      if response.success?
        {
          success: true,
          status: result['status'],
          delivered: result['delivered']
        }
      else
        {
          success: false,
          error: result['error'] || response.body
        }
      end
    rescue JSON::ParserError => e
      {
        success: false,
        error: "Failed to parse response: #{e.message}"
      }
    rescue => e
      {
        success: false,
        error: "Network error: #{e.message}"
      }
    end
  end
end

### 2. `unione_client.rb` — основний клас для роботи з API UniOne

```ruby
require 'httparty'
require 'json'

class UniOneClient
  include HTTParty

  base_uri 'https://api.unione.io/v1'

  attr_accessor :api_key

  def initialize(api_key)
    @api_key = api_key
    self.class.default_timeout 30
  end

  # Надсилання транзакційного повідомлення
  def send_transactional_message(recipient, subject, body, sender = nil)
    headers = {
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
      'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@api_key}"
    }

    payload = {
      recipient: recipient,
      subject: subject,
      body: body,
      sender: sender || 'noreply@yourdomain.com'
    }

    response = self.class.post(
      '/send',
      headers: headers,
      body: payload.to_json
    )

    parse_response(response)
  end

  private

  def parse_response(response)
    case response.code
    when 200
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      raise "API error: #{response.code} - #{response.body}"
    end
  end
end
```

require 'httparty'
require 'dotenv/load'
require 'json'

class SendPulseEmail
  include HTTParty

  BASE_URL = 'https://api.sendpulse.com'.freeze

  def initialize
    @client_id = ENV['SENDPULSE_CLIENT_ID']
    @client_secret = ENV['SENDPULSE_CLIENT_SECRET']
    @access_token = nil
  end

  def get_token
    response = self.class.post(
      "#{BASE_URL}/oauth/access_token",
      body: {
        grant_type: 'client_credentials',
        client_id: @client_id,
        client_secret: @client_secret
      }
    )

    if response.success?
      @access_token = response['access_token']
    else
      raise "Failed to get access token: #{response.body}"
    end
  end

  def send_email(to_email, subject, body, from_email = nil, from_name = nil)
    get_token unless @access_token

    response = self.class.post(
      "#{BASE_URL}/smtp/emails",
      headers: {
        'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@access_token}",
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
      },
      body: {
        email: {
          subject: subject,
          body: body,
          from: {
            email: from_email || 'default@example.com',
            name: from_name || 'Default Sender'
          },
          to: [
            {
              email: to_email
            }
          ]
        }
      }.to_json
    )

    if response.success?
      puts "Email sent successfully to #{to_email}"
    else
      puts "Error sending email: #{response.body}"
    end
  end
end

Here's a complete Ruby solution for sending push notifications to Diia app users via the Diia partner API:

**Gemfile**
```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'httparty'
gem 'json'
gem 'dotenv'
gem 'logger'
```

**lib/diia_push_notification.rb**
```ruby
require 'httparty'
require 'json'
require 'logger'
require 'dotenv/load'

class DiiaPushNotification
  include HTTParty

  # Configure HTTParty
  default_timeout 30
  format :json

  def initialize(api_key:, base_url: 'https://partner-api.diia.gov.ua')
    @api_key = api_key
    @base_url = base_url
    @logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
    @logger.level = Logger::INFO
  end

  # Send push notification to a single user
  def send_notification(user_id:, title:, body:, data: {}, badge: nil, sound: 'default')
    payload = {
      userId: user_id,
      title: title,
      body: body,
      data: data,
      badge: badge,
      sound: sound
    }

    response = self.class.post(
      "#{@base_url}/notifications",
      headers: {
        'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@api_key}",
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
      },
      body: payload.to_json
    )

    handle_response(response)
  end

  # Send push notification to multiple users
  def send_bulk_notifications(notifications)
    payload = {
      notifications: notifications
    }

    response = self.class.post(
      "#{@base_url}/notifications/bulk",
      headers: {
        'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@api_key}",
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
      },
      body: payload.to_json
    )

    handle_response(response)
  end

  # Send scheduled notification
  def schedule_notification(user_id:, title:, body:, scheduled_time:, data: {})
    payload = {
      userId: user_id,
      title: title,
      body: body,
      scheduledTime: scheduled_time,
      data: data
    }

    response = self.class.post(
      "#{@base_url}/notifications/schedule",
      headers: {
        'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@api_key}",
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
      },
      body: payload.to_json
    )

    handle_response(response)
  end

  # Get notification status
  def get_notification_status(notification_id)
    response = self.class.get(
      "#{@base_url}/notifications/#{notification_id}",
      headers: {
        'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@api_key}",
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
      }
    )

    handle_response(response)
  end

  private

  def handle_response(response)
    @logger.info("API Response Status: #{response.code}")
    
    case response.code
    when 200..299
      @logger.info("Notification sent successfully")
      response.parsed_response
    when 400
      @logger.error("Bad Request: #{response.parsed_response['error']}")
      raise ArgumentError, response.parsed_response['error']
    when 401
      @logger.error("Unauthorized: Invalid API key")
      raise AuthenticationError, "Invalid API key"
    when 403
      @logger.error("Forbidden: Access denied")
      raise AuthorizationError, "Access denied"
    when 429
      @logger.error("Too Many Requests")
      raise RateLimitError, "Rate limit exceeded"
    when 500..599
      @logger.error("Server Error: #{response.parsed_response['error']}")
      raise ServerError, "Server error occurred"
    else
      @logger.error("Unexpected response: #{response.code}")
      raise StandardError, "Unexpected response code: #{response.code}"
    end
  end
end

# Custom exceptions
class AuthenticationError < StandardError; end
class AuthorizationError < StandardError; end
class RateLimitError < StandardError; end
class ServerError < StandardError; end
```

**lib/diia_notification_service.rb**
```ruby
require_relative 'diia_push_notification'

class DiiaNotificationService

# sms_fly_sender.rb
require 'httparty'
require 'json'
require 'dotenv/load'

class SMSFlySender
  include HTTParty
  
  # Configure HTTParty
  base_uri 'https://api.sms-fly.com'
  headers 'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
  
  def initialize(api_key, sender_name = nil)
    @api_key = api_key
    @sender_name = sender_name
  end
  
  # Send SMS message
  def send_sms(phone_number, message, sender = nil)
    # Validate required parameters
    raise ArgumentError, "Phone number is required" if phone_number.nil? || phone_number.empty?
    raise ArgumentError, "Message is required" if message.nil? || message.empty?
    
    # Prepare request data
    data = {
      apikey: @api_key,
      to: phone_number,
      text: message
    }
    
    # Add sender if provided
    if sender || @sender_name
      data[:from] = sender || @sender_name
    end
    
    # Make API request
    response = self.class.post('/send', body: data.to_json)
    
    # Parse response
    parse_response(response)
  end
  
  # Check account balance
  def get_balance
    response = self.class.get("/balance?apikey=#{@api_key}")
    parse_response(response)
  end
  
  # Get message status
  def get_status(message_id)
    response = self.class.get("/status?apikey=#{@api_key}&id=#{message_id}")
    parse_response(response)
  end
  
  private
  
  # Parse API response
  def parse_response(response)
    if response.success?
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      {
        success: false,
        error: "API Error: #{response.code} - #{response.body}"
      }
    end
  end
end

  # Validate credentials
  if api_key.nil? || api_key.empty?
    puts "Error: SMS_FLY_API_KEY environment variable is required"
    exit 1
  end
  
  # Create SMS sender instance
  sms_sender = SMSFlySender.new(api_key, sender_name)
  
  # Example: Send SMS

# encoding: utf-8
require 'stemmer'
require 'stopwords'

class ProductDescriptionProcessor
  def initialize
    @stopwords = Stopwords::Stopwords.new(:language => :en)
    @stemmer = PorterStemmer::Stemmer.new
  end

  def process_description(description)
    # Перетворюємо на нижній регістр
    text = description.downcase

    # Видаляємо пунктуацію (простий спосіб)
    text = text.gsub(/[^\w\s]/, '')

    # Розбиваємо на слова
    words = text.split

    # Видаляємо стоп-слова
    words = words.reject { |word| @stopwords.stopword?(word) }

    # Стемінг
    stemmed_words = words.map { |word| @stemmer.stem(word) }

    # Об'єднуємо назад у рядок
    stemmed_words.join(' ')
  end
end

class CommentLanguageDetector

# call_client.rb

require 'httparty'
require 'dotenv/load'
require 'json'

class BinotelClient
  include HTTParty

  BASE_URL = 'https://api.binotel.com/api'.freeze

  def initialize
    @api_key = ENV['BINOTEL_API_KEY']
    @api_secret = ENV['BINOTEL_API_SECRET']
    @account_id = ENV['BINOTEL_ACCOUNT_ID']
    @headers = {
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
      'Accept' => 'application/json'
    }
  end

  def make_call(client_phone, message)
    uri = "/call?api_key=#{@api_key}&api_secret=#{@api_secret}&account_id=#{@account_id}&from=#{ENV['BINOTEL_PHONE_NUMBER']}&to=#{client_phone}&text=#{URI.escape(message)}"
    
    response = self.class.get(BASE_URL + uri, headers: @headers)

    if response.success?
      puts "Виклик успішно здійснено!"
      puts response.body
    else
      puts "Помилка при виклику: #{response.code} - #{response.body}"
    end
  end
end

# Виклик клієнта з голосовим повідомленням

```ruby
require 'pdf/reader'
require 'pdf/table'
require 'combine_pdf'

# Функція для витягнення тексту з PDF
def extract_text_from_pdf(pdf_path)
  text = ""
  PDF::Reader.open(pdf_path) do |reader|
    reader.pages.each do |page|
      text += page.text + "\n"
    end
  end
  text
end

# Функція для витягнення таблиць із PDF
def extract_tables_from_pdf(pdf_path)
  tables = []
  PDF::Reader.open(pdf_path) do |reader|
    reader.pages.each_with_index do |page, index|
      # Витягнення таблиць (простий спосіб — якщо таблиці є у форматі тексту)
      page_text = page.text
      # Можливо, тут треба додатково обробляти форматування або використовувати pdf-table
      # Звичайно, pdf-table краще підходить для реальних таблиць
      tables << {
        page: index + 1,
        content: page_text
      }
    end
  end
  tables
end

# Приклад використання
pdf_path = "example.pdf"

puts "=== Текст із PDF ==="
puts extract_text_from_pdf(pdf_path)

puts "\n=== Таблиці із PDF ==="
tables = extract_tables_from_pdf(pdf_path)
tables.each do |table|
  puts "Сторінка #{table[:page]}:"
  puts table[:content]
  puts "-" * 40
end
```

- `pdf-reader` добре працює з простим текстом.
- `pdf-table` — для витягнення таблиць із PDF, але не завжди працює з усіма PDF (особливо якщо таблиці були зображеними або неправильно структурованими).
- Якщо таблиці не витягуються коректно, можна розглянути використання інструментів на основі `pdftotext` або `tabula-java`.

```ruby
# spell_checker.rb
require 'hunspell'
require 'pathname'

class SpellChecker
  def initialize(dictionary_path = nil)
    @dictionary_path = dictionary_path || find_default_dictionary
    @spell_checker = Hunspell::Checker.new(@dictionary_path)
  end

  def check_text(text)
    words = extract_words(text)
    misspelled = []

    words.each do |word|
      next if word.empty?
      
      # Skip words with numbers or special characters
      next if word.match?(/\d+/) || word.match?(/[^\w]/)
      
      # Check if word is misspelled
      unless @spell_checker.spell?(word)
        suggestions = @spell_checker.suggest(word)
        misspelled << {
          word: word,
          suggestions: suggestions.first(5)  # Limit to 5 suggestions
        }
      end
    end

    misspelled
  end

  def check_and_correct(text)
    misspelled = check_text(text)
    
    # Create a copy of the text for correction
    corrected_text = text.dup
    
    # Replace misspelled words with first suggestion
    misspelled.each do |error|
      original_word = error[:word]
      suggestion = error[:suggestions].first
      
      if suggestion
        # Use word boundaries to avoid partial replacements
        corrected_text.gsub!(/\b#{Regexp.escape(original_word)}\b/, suggestion)
      end
    end
    
    {
      original: text,
      corrected: corrected_text,
      errors: misspelled
    }
  end

  def add_word_to_dictionary(word)
    @spell_checker.add(word)
  end

  private

  def extract_words(text)
    # Simple word extraction - split by non-alphabetic characters
    text.downcase.gsub(/[^a-zA-Z]/, ' ').split
  end

  def find_default_dictionary
    # Try to find a default dictionary path
    possible_paths = [
      '/usr/share/hunspell/en_US.dic',
      '/usr/share/hunspell/en_US.aff',
      '/usr/share/dict/words',
      'en_US.dic'
    ]
    
    possible_paths.find { |path| File.exist?(path) } || 'en_US.dic'
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0
  # Initialize spell checker
  checker = SpellChecker.new
  
  # Test text with misspellings
  sample_text = "Ths is a smple text with som mispelled words."
  
  puts "Original text: #{sample_text}"
  puts "\nChecking spelling..."
  
  # Check for errors
  errors = checker.check_text(sample_text)
  
  if errors.empty?
    puts "No spelling errors found!"
  else
    puts "Found spelling errors:"
    errors.each do |error|
      puts "  '#{error[:word]}' -> Suggestions: #{error[:suggestions].join(', ')}"
    end
  end
  
  # Check and correct
  result = checker.check_and_correct(sample_text)
  
  puts "\nCorrected text: #{result[:corrected]}"
  
  # Add a custom word to dictionary
  puts "\nAdding 'Ruby' to dictionary..."
  checker.add_word_to_dictionary('Ruby')
  
  # Test with a word that should now be recognized
  test_with_custom = "I love Ruby programming."
  puts "Testing with custom word: #{test_with_custom}"
  
  errors = checker.check_text(test_with_custom)
  if errors.empty?
    puts "No errors found in custom word test!"
  else
    puts "Errors found: #{errors}"
  end
end
```

# slug_generator.rb
require 'active_support'
require 'active_support/core_ext/string'
require 'unicode'

class SlugGenerator
  def self.generate(title)
    # Convert accented characters to ASCII equivalents
    normalized_title = title.mb_chars.normalize(:d).to_s
    
    # Remove special characters and replace spaces with hyphens
    slug = normalized_title.gsub(/[^a-zA-Z0-9\s-]/, '').gsub(/\s+/, '-').downcase
    
    # Remove leading and trailing hyphens
    slug = slug.gsub(/^-+|-+$/, '')
    
    # Ensure we don't have consecutive hyphens
    slug = slug.gsub(/-+/, '-')
    
    # Handle edge cases
    slug = 'untitled' if slug.empty?
    
    slug
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0

    "Café au Lait: A Cultural Journey",
    "Cómo Vamos? ¡Qué Tal!",
    "Nǐ hǎo, Shìjiè! - Hello World",
    "São Paulo: City of Dreams",
    "À propos de l'art",
    "Hello World!",
    "   Multiple   Spaces   ",
    "Special chars: @#$%^&*()",
    "",
    "123 Numbers 456"
  ]

  puts "Slug Generation Examples:"
  puts "=" * 40
  
  test_titles.each do |title|
    slug = SlugGenerator.generate(title)
    puts "#{title.inspect} => #{slug.inspect}"
  end
end
```

This implementation provides a robust slug generator that:

1. **Handles accented characters** using ActiveSupport's `mb_chars.normalize(:d)` to decompose Unicode characters into their ASCII equivalents
2. **Removes special characters** while preserving alphanumeric characters and hyphens
3. **Converts spaces to hyphens** and normalizes multiple spaces into single hyphens
4. **Handles edge cases** like empty strings, leading/trailing hyphens, and consecutive hyphens
5. **Returns "untitled"** for completely empty or invalid titles

The solution uses:

- `unicode` gem for proper character handling

# lib/product_stemmer.rb
require 'stemmer'
require 'stopwords'
require 'nokogiri'

class ProductStemmer
  # Initialize with default stop words
  def initialize
    @stemmer = Lingua::Stemmer.new(:language => :english)
    @stop_words = Stopwords::Stopwords.stopwords(:language => :english)
  end

  # Process a product description for indexing
  def process_description(description)
    return "" if description.nil? || description.strip.empty?
    
    # Clean and tokenize the description
    tokens = tokenize(description)
    
    # Remove stop words
    tokens = remove_stop_words(tokens)
    
    # Stem the remaining words
    stemmed_tokens = stem_words(tokens)
    
    # Join back into a string
    stemmed_tokens.join(' ')
  end

  # Tokenize text into words
  def tokenize(text)
    # Remove HTML tags if present
    clean_text = Nokogiri::HTML(text).text
    
    # Split by whitespace and punctuation, convert to lowercase
    clean_text.downcase.scan(/[a-zA-Z]+/)
  end

  # Remove stop words from tokens
  def remove_stop_words(tokens)
    tokens.reject { |token| @stop_words.include?(token) }
  end

  # Stem words using Porter stemmer
  def stem_words(tokens)
    tokens.map { |token| @stemmer.stem(token) }
  end

  # Process multiple product descriptions
  def process_descriptions(descriptions)
    descriptions.map { |desc| process_description(desc) }
  end

  # Get the list of stop words (for reference)
  def stop_words
    @stop_words
  end

  # Get the stemmer instance (for testing)
  def stemmer
    @stemmer
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0
  # Create instance
  processor = ProductStemmer.new
  
  # Sample product descriptions
  descriptions = [
    "This is a wonderful product with great features and amazing quality",
    "The product is very good and works perfectly for all your needs",
    "Amazing features, excellent build quality, highly recommended product"
  ]
  
  puts "Original descriptions:"
  descriptions.each_with_index do |desc, index|
    puts "#{index + 1}: #{desc}"
  end
  
  puts "\nProcessed descriptions:"
  processed = processor.process_descriptions(descriptions)
  processed.each_with_index do |proc_desc, index|
    puts "#{index + 1}: #{proc_desc}"
  end
  
  puts "\nStop words sample: #{processor.stop_words.first(10).join(', ')}"
end
```

This implementation provides:

1. **Gemfile** with required gems:
   - `stemmer` for word stemming (Porter stemmer)
   - `stopwords` for stop word removal
   - `nokogiri` for HTML cleaning

2. **ProductStemmer class** with methods:
   - `process_description` - Main method to clean, stem, and remove stop words
   - `tokenize` - Splits text into words, removes HTML tags
   - `remove_stop_words` - Filters out common stop words
   - `stem_words` - Applies stemming to remaining words
   - `process_descriptions` - Processes multiple descriptions

3. **Key features**:
   - Removes HTML tags from descriptions
   - Converts to lowercase for consistency
   - Removes common English stop words
   - Applies Porter stemming algorithm
   - Handles empty or nil inputs gracefully
   - Provides both single and batch processing

4. **Example usage** included to demonstrate functionality

The code will transform "wonderful product with great features" into something like "wonder product great featur" after processing.

require 'httparty'
require 'json'

class MobizonSMS
  include HTTParty
  
  # Base URL for Mobizon API
  base_uri 'https://api.mobizon.com'
  
  def initialize(api_key, sender = nil)
    @api_key = api_key
    @sender = sender
  end
  
  # Send SMS message
  def send_sms(to, message, sender = nil)
    options = {
      query: {
        apikey: @api_key,
        recipient: to,
        text: message
      }
    }
    
    # Add sender if provided
    if sender || @sender
      options[:query][:sender] = sender || @sender
    end
    
    response = self.class.post('/service/message/sendsms', options)
    
    if response.success?
      result = JSON.parse(response.body)
      if result['success']
        {
          success: true,
          message_id: result['data']['messageid'],
          status: 'sent'
        }
      else
        {
          success: false,
          error: result['message']
        }
      end
    else
      {
        success: false,
        error: "HTTP Error: #{response.code}"
      }
    end
  end
  
  # Send SMS with multiple recipients
  def send_sms_bulk(recipients, message, sender = nil)
    # recipients should be an array of phone numbers
    options = {
      query: {
        apikey: @api_key,
        recipient: recipients.join(','),
        text: message
      }
    }
    
    if sender || @sender
      options[:query][:sender] = sender || @sender
    end
    
    response = self.class.post('/service/message/sendsms', options)
    
    if response.success?
      result = JSON.parse(response.body)
      if result['success']
        {
          success: true,
          message_id: result['data']['messageid'],
          status: 'sent'
        }
      else
        {
          success: false,
          error: result['message']
        }
      end
    else
      {
        success: false,
        error: "HTTP Error: #{response.code}"
      }
    end
  end
  
  # Get account balance
  def get_balance
    response = self.class.get('/service/account/getbalance', 
                              query: { apikey: @api_key })
    
    if response.success?
      result = JSON.parse(response.body)
      if result['success']
        {
          success: true,
          balance: result['data']['balance'],
          currency: result['data']['currency']
        }
      else
        {
          success: false,
          error: result['message']
        }
      end
    else
      {
        success: false,
        error: "HTTP Error: #{response.code}"
      }
    end
  end
  
  # Check message status
  def check_message_status(message_id)
    response = self.class.get('/service/message/getmessagestatus', 
                              query: { 
                                apikey: @api_key,
                                messageid: message_id
                              })
    
    if response.success?
      result = JSON.parse(response.body)
      if result['success']
        {
          success: true,
          status: result['data']['status'],
          status_description: result['data']['statusdescription']
        }
      else
        {
          success: false,
          error: result['message']
        }
      end
    else
      {
        success: false,
        error: "HTTP Error: #{response.code}"
      }
    end
  end
end

require 'aspell'
require 'linguist'
require 'colorize'

class SpellChecker
  def initialize
    @aspell = Aspell.new('en_US')
  end

  def check_text(text)
    # Перевірка, чи текст англійською
    if !is_english?(text)
      puts "Помилка: текст не англійською мовою".red
      return
    end

    # Розділення тексту на слова
    words = text.downcase.split(/[^a-zA-Z]+/).reject(&:empty?)
    
    # Пошук помилок
    errors = []
    words.each_with_index do |word, index|
      unless @aspell.check(word)
        errors << {
          word: word,
          position: index,
          suggestions: @aspell.suggest(word)
        }
      end
    end

    # Виведення результатів
    if errors.empty?
      puts "Орфографія в тексті правильна!".green
    else
      puts "Знайдені помилки:".red
      errors.each do |error|
        puts "Слово: #{error[:word]}".yellow
        puts "Пропозиції: #{error[:suggestions].join(', ')}".blue
        puts
      end
    end
  end

  private

  def is_english?(text)
    # Використовуємо Linguist для перевірки мови
    language = Linguist::Language.find_by_name('English')
    # Проста перевірка на наявність англійських символів
    text.match?(/[a-zA-Z]/) && text.length > 0
  end
end

# Використання

  checker = SpellChecker.new
  
  # Приклад використання
  sample_text = "Ths is a smple text with som misstakes."
  puts "Вхідний текст:"
  puts sample_text
  puts
  checker.check_text(sample_text)
  
  puts "\n" + "="*50 + "\n"
  
  # Ще один приклад
  correct_text = "This is a simple text with no mistakes."
  puts "Вхідний текст:"
  puts correct_text
  puts
  checker.check_text(correct_text)
end

require 'httparty'
require 'json'
require 'logger'

class NovaPoshtaSMS
  include HTTParty
  
  # Base URL for Nova Poshta API
  base_uri 'https://api.novaposhta.ua/v2.0/json/'
  
  # Initialize with API key
  def initialize(api_key)
    @api_key = api_key
    @logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
    @logger.level = Logger::INFO
  end
  
  # Send SMS notification to customer
  def send_sms(phone_number, message, sender = nil)
    # Validate phone number format (Ukrainian format)
    unless valid_phone?(phone_number)
      raise ArgumentError, "Invalid phone number format: #{phone_number}"
    end
    
    # Prepare request data
    request_data = {
      'apiKey' => @api_key,
      'modelName' => 'InternetDocument',
      'calledMethod' => 'sendSMS',
      'methodProperties' => {
        'phone' => phone_number,
        'message' => message,
        'sender' => sender || 'NovaPoshta'
      }
    }
    
    # Make API request
    response = self.class.post(
      '/sendSMS',
      body: request_data.to_json,
      headers: {
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
        'Accept' => 'application/json'
      }
    )
    
    handle_response(response)
  rescue => e
    @logger.error("Failed to send SMS to #{phone_number}: #{e.message}")
    raise
  end
  
  # Send multiple SMS notifications
  def send_sms_batch(recipients)
    results = []
    
    recipients.each do |recipient|
      begin
        result = send_sms(recipient[:phone], recipient[:message], recipient[:sender])
        results << { phone: recipient[:phone], success: true, result: result }
      rescue => e
        results << { phone: recipient[:phone], success: false, error: e.message }
      end
    end
    
    results
  end
  
  # Check SMS delivery status
  def check_sms_status(message_id)
    request_data = {
      'apiKey' => @api_key,
      'modelName' => 'InternetDocument',
      'calledMethod' => 'getSMSStatus',
      'methodProperties' => {
        'messageId' => message_id
      }
    }
    
    response = self.class.post(
      '/getSMSStatus',
      body: request_data.to_json,
      headers: {
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
        'Accept' => 'application/json'
      }
    )
    
    handle_response(response)
  end
  
  private
  
  # Validate Ukrainian phone number format
  def valid_phone?(phone)
    # Remove spaces, dashes, and parentheses
    cleaned_phone = phone.gsub(/[^\d+]/, '')
    
    # Ukrainian phone number patterns:
    # +380XXXXXXXXX (12 digits)
    # 380XXXXXXXXX (11 digits)
    # 0XXXXXXXXX (10 digits)
    # +38 0XX XXX XXX (with spaces)
    
    return false if cleaned_phone.empty?
    
    # Remove leading + if present
    cleaned_phone = cleaned_phone.sub(/^\+/, '') if cleaned_phone.start_with?('+')
    
    # Check if it's a valid Ukrainian number
    case cleaned_phone.length
    when 10
      # 0XXXXXXXXX format
      cleaned_phone.match?(/^0\d{9}$/)
    when 11
      # 380XXXXXXXXX format
      cleaned_phone.match?(/^380\d{9}$/)
    when 12
      # +380XXXXXXXXX format
      cleaned_phone.match?(/^\+380\d{9}$/)
    else
      false
    end
  end
  
  # Handle API response
  def handle_response(response)
    if response.code == 200
      data = JSON.parse(response.body)
      
      if data['success'] == true
        @logger.info("SMS sent successfully: #{data}")
        data
      else
        error_message = data['errors']&.first || data['message'] || 'Unknown error'
        @logger.error("SMS sending failed: #{error_message}")
        raise StandardError, "SMS sending failed: #{error_message}"
      end
    else
      error_message = "HTTP Error: #{response.code} - #{response.body}"
      @logger.error(error_message)
      raise StandardError, error_message
    end
  end
end

require 'kramdown'
require 'pygments'
require 'nokogiri'

class MarkdownToHtml
  def self.convert(markdown_text)
    # Крок 1: Перетворюємо Markdown в HTML
    html = Kramdown::Document.new(markdown_text, input: 'GFM').to_html

    # Крок 2: Підсвічування синтаксису коду
    doc = Nokogiri::HTML::DocumentFragment.parse(html)
    doc.css('pre code').each do |element|
      code = element.text
      language = element['class']&.split('language-')&.last || 'text'

      # Підсвічування синтаксису
      highlighted = Pygments.highlight(code, lexer: language)
      element.replace(highlighted)
    end

    # Крок 3: Видаляємо небезпечні теги (наприклад, script, iframe)
    clean_doc = remove_unsafe_tags(doc)

    clean_doc.to_html
  end

  private

  def self.remove_unsafe_tags(doc)
    doc.css('script, iframe, object, embed').remove
    doc
  end
end
```

```python

```

MD

### 1. **Gemfile**

```ruby
require 'active_support'
require 'active_support/core_ext/string'

class SlugGenerator
  def self.generate(title)
    # Видаляємо HTML-теги (якщо є)
    title = Nokogiri::HTML(title).text if title.is_a?(String)

    # Перетворюємо на нижній регістр
    title = title.downcase

    # Видаляємо всі символи, крім букв, цифр і пробілів
    title = title.gsub(/[^a-z0-9\s]/, '')

    # Замінюємо більше одного пробілу на один дефіс
    title = title.squeeze(' ').tr(' ', '-')

    # Видаляємо початкові та кінцеві дефіси
    title = title.gsub(/^-+|-+$/, '')

    # Якщо порожній, повертаємо стандартний slug
    title.empty? ? 'untitled' : title
  end
end

# Приклад використання
puts SlugGenerator.generate("Привіт, світ!") # => "privit-svit"
puts SlugGenerator.generate("Café & Restaurant") # => "cafe-restaurant"
puts SlugGenerator.generate("  Моя стаття з діакритикою  ") # => "moia-statia-z-dyakrytykoiu"
puts SlugGenerator.generate("HTML & CSS: The Basics") # => "html-css-the-basics"
```

### Пояснення:

- **`active_support`** — використовується для методів типу `downcase`, `squeeze`, `tr`, що спрощують обробку рядків.
- **`Nokogiri`** — потрібен для обробки HTML-тегів, якщо заголовок може містити їх.
- **`gsub(/[^a-z0-9\s]/, '')`** — видаляє всі символи, крім букв, цифр і пробілів.
- **`squeeze(' ')`** — зменшує кількість послідовних пробілів до одного.
- **`tr(' ', '-')`** — замінює пробіли на дефіси.
- **`gsub(/^-+|-+$/, '')`** — видаляє початкові та кінцеві дефіси.
- Якщо заголовок порожній або містить лише недопустимі символи, повертається `'untitled'`.

require 'deep-l'
require 'redis'
require 'json'

class ProductTranslator
  def initialize(api_key:, redis_url: 'redis://localhost:6379')
    @deepl = DeepL::Client.new(api_key)
    @redis = Redis.new(url: redis_url)
  end

  def translate_description(description, target_lang = 'UK')
    # Генеруємо унікальний ключ для кешу на основі опису та мови
    cache_key = "translation:#{target_lang}:#{description.hash}"

    # Спробуємо отримати переклад із кешу
    cached = @redis.get(cache_key)
    return JSON.parse(cached) if cached

    # Якщо немає в кеші — робимо запит до DeepL
    begin
      result = @deepl.translate(description, target_lang: target_lang)
      translated = result.text

      # Зберігаємо в кеш (наприклад, на 1 день)
      @redis.setex(cache_key, 86400, JSON.generate(translated))

      translated
    rescue => e
      puts "Помилка перекладу: #{e.message}"
      description # повертаємо оригінал у разі помилки
    end
  end
end
```

require 'pycall/import'
include PyCall::Import

class SentimentClassifier
  def classify(text)
    blob = tb::TextBlob[text]
    polarity = blob.sentiment.polarity

    case polarity
    when 0.1..1.0
      :positive
    when -1.0..-0.1
      :negative
    else
      :neutral
    end
  end
end

  "I hate this item. It's terrible.",
  "It's okay, nothing special."

  puts "#{review} => #{classifier.classify(review)}"
end

### 3. **Пояснення**

- `textblob` – це Python-пакет для обробки тексту, який включає аналіз тональності.
- `pycall` дозволяє викликати Python-код з Ruby.
- `TextBlob` аналізує текст і повертає `polarity` (від -1 до 1), де:
  - `polarity > 0` – позитивна тональність
  - `polarity < 0` – негативна
  - `polarity ≈ 0` – нейтральна

# lib/translation_service.rb
require 'deep-ruby'
require 'redis'
require 'json'
require 'logger'
require 'dotenv/load'

class TranslationService
  # Initialize with DeepL API credentials and Redis connection
  def initialize(api_key:, redis_url: nil, logger: nil)
    @api_key = api_key
    @client = DeepRuby::Client.new(api_key)
    
    # Configure Redis connection
    redis_url ||= ENV['REDIS_URL'] || 'redis://localhost:6379/0'
    @redis = Redis.new(url: redis_url)
    
    # Setup logger
    @logger = logger || Logger.new(STDOUT)
    @logger.level = Logger::INFO
  end

  # Translate a single product description
  def translate_description(description, target_lang, source_lang: 'EN')
    # Create cache key
    cache_key = cache_key_for(description, target_lang, source_lang)
    
    # Try to get from cache first
    cached_translation = @redis.get(cache_key)
    if cached_translation
      @logger.info("Cache hit for description: #{description[0..50]}...")
      return JSON.parse(cached_translation)
    end
    
    # If not cached, translate via DeepL
    @logger.info("Translating description: #{description[0..50]}...")
    
    begin
      translation = @client.translate(
        text: description,
        target_lang: target_lang,
        source_lang: source_lang
      )
      
      # Cache the result
      @redis.setex(cache_key, 24 * 60 * 60, translation.to_json) # Cache for 24 hours
      @logger.info("Cached translation for #{cache_key}")
      
      translation
    rescue StandardError => e
      @logger.error("Translation failed: #{e.message}")
      raise
    end
  end

  # Translate multiple descriptions efficiently (batch processing)
  def translate_descriptions(descriptions, target_lang, source_lang: 'EN')
    translations = {}
    
    # First, check which descriptions are already cached
    uncached_descriptions = []
    
    descriptions.each do |desc|
      cache_key = cache_key_for(desc, target_lang, source_lang)
      cached_translation = @redis.get(cache_key)
      
      if cached_translation
        translations[desc] = JSON.parse(cached_translation)
        @logger.info("Cache hit for description: #{desc[0..30]}...")
      else
        uncached_descriptions << desc
      end
    end
    
    # Translate uncached descriptions
    if !uncached_descriptions.empty?
      @logger.info("Translating #{uncached_descriptions.length} uncached descriptions...")
      
      begin
        batch_result = @client.translate_batch(
          texts: uncached_descriptions,
          target_lang: target_lang,
          source_lang: source_lang
        )
        
        # Cache each translation and store in result
        uncached_descriptions.each_with_index do |desc, index|
          translation = batch_result[index]
          
          # Cache translation
          cache_key = cache_key_for(desc, target_lang, source_lang)
          @redis.setex(cache_key, 24 * 60 * 60, translation.to_json)
          
          translations[desc] = translation
        end
        
        @logger.info("Translated and cached batch of #{uncached_descriptions.length} descriptions")
      rescue StandardError => e
        @logger.error("Batch translation failed: #{e.message}")
        raise
      end
    else
      @logger.info("All descriptions found in cache")
    end
    
    translations
  end

  # Clear cache for a specific description
  def clear_cache(description, target_lang, source_lang: 'EN')
    cache_key = cache_key_for(description, target_lang, source_lang)
    @redis.del(cache_key)
    @logger.info("Cleared cache for: #{description[0..30]}...")
  end

  # Clear entire cache
  def clear_all_cache
    @redis.flushdb
    @logger.info("Cleared entire translation cache")
  end

  private

  # Generate cache key for a description
  def cache_key_for(description, target_lang, source_lang)
    # Create a unique key based on description content, target language, and source language
    require 'digest'
    desc_hash = Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(description)
    "translation:#{desc_hash}:#{source_lang}:#{target_lang}"
  end
end

require 'pdf/reader'
require 'csv'
require 'json'
require 'tmpdir'

class PDFExtractor
  def initialize(pdf_path)
    @pdf_path = pdf_path
    @reader = PDF::Reader.new(pdf_path)
  end

  def extract_text
    text = ""
    @reader.pages.each_with_index do |page, index|
      text += "Page #{index + 1}:\n"
      text += page.text
      text += "\n\n"
    end
    text
  end

  def extract_tables
    tables = []
    @reader.pages.each_with_index do |page, page_index|
      # Simple table detection - look for structured content with consistent spacing
      page_text = page.text
      lines = page_text.split("\n")
      
      # Look for potential tables (lines with consistent alignment)
      potential_tables = detect_tables_in_lines(lines)
      
      if !potential_tables.empty?
        tables << {
          page: page_index + 1,
          tables: potential_tables
        }
      end
    end
    
    tables
  end

  private

  def detect_tables_in_lines(lines)
    tables = []
    current_table = []
    table_start = nil
    
    lines.each_with_index do |line, index|
      # Skip empty lines
      next if line.strip.empty?
      
      # Simple table detection: look for lines with consistent number of columns
      # and potential alignment
      if is_potential_table_line?(line) && current_table.empty?
        table_start = index
        current_table << line
      elsif !current_table.empty? && is_potential_table_line?(line)
        current_table << line
      elsif !current_table.empty?
        # End of table
        if current_table.length > 1
          tables << parse_table_lines(current_table)
        end
        current_table = []
      end
    end
    
    # Handle last table if it exists
    if !current_table.empty? && current_table.length > 1
      tables << parse_table_lines(current_table)
    end
    
    tables
  end

  def is_potential_table_line?(line)
    # Check if line has consistent spacing (indicative of table structure)
    # This is a simple heuristic - more sophisticated approaches would be needed
    # for production use
    return false if line.length < 10
    
    # Look for consistent use of spaces or other separators
    return true if line.count(' ') > 3 && line.count('|') > 0
    return true if line.count("\t") > 0
    return true if line.length > 50 && line.split(/\s{2,}/).length > 2
    false
  end

  def parse_table_lines(lines)
    # Simple table parsing - split by common delimiters
    table_data = []
    
    lines.each do |line|
      # Try different delimiters
      if line.include?('|')
        # Pipe-delimited table
        cells = line.split('|').map(&:strip).reject(&:empty?)
      elsif line.include?("\t")
        # Tab-delimited table
        cells = line.split("\t").map(&:strip).reject(&:empty?)
      else
        # Space-delimited table
        cells = line.split(/\s{2,}/).reject(&:empty?)
      end
      
      table_data << cells if cells.any?
    end
    
    table_data
  end
end

class PDFExtractorApp
  def self.extract_from_file(file_path)
    extractor = PDFExtractor.new(file_path)
    
    {
      text: extractor.extract_text,
      tables: extractor.extract_tables
    }
  end
  
  def self.extract_from_uploaded_file(uploaded_file)
    # Create a temporary file to work with
    temp_file = Tempfile.new(['pdf', '.pdf'])
    temp_file.binmode
    temp_file.write(uploaded_file.read)
    temp_file.close
    
    begin
      result = extract_from_file(temp_file.path)
      result[:file_name] = uploaded_file.original_filename
      result
    ensure
      temp_file.unlink
    end
  end
end

# sentiment_classifier.rb
require 'sentimental'
require 'csv'
require 'json'
require 'nokogiri'
require 'httparty'

class SentimentClassifier
  def initialize
    @sentiment_analyzer = Sentimental.new
    @sentiment_analyzer.load_defaults
  end

  # Classify a single review
  def classify_review(review_text)
    return 'neutral' if review_text.nil? || review_text.strip.empty?
    
    score = @sentiment_analyzer.score(review_text)
    
    case score
    when -0.1..0.1
      'neutral'
    when -1.0..-0.1
      'negative'
    else
      'positive'
    end
  end

  # Classify multiple reviews
  def classify_reviews(review_texts)
    review_texts.map { |text| classify_review(text) }
  end

  # Process CSV file with reviews
  def process_csv_file(file_path, text_column = 'review')
    reviews = []
    CSV.foreach(file_path, headers: true) do |row|
      reviews << row[text_column].to_s
    end
    classify_reviews(reviews)
  end

  # Process JSON file with reviews
  def process_json_file(file_path, text_field = 'review')
    data = JSON.parse(File.read(file_path))
    reviews = data.map { |item| item[text_field].to_s }
    classify_reviews(reviews)
  end

  # Get detailed sentiment analysis
  def analyze_sentiment_detailed(review_text)
    return nil if review_text.nil? || review_text.strip.empty?
    
    sentiment = @sentiment_analyzer.sentiment(review_text)
    score = @sentiment_analyzer.score(review_text)
    confidence = @sentiment_analyzer.confidence(review_text)
    
    {
      text: review_text,
      sentiment: sentiment,
      score: score,
      confidence: confidence
    }
  end

  # Batch process reviews with detailed results
  def analyze_reviews_detailed(review_texts)
    review_texts.map do |text|
      analyze_sentiment_detailed(text)
    end
  end

  # Generate summary statistics
  def generate_summary(sentiment_results)
    total = sentiment_results.length
    return { total: 0, positive: 0, negative: 0, neutral: 0 } if total == 0
    
    counts = sentiment_results.group_by { |r| r }.transform_values(&:count)
    
    {
      total: total,
      positive: counts['positive'] || 0,
      negative: counts['negative'] || 0,
      neutral: counts['neutral'] || 0
    }
  end

  # Sample reviews for testing
  def sample_reviews
    [
      "This product is amazing! I love it so much.",
      "Terrible quality, waste of money.",
      "It's okay, nothing special but does the job.",
      "Outstanding performance and great value for money!",
      "Not worth the price, very disappointed.",
      "Average product, meets expectations.",
      "Absolutely fantastic! Highly recommended!",
      "Poor build quality, broke after one week.",
      "It's a decent product for the price.",
      "I'm extremely happy with my purchase."
    ]
  end

  # Print classification results
  def print_results(reviews, results)
    puts "Sentiment Analysis Results:"
    puts "=" * 50
    
    reviews.each_with_index do |review, index|
      puts "Review #{index + 1}:"
      puts "Text: #{review}"
      puts "Sentiment: #{results[index]}"
      puts "-" * 30
    end
    
    summary = generate_summary(results)
    puts "Summary:"
    puts "Total reviews: #{summary[:total]}"
    puts "Positive: #{summary[:positive]}"
    puts "Negative: #{summary[:negative]}"
    puts "Neutral: #{summary[:neutral]}"
  end
end

require 'badwords'
require 'sanitize'

class CommentFilter
  def initialize(bad_words_file = nil)
    @bad_words = load_bad_words(bad_words_file)
  end

  def filter_comment(comment)
    filtered_comment = comment.dup

    @bad_words.each do |word|
      # Замінюємо заборонене слово на ***
      filtered_comment = filtered_comment.gsub(/\b#{Regexp.escape(word)}\b/i, '***')
    end

    filtered_comment
  end

  private

  def load_bad_words(file = nil)
    if file && File.exist?(file)
      File.readlines(file).map(&:strip).reject(&:empty?)
    else
      # Вбудований список заборонених слів
      %w[badword1 badword2 damn hell]
    end
  end
end

    to_time = to_time.to_time if to_time.respond_to?(:to_time)

  rescue
    # Fallback if ActiveSupport methods fail
    time_diff = (to_time - from_time).to_i
    case time_diff
    when 0..59
      "less than a minute ago"
    when 60..3599
      "#{(time_diff / 60).floor} minutes ago"
    when 3600..86399
      "#{(time_diff / 3600).floor} hours ago"
    when 86400..2591999
      "#{(time_diff / 86400).floor} days ago"
    when 2592000..31535999
      "#{(time_diff / 2592000).floor} months ago"

# Функція для порівняння з використанням відстані Левенштейна
def levenshtein_similarity(str1, str2)
  # Використовуємо бібліотеку fuzzy_match для обчислення відстані Левенштейна
  FuzzyMatch::Levenshtein.distance(str1.downcase, str2.downcase)
end

# Функція для порівняння з використанням Джаро-Вінклера

  JaroWinkler::Distance.jaro_winkler_similarity(str1.downcase, str2.downcase)

def find_similar_companies(companies, threshold_lev = 3, threshold_jw = 0.8)
  similar_pairs = []

  companies.each_with_index do |company1, i|
    companies.each_with_index do |company2, j|
      next if i >= j # Щоб не порівнювати одну і ту ж пару двічі

      # Відстань Левенштейна
      lev_distance = levenshtein_similarity(company1, company2)

      # Джаро-Вінклера
      jw_similarity = jaro_winkler_similarity(company1, company2)

      if lev_distance <= threshold_lev || jw_similarity >= threshold_jw
        similar_pairs << {
          company1: company1,
          company2: company2,
          levenshtein: lev_distance,
          jaro_winkler: jw_similarity
        }
      end
    end
  end

  similar_pairs
end

require 'email_address'
require 'addressable/uri'
require 'uri'

class USAddressNormalizer
  # Валідний регулярний вираз для поштової адреси США
  EMAIL_REGEX = /\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z|a-z]{2,}\b/.freeze

  def self.normalize(text)
    # Знаходимо всі потенційні email-адреси
    emails = text.scan(EMAIL_REGEX)

    # Нормалізуємо кожну адресу
    normalized_emails = emails.map do |email|
      normalize_email(email)
    end

    normalized_emails.uniq
  end

  private

  def self.normalize_email(email)
    # Перетворюємо на нижній регістр
    email = email.downcase

    # Валідація адреси
    addr = EmailAddress.parse(email)
    return nil unless addr.valid?

    # Нормалізуємо використовуючи Addressable
    uri = Addressable::URI.parse("mailto:#{email}")
    uri.to_s.gsub('mailto:', '')
  end
end

- **`EmailAddress.parse`** — перевіряє, чи є адреса валідною.
- **`Addressable::URI.parse`** — для нормалізації URL-подобних адрес (може бути корисно, якщо використовується `mailto:` або подібні формати).

# Fuzzy Matching of Company Names

Here's a complete Ruby solution for finding fuzzy matches between company names using Levenshtein and Jaro-Winkler distances.

## Gemfile
```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'levenshtein'
gem 'jaro_winkler'
gem 'csv'
```

## Implementation

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'levenshtein'
require 'jaro_winkler'
require 'csv'
require 'json'

class CompanyMatcher
  # Initialize with company data
  def initialize(companies = [])
    @companies = companies
  end

  # Add a company to the dataset
  def add_company(name)
    @companies << name
  end

  # Calculate Levenshtein distance between two strings
  def levenshtein_distance(str1, str2)
    Levenshtein.distance(str1.downcase, str2.downcase)
  end

  # Calculate Jaro-Winkler similarity between two strings
  def jaro_winkler_similarity(str1, str2)
    JaroWinkler.distance(str1.downcase, str2.downcase)
  end

  # Find fuzzy matches for a given company name
  def find_matches(company_name, threshold = 0.8, max_matches = 10)
    matches = []

    @companies.each do |company|
      next if company.nil? || company.strip.empty?
      next if company == company_name

      lev_distance = levenshtein_distance(company_name, company)
      jaro_similarity = jaro_winkler_similarity(company_name, company)

      # Calculate normalized Levenshtein score (0-1)
      max_length = [company_name.length, company.length].max
      lev_score = max_length.zero? ? 1.0 : 1.0 - (lev_distance.to_f / max_length)

      # Only include matches that meet the threshold
      if jaro_similarity >= threshold || lev_score >= threshold
        matches << {
          company: company,
          levenshtein_distance: lev_distance,
          levenshtein_score: lev_score,
          jaro_winkler_similarity: jaro_similarity
        }
      end

```ruby
# lib/number_to_words.rb
class NumberToWords
  ONES = %w[zero one two three four five six seven eight nine
            ten eleven twelve thirteen fourteen fifteen sixteen
            seventeen eighteen nineteen].freeze

  TENS = %w[zero ten twenty thirty forty fifty sixty seventy eighty ninety].freeze

  SCALES = %w[thousand million billion trillion].freeze

  def self.convert(number)
    return 'zero' if number == 0
    return 'negative ' + convert(-number) if number < 0

    result = []
    scale_index = 0

    while number > 0
      chunk = number % 1000
      if chunk != 0
        chunk_words = convert_chunk(chunk)
        chunk_words += " #{SCALES[scale_index]}" if scale_index > 0
        result.unshift(chunk_words)
      end
      number /= 1000
      scale_index += 1
    end

    result.join(' ')
  end

  private_class_method def self.convert_chunk(number)
    result = []

    # Handle hundreds place
    if number >= 100
      result << ONES[number / 100]
      result << 'hundred'
      number %= 100
    end

    # Handle tens and ones
    if number >= 20
      tens_digit = number / 10
      ones_digit = number % 10
      result << TENS[tens_digit]
      result << ONES[ones_digit] if ones_digit > 0
    elsif number > 0
      result << ONES[number]
    end

    result.join(' ')
  end
end

require 'pg'
require 'openai'
require 'pgvector'
require 'dotenv/load'

class DocumentSearcher
  def initialize
    # Initialize database connection
    @db = PG.connect(
      dbname: ENV['DB_NAME'] || 'documents',
      user: ENV['DB_USER'] || 'postgres',
      password: ENV['DB_PASSWORD'] || 'password',
      host: ENV['DB_HOST'] || 'localhost',
      port: ENV['DB_PORT'] || 5432
    )
    
    # Initialize OpenAI client
    OpenAI.configure do |config|
      config.access_token = ENV['OPENAI_API_KEY']
    end
    
    @client = OpenAI::Client.new
    
    setup_database
  end

  def setup_database
    # Create the documents table with vector column
    @db.exec(<<-SQL)
      CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;
    SQL

    @db.exec(<<-SQL)
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS documents (
        id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
        title TEXT,
        content TEXT,
        embedding VECTOR(1536)
      );
    SQL

    # Create index for faster similarity search
    @db.exec(<<-SQL)
      CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS documents_embedding_idx ON documents USING ivfflat (embedding vector_cosine_ops);
    SQL
  end

  def embed_text(text)
    # Generate embedding using OpenAI's text-embedding-ada-002 model
    response = @client.embeddings(
      model: "text-embedding-ada-002",
      input: text
    )
    
    # Extract vector from response
    embedding = response['data'][0]['embedding']
    embedding.join(',')
  end

  def add_document(title, content)
    # Generate embedding for the content
    embedding = embed_text(content)
    
    # Insert document into database
    @db.exec_params(<<-SQL, [title, content, embedding])
      INSERT INTO documents (title, content, embedding) 
      VALUES ($1, $2, $3::vector)
    SQL
    
    puts "Added document: #{title}"
  end

  def search_documents(query, limit: 5)
    # Generate embedding for the query
    query_embedding = embed_text(query)
    
    # Search for similar documents using cosine similarity
    results = @db.exec_params(<<-SQL, [query_embedding, limit])
      SELECT title, content, 1 - (embedding <=> $1::vector) AS similarity
      FROM documents
      ORDER BY embedding <=> $1::vector
      LIMIT $2
    SQL
    
    # Format results
    results.map do |row|
      {
        title: row['title'],
        content: row['content'],
        similarity: row['similarity'].to_f
      }
    end
  end

  def close
    @db.close
  end
end

# Example usage

class OpenAIEmbedding
  include HTTParty

  base_uri 'https://api.openai.com/v1'

  def initialize(api_key)
    @headers = {
      'Authorization' => "Bearer #{api_key}",
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
    }
  end

  def create_embedding(text)
    response = self.class.post(
      '/embeddings',
      headers: @headers,
      body: {
        model: 'text-embedding-ada-002',
        input: text
      }.to_json
    )

    if response.success?
      response['data'][0]['embedding']
    else
      raise "OpenAI API error: #{response.body}"
    end
  end
end

# Клас для роботи з PostgreSQL + pgvector
class VectorDB
  def initialize
    @conn = PG.connect(
      host: DB_HOST,
      port: DB_PORT,
      dbname: DB_NAME,
      user: DB_USER,
      password: DB_PASS

    @conn.exec(<<-SQL)
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS documents (
        id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
        content TEXT NOT NULL,
        embedding vector(1536)
      );
    SQL
  end

  def insert_document(content, embedding)
    @conn.exec_params(
      'INSERT INTO documents (content, embedding) VALUES ($1, $2)',
      [content, embedding]
    )
  end

  def search_similar(query_embedding, limit: 5)
    result = @conn.exec_params(
      'SELECT content, 1 - (embedding <=> $1) AS similarity FROM documents ORDER BY similarity DESC LIMIT $2',
      [query_embedding, limit]
    )
    result.map { |row| { content: row['content'], similarity: row['similarity'].to_f } }
  end
end

require 'stanford-core-nlp'

class NewsEntityExtractor
  def initialize
    # Initialize Stanford CoreNLP
    @corenlp = StanfordCoreNLP::Pipeline.new(
      :annotators => 'tokenize,ssplit,pos,lemma,ner',
      :corenlp => {
        :properties => {
          'annotators' => 'tokenize,ssplit,pos,lemma,ner',
          'ner.useSUTime' => 'false'
        }
      }
    )
  end

  # Extract entities from raw text
  def extract_entities(text)
    return {} if text.nil? || text.strip.empty?
    
    # Process the text with CoreNLP
    annotations = @corenlp.annotate(text)
    
    # Extract named entities
    entities = {
      people: Set.new,
      organizations: Set.new,
      locations: Set.new
    }
    
    # Iterate through sentences and tokens
    annotations.get(:sentences).each do |sentence|
      sentence.get(:tokens).each do |token|
        word = token.get(:word)
        ner = token.get(:ner)
        
        case ner
        when 'PERSON'
          entities[:people] << word
        when 'ORGANIZATION'
          entities[:organizations] << word
        when 'LOCATION'
          entities[:locations] << word
        end
      end
    end
    
    # Convert sets to arrays and return
    {
      people: entities[:people].to_a,
      organizations: entities[:organizations].to_a,
      locations: entities[:locations].to_a
    }
  end

  # Extract entities from HTML content (like news articles)
  def extract_from_html(html_content)
    return {} if html_content.nil? || html_content.strip.empty?
    
    # Parse HTML with Nokogiri
    doc = Nokogiri::HTML(html_content)
    
    # Extract text from body and headings
    text_parts = []
    text_parts << doc.css('body').text
    doc.css('h1, h2, h3').each { |h| text_parts << h.text }
    
    # Join all text parts
    full_text = text_parts.join(' ')
    
    extract_entities(full_text)
  end

  # Extract entities from a file path
  def extract_from_file(file_path)
    return {} unless File.exist?(file_path)
    
    content = File.read(file_path)
    extract_from_html(content)
  end

  # Extract entities from multiple articles
  def extract_from_articles(articles)
    results = {}
    
    articles.each_with_index do |article, index|
      if article.is_a?(String)
        # Handle raw text
        results["article_#{index}"] = extract_entities(article)
      elsif article.is_a?(Hash) && article.key?(:content)
        # Handle hash with content key
        results["article_#{index}"] = extract_from_html(article[:content])
      end
    end

      organizations: [],
      locations: []

        when 'ORGANIZATION'
          entities[:organizations] << {
            name: word,
            part_of_speech: pos,
            sentence: sentence.get(:text)
          }
        when 'LOCATION'
          entities[:locations] << {
            name: word,
            part_of_speech: pos,
            sentence: sentence.get(:text)
          }
        end
      end
    end
    
    entities
  end

# tf_idf_similar_documents.rb
require 'tf-idf'
require 'matrix'
require 'csv'
require 'json'

class DocumentSimilarity
  def initialize
    @documents = []
    @term_frequency = {}
    @idf_values = {}
    @tf_idf_matrix = nil
    @document_vectors = []
  end

  def add_document(id, content)
    @documents << { id: id, content: content }
  end

  def compute_tf_idf
    # Preprocess documents and compute term frequencies
    documents_with_terms = @documents.map do |doc|
      terms = preprocess_text(doc[:content])
      { id: doc[:id], terms: terms }
    end

    # Calculate term frequencies
    all_terms = Set.new(documents_with_terms.flat_map { |d| d[:terms] })
    
    documents_with_terms.each do |doc|
      term_freq = Hash.new(0)
      doc[:terms].each { |term| term_freq[term] += 1 }
      @term_frequency[doc[:id]] = term_freq
    end

    # Calculate IDF values
    total_docs = documents_with_terms.length
    all_terms.each do |term|
      doc_count = documents_with_terms.count { |doc| doc[:terms].include?(term) }
      @idf_values[term] = Math.log(total_docs.to_f / doc_count)
    end

    # Compute TF-IDF vectors
    @document_vectors = documents_with_terms.map do |doc|
      vector = {}
      @term_frequency[doc[:id]].each do |term, freq|
        vector[term] = freq * @idf_values[term]
      end
      vector
    end
  end

  def calculate_cosine_similarity(v1, v2)
    # Convert vectors to sparse vectors for easier computation
    all_terms = (v1.keys + v2.keys).uniq
    
    # Create vectors with all terms
    vector1 = all_terms.map { |term| v1[term] || 0 }
    vector2 = all_terms.map { |term| v2[term] || 0 }
    
    # Calculate dot product
    dot_product = vector1.zip(vector2).map(&:product).sum
    
    # Calculate magnitudes
    magnitude1 = Math.sqrt(vector1.map { |x| x * x }.sum)
    magnitude2 = Math.sqrt(vector2.map { |x| x * x }.sum)
    
    # Avoid division by zero
    return 0.0 if magnitude1 == 0 || magnitude2 == 0
    
    dot_product / (magnitude1 * magnitude2)
  end

  def find_similar_documents(document_id, top_n = 5)
    return [] if @document_vectors.empty?
    
    target_vector = @document_vectors[@documents.index { |d| d[:id] == document_id }]
    return [] unless target_vector
    
    similarities = []
    
    @documents.each_with_index do |doc, index|
      next if doc[:id] == document_id
      
      other_vector = @document_vectors[index]
      similarity = calculate_cosine_similarity(target_vector, other_vector)
      
      similarities << { 
        document_id: doc[:id], 
        similarity: similarity 
      }
    end
    
    similarities.sort_by { |s| -s[:similarity] }.first(top_n)
  end

  def get_keywords(document_id, top_n = 10)
    return [] if @document_vectors.empty?
    
    vector = @document_vectors[@documents.index { |d| d[:id] == document_id }]
    return [] unless vector
    
    # Sort by TF-IDF score
    keywords = vector.sort_by { |term, score| -score }.first(top_n)
    keywords.map { |term, score| { term: term, tf_idf_score: score } }
  end

  private

  def preprocess_text(text)
    # Simple text preprocessing
    text.downcase
        .gsub(/[^\w\s]/, '')  # Remove punctuation
        .split                   # Split into words
        .reject { |word| word.length < 3 || word.length > 20 }  # Filter short/long words
        .reject { |word| %w[the a an and or but in on at to for of with by].include?(word) }  # Filter common stopwords
  end
end

# readability_calculator.rb
require 'nokogiri'
require 'lingua'
require 'text-statistics'

class ReadabilityCalculator
  def initialize
    @sentence_endings = %w[. ! ?]
  end

  # Main method to calculate Flesch reading ease
  def calculate_flesch_ease(text)
    return 0 if text.nil? || text.strip.empty?
    
    # Preprocess text
    clean_text = preprocess_text(text)
    
    # Calculate statistics
    syllable_count = count_syllables(clean_text)
    sentence_count = count_sentences(clean_text)
    word_count = count_words(clean_text)
    
    # Handle edge cases
    return 100 if sentence_count == 0 || word_count == 0
    
    # Calculate Flesch reading ease
    # Formula: 206.835 - (1.015 * (words/sentences)) - (84.6 * (syllables/words))
    flesch_ease = 206.835 - (1.015 * (word_count.to_f / sentence_count)) - (84.6 * (syllable_count.to_f / word_count))
    
    # Clamp between 0 and 100
    [0, [100, flesch_ease].min].max
  end

  # Alternative method using text-statistics gem
  def calculate_flesch_ease_gem(text)
    return 0 if text.nil? || text.strip.empty?
    
    stats = TextStatistics.new(text)
    stats.flesch_reading_ease
  end

  # Get detailed readability analysis
  def analyze_readability(text)
    return nil if text.nil? || text.strip.empty?
    
    clean_text = preprocess_text(text)
    syllable_count = count_syllables(clean_text)
    sentence_count = count_sentences(clean_text)
    word_count = count_words(clean_text)
    
    flesch_ease = calculate_flesch_ease(text)
    
    {
      flesch_ease: flesch_ease.round(2),
      syllable_count: syllable_count,
      sentence_count: sentence_count,
      word_count: word_count,
      words_per_sentence: sentence_count > 0 ? (word_count.to_f / sentence_count).round(2) : 0,
      syllables_per_word: word_count > 0 ? (syllable_count.to_f / word_count).round(2) : 0,
      readability_level: get_readability_level(flesch_ease)
    }
  end

  # Get human-readable readability level
  def get_readability_level(score)

    when 90..100
      "Very Easy"
    when 80..89
      "Easy"
    when 70..79
      "Fairly Easy"
    when 60..69
      "Standard"
    when 50..59

    when 30..49
      "Difficult"
    when 0..29
      "Very Difficult"
    else
      "Unknown"

    text.gsub(/\s+/, ' ').strip
  end

  def count_sentences(text)
    # Count sentence endings
    sentence_count = text.chars.count { |char| @sentence_endings.include?(char) }
    
    # If no sentence endings found or text is very short, assume 1 sentence
    sentence_count = 1 if sentence_count == 0 && text.length > 0
    
    sentence_count
  end

  def count_words(text)
    # Split by whitespace and filter out empty strings
    words = text.split(/\s+/).reject(&:empty?)
    words.length
  end

  def count_syllables(text)

    # For this implementation, we'll use a basic heuristic

    total_syllables = 0
    words.each do |word|
      # Remove punctuation and convert to lowercase

      next if clean_word.empty?
      
      # Count vowel groups

      total_syllables += syllables
    end
    
    total_syllables
  end

  def count_syllables_in_word(word)

    # This is an approximation and works for most cases

    word = word.gsub(/[aeiouy]+/, 'a') # Replace vowel groups with 'a'
    count = word.chars.count { |char| char == 'a' }
    count = [1, count].max # At least 1 syllable

# lib/ticket_summarizer.rb
require 'anthropic'
require 'json'
require 'logger'
require 'dotenv/load'

class TicketSummarizer
  def initialize(api_key = ENV['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'])
    @client = Anthropic::Client.new(api_key: api_key)
    @logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
    @logger.level = Logger::INFO
  end

  def summarize_ticket(ticket_content, max_length = 200)
    # Validate input
    raise ArgumentError, "Ticket content cannot be empty" if ticket_content.nil? || ticket_content.strip.empty?
    
    # Truncate if needed
    truncated_content = truncate_content(ticket_content, max_length)
    
    # Create prompt for Claude
    prompt = build_prompt(truncated_content)
    
    # Call Claude API
    response = call_claude_api(prompt)
    
    # Process response
    process_response(response)
  end

  private

  def truncate_content(content, max_length)
    return content if content.length <= max_length
    
    # Truncate and add ellipsis
    content[0..max_length-4] + "..."
  end

  def build_prompt(content)
    <<~PROMPT
      Please provide a concise summary of the following support ticket. 
      The summary should be 1-2 sentences and capture the key issue, 
      the customer's main concern, and any important technical details.
      
      Ticket content:
      #{content}
      
      Summary:
    PROMPT
  end

  def call_claude_api(prompt)
    @logger.info("Calling Claude API with prompt of #{prompt.length} characters")
    
    response = @client.completions.create(
      model: "claude-3-haiku-20240307",
      prompt: prompt,
      max_tokens: 300,
      temperature: 0.3
    )
    
    @logger.info("Received response from Claude API")
    response
  end

  def process_response(response)
    summary = response.completion.strip
    
    # Validate response
    if summary.empty?
      @logger.warn("Received empty summary from Claude")
      return "No summary available"
    end
    
    summary
  end
end

  end

  def process_multiple_tickets(tickets)

    tickets.each_with_index do |ticket, index|
      begin
        summary = @summarizer.summarize_ticket(ticket[:content], ticket[:max_length] || 200)
        results << {
          id: ticket[:id],
          title: ticket[:title],
          summary: summary,
          original_length: ticket[:content].length
        }

          id: ticket[:id],
          title: ticket[:title],
          summary: "Error: #{e.message}",
          original_length: ticket[:content].length
        }
      end
    end
    
    results
  end

source 'https://rubygems.org'
