```ruby
# lib/profanity_filter.rb
require 'redact'

class ProfanityFilter
  PROFANITY_LIST = [
    'shit', 'shitty', 'damn', 'fuck', 'fucking', 'pussy', 'bitch', 'ass',
    'asshole', 'dick', 'dickhead', 'douche', 'douchebag', 'cunt', 'cock',
    'cockhead', 'cocksucker', 'motherfucker', 'motherfucking', 'bullshit',
    'bullshitter', 'bullshitting', 'shithead', 'shitlist', 'shitty',
    'piss', 'pissed', 'pissed off', 'piss off', 'pissed off', 'pissed-off'
  ].freeze

  def initialize(replacement: '****')
    @replacement = replacement
  end

  def filter(text)
    words = text.split
    filtered_words = words.map do |word|
      # Check each word and its variations (plural, past tense, etc.)
      PROFANITY_LIST.any? { |profanity| word.downcase.include?(profanity) } ? @replacement : word
    end
    filtered_words.join(' ')
  end

  # Alternative using the Redact gem (more sophisticated)
  def self.filter_with_redact(text, replacement: '****')
    Redact::Filter.new(
      text: text,
      replacements: [replacement],
      dictionaries: {
        'en' => { words: PROFANITY_LIST }
      }
    ).call
  end
end
```

  let(:text) { "That's some pretty shitty work, you asshole!" }

  it 'filters profanity' do
    expect(filter.filter(text)).to eq("That's some pretty ** work, you **!")
  end

  it 'works with the Redact gem' do
    expect(ProfanityFilter.filter_with_redact(text, replacement: '**')).to eq("That's some pretty ** work, you **!")

```ruby
# lib/ticket_summarizer.rb
require 'anthropic'
require 'dotenv'
require 'json'

class TicketSummarizer
  def initialize
    Dotenv.load # Load environment variables from .env file
    @anthropic = Anthropic::Client.new(api_key: ENV['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'])
  end

  def summarize_ticket(ticket_text, max_tokens = 200, temperature = 0.5)
    prompt = build_prompt(ticket_text, max_tokens, temperature)
    response = @anthropic.completions(params: prompt)

    if response.success?
      { success: true, summary: response.body.completion }
    else
      { success: false, error: response.body.error }
    end
  rescue StandardError => e
    { success: false, error: e.message }
  end

  private

  def build_prompt(ticket_text, max_tokens, temperature)
    {
      model: "claude-2.1",
      max_tokens_to_sample: max_tokens,
      temperature: temperature,
      prompt: <<~PROMPT
        You are an expert support ticket summarizer. Please summarize the following support ticket concisely:

        #{ticket_text}

        Summary (keep it to one or two sentences):
      PROMPT
    }
  end
end
```

# docx_converter.rb
require 'fileutils'
require 'optparse'
require 'docx'
require 'nokogiri'

class DocxConverter
  def initialize(input_file)
    @input_file = input_file
    validate_input_file
  end

  def convert_to_html(output_file = nil)
    output_file ||= "#{File.basename(@input_file, '.*')}.html"
    docx = Docx::Document.open(@input_file)

    html_content = docx.to_html

    File.write(output_file, html_content)
    puts "Successfully converted to HTML: #{output_file}"
  end

  def convert_to_text(output_file = nil)
    output_file ||= "#{File.basename(@input_file, '.*')}.txt"

    # Using Docx gem's text extraction
    docx = Docx::Document.open(@input_file)
    text_content = docx.to_text

    # Alternatively, using Nokogiri for more control
    # text_content = Nokogiri::HTML(docx.to_html).text

    File.write(output_file, text_content)
    puts "Successfully converted to plain text: #{output_file}"
  end

  private

  def validate_input_file
    unless File.exist?(@input_file) && @input_file.end_with?('.docx')
      raise "Input file '#{@input_file}' does not exist or is not a DOCX file"
    end
  end
end

if __FILE__ == $0
  options = {}
  OptionParser.new do |opts|
    opts.banner = "Usage: docx_converter.rb [options] input_file.docx"

    opts.on("-t", "--to-text OUTPUT_FILE", "Convert to plain text") do |output_file|
      options[:to_text] = output_file
    end

    opts.on("-h", "--to-html OUTPUT_FILE", "Convert to HTML") do |output_file|
      options[:to_html] = output_file
    end
  end.parse!

  if ARGV.empty?
    puts "Please provide an input file"
    exit(1)
  end

  input_file = ARGV[0]
  converter = DocxConverter.new(input_file)

  if options[:to_text]
    converter.convert_to_text(options[:to_text])
  elsif options[:to_html]
    converter.convert_to_html(options[:to_html])
  else
    # Default to both if no option specified
    converter.convert_to_html
    converter.convert_to_text
  end
end
```

  end

Here's a complete solution that includes a Gemfile and the implementation code for finding fuzzy matches between company names using Levenshtein and Jaro-Winkler distances.

## Implementation

```ruby
# company_name_matcher.rb
require 'string_score'
require 'levenshtein'

class CompanyNameMatcher
  def initialize(company_names)
    @company_names = company_names
  end

  # Find potential matches for a given company name
  def find_matches(target_name, threshold: 0.7, max_results: 5)
    @company_names.map do |name|
      {
        name: name,
        levenshtein_distance: levenshtein_distance(target_name, name),
        jaro_winkler_similarity: jaro_winkler_similarity(target_name, name)
      }
    end.sort_by { |m| -m[:jaro_winkler_similarity] }
      .take(max_results)
      .select { |m| m[:jaro_winkler_similarity] >= threshold }
  end

  private

  # Calculate Levenshtein distance (edit distance)
  def levenshtein_distance(a, b)
    Levenshtein.distance(a, b)
  end

  # Calculate Jaro-Winkler similarity (0 to 1)
  def jaro_winkler_similarity(a, b)
    StringScore::JaroWinkler.similar(a, b)
  end
end
```

require 'httparty'

Dotenv.load

class TicketSummarizer
  include HTTParty

  # Initialize with Claude API details
  def initialize
    @api_key = ENV['CLAUDE_API_KEY']
    @base_url = 'https://api.anthropic.com/v1/complete'
    @headers = {
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
      'anthropic-version' => '2023-06-01',
      'x-api-key' => @api_key
    }
  end

  # Summarize a support ticket
  def summarize_ticket(ticket_content, max_tokens = 200)
    # Prepare the prompt for Claude
    prompt = <<~PROMPT
      You are an expert support ticket summarizer. Please read the following support ticket and provide a concise summary (max #{max_tokens} tokens). Focus on the key issues, symptoms, and any important details.

      Ticket Content:
      #{ticket_content}

      Summary:
    PROMPT

    # Make the API request
    response = self.class.post(
      @base_url,
      headers: @headers,
      body: {
        prompt: "\n\nHuman: #{prompt}\n\nAssistant:",
        stop_sequences: ["\n\nHuman:"],
        model: "claude-2",
        max_tokens_to_sample: max_tokens
      }.to_json
    )

    # Parse and return the response
    if response.success?
      JSON.parse(response.body)['completion'].strip
    else
      "Error: #{response.parsed_response['error'].to_s}"
    end
  rescue StandardError => e
    "Error summarizing ticket: #{e.message}"
  end
end

# Ruby Fuzzy Matching for Company Names

I'll create a solution that uses fuzzy string matching with both Levenshtein and Jaro-Winkler distances to find similar company names.

```

## Implementation

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'fuzzymatch'
require 'levenshtein'
require 'jaro_winkler'

class CompanyNameMatcher
  def initialize(companies, threshold: 0.8, max_distance: 3)
    @companies = companies
    @threshold = threshold
    @max_distance = max_distance
  end

  # Find all similar company names using multiple fuzzy matching algorithms
  def find_similar(companies_to_match, algorithm: :auto)
    results = []

    companies_to_match.each do |query|
      similar_companies = []

      @companies.each do |company|
        next if company == query

        # Calculate similarity scores
        jaro_winkler = jaro_winkler_similarity(query, company)
        levenshtein_similarity = 1.0 - (levenshtein_distance(query, company).to_f / [query.length, company.length].max)

        # Use the specified algorithm or combine scores
        if algorithm == :auto
          # Combine scores (you can adjust weights as needed)
          combined_score = (jaro_winkler * 0.7) + (levenshtein_similarity * 0.3)
          similarity = combined_score
        elsif algorithm == :jaro_winkler
          similarity = jaro_winkler
        elsif algorithm == :levenshtein
          similarity = levenshtein_similarity
        else
          raise ArgumentError, "Unknown algorithm: #{algorithm}"
        end

        # Add to results if above threshold and within max distance
        if similarity >= @threshold && levenshtein_distance(query, company) <= @max_distance
          similar_companies << {
            company: company,
            similarity: similarity,
            jaro_winkler: jaro_winkler,
            levenshtein_similarity: levenshtein_similarity,
            levenshtein_distance: levenshtein_distance(query, company)
          }
        end
      end

      results << {
        query: query,
        similar_companies: similar_companies
      }
    end

    results
  end

  private

  def jaro_winkler_similarity(str1, str2)
    JaroWinkler.jaro_winkler(str1, str2)
  end

  def levenshtein_distance(str1, str2)
    Levenshtein.distance(str1, str2)
  end
end

```ruby
# lib/profanity_filter.rb
require 'strscan'
require 'pathname'

class ProfanityFilter
  # Default English profanity list (you can expand this)
  DEFAULT_PROFANITY_LIST = [
    'fuck', 'shit', 'bitch', 'ass', 'damn', 'hell', 'piss',
    'cunt', 'dick', 'pussy', 'cock', 'bastard', 'whore',
    'slut', 'nigger', 'nigga', 'jew', 'kike', 'spic',
    'chink', 'gook', 'raghead', 'gypsy', 'tranny',
    'retard', 'spaz', 'cripple', 'mongoloid'
  ].freeze

  def initialize(profanity_list: nil, custom_replacement: '**')
    @profanity_list = profanity_list || DEFAULT_PROFANITY_LIST
    @custom_replacement = custom_replacement
  end

  # Filter a single string
  def filter(text)
    return text if text.is_a?(Numeric) || text.nil?

    text.to_s.gsub(profanity_regex) do |match|
      @custom_replacement * (match.length / @custom_replacement.length.to_f).ceil
    end
  end

  # Filter an array of strings
  def filter_all(texts)
    texts.map { |text| filter(text) }
  end

  private

  # Generate a regex pattern that matches any profanity word
  def profanity_regex
    @profanity_regex ||= begin
      # Escape special regex characters in the profanity words
      escaped_words = @profanity_list.map { |word| Regexp.escape(word) }

      # Create a regex that matches whole words or common variations

Here's a complete implementation that parses natural language dates like "next Friday at 5pm" using Ruby. I'll include a Gemfile first, followed by the implementation.

## Gemfile

## Implementation

```ruby
# date_parser.rb

require 'chronic'
require 'chronic_duration'

class NaturalLanguageDateParser
  def initialize
    @parser = Chronic::Parser.new
  end

  # Parse a natural language date string
  # Returns Time object or nil if parsing fails
  def parse(text)
    # Chronic can handle many natural language formats
    parsed = @parser.parse(text)

    return parsed if parsed

    # Try more specific parsing for cases like "next Friday at 5pm"
    parse_with_time_expression(text)
  end

  private

  def parse_with_time_expression(text)
    # Split into day part and time part
    parts = text.split(' at ')
    day_part = parts.first
    time_part = parts.last if parts.size > 1

    # Parse the day part (e.g., "next Friday")
    day_result = Chronic.parse(day_part)
    return nil unless day_result

    # Parse the time part (e.g., "5pm") if exists
    if time_part
      time_result = Chronic.parse(time_part)
      return nil unless time_result

      # Combine the day and time
      day_result.change(hour: time_result.hour, min: time_result.min)
    else
      day_result
    end
  end
end
```

# Ukrainian Mobile Number Normalizer

Here's a Ruby implementation that normalizes Ukrainian mobile phone numbers to the +380 format and detects the operator. I'll provide a Gemfile and the implementation code.

## Gemfile

```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

# Required gems
gem 'phonelib'  # For phone number parsing and normalization
gem 'i18n'      # For internationalization support
```

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'phonelib'
require 'i18n'

# Load Ukrainian translations for phone number formats
I18n.load_path << Phonelib.config.i18n_path.join('uk.yml')

class UkrainianMobileNormalizer
  # Known Ukrainian mobile operators and their prefixes
  OPERATOR_PREFIXES = {
    'Kyivstar' => ['067', '068', '096', '097', '098'],
    'Vodafone' => ['050', '066', '095', '099'],
    'lifecell' => ['063', '073', '093'],
    '3mobile' => ['091', '092', '094']
  }.freeze

  def self.normalize_and_detect(number)
    # Parse and normalize the phone number
    phone = Phonelib.parse(number, 'UA')

    return { error: 'Invalid phone number' } unless phone.valid?

    # Normalize to +380 format
    normalized = phone.international

    # Extract the operator prefix
    operator = detect_operator(normalized)

    {
      normalized: normalized,
      operator: operator,
      valid: true
    }
  end

  def self.detect_operator(normalized_number)
    # Extract the first 3 digits after country code
    prefix = normalized_number.to_s[3, 3]

    OPERATOR_PREFIXES.each do |operator, prefixes|
      return operator if prefixes.include?(prefix)
    end

    'Unknown operator'
  end
end
```

## Usage Example

```ruby
# Example usage
numbers = [
  '+380671234567',
  '0681234567',
  '380961234567',
  '0501234567',
  '0931234567',
  '0911234567',
  'invalid_number'
]

numbers.each do |number|
  result = UkrainianMobileNormalizer.normalize_and_detect(number)
  if result[:valid]
    puts "Number: #{number}"
    puts "Normalized: #{result[:normalized]}"
    puts "Operator: #{result[:operator]}"
    puts "-" * 40
  else
    puts "Invalid number: #{number}"
    puts "-" * 40
  end
end
```

## How It Works

1. **Gem Dependencies**:
   - `phonelib`: Provides phone number parsing, validation, and normalization
   - `i18n`: Helps with internationalization, though we only use it for number parsing

2. **Normalization Process**:
   - The `Phonelib.parse` method attempts to parse the phone number according to Ukrainian standards
   - `phone.international` returns the normalized number in +380 format
   - The method validates the number before processing

3. **Operator Detection**:
   - The class maintains a hash of known Ukrainian mobile operators and their prefixes
   - After normalization, it extracts the first 3 digits after the country code (+380)
   - It matches these digits against the known prefixes to determine the operator

4. **Error Handling**:
   - Returns an error message if the phone number is invalid

To detect whether a comment is written in Ukrainian, Russian, or Surzhyk, we can use a combination of language detection and some heuristics specific to Surzhyk (a mix of Ukrainian and Russian). Here's a Ruby implementation using the `linguist` gem for language detection and some custom logic for Surzhyk identification.

### Gemfile
```ruby
source "https://rubygems.org"

gem "linguist", "~> 1.0"
```

### Implementation
```ruby
require 'linguist'
require 'set'

class LanguageDetector
  UKRAINIAN_WORDS = Set.new(%w[
    українська український українка українці українські українці
    Галіція Львів Київ Харків Одеса
  ])

  RUSSIAN_WORDS = Set.new(%w[
    русский русская русские Россия Москви
    Санкт-Петербург Новороссия
  ])

  SURZHYK_INDICATORS = Set.new(%w[
    часопис газета газети
    газеті
  ])

  def initialize
    @linguist = Linguist::Language
  end

  def detect_language(text)
    normalized_text = text.downcase

    ukrainian_common = common_words(normalized_text, UKRAINIAN_WORDS)
    russian_common = common_words(normalized_text, RUSSIAN_WORDS)

    # Check for Surzhyk indicators (Ukrainian grammar with Russian words)
    surzhyk_score = common_words(normalized_text, SURZHYK_INDICATORS).size

    # First try linguistic detection
    linguistic_result = @linguist.detect(normalized_text)

    if linguistic_result.nil? || linguistic_result.language.nil?
      # Fallback to word frequency analysis
      if ukrainian_common > russian_common && surzhyk_score > 0
        :surzhyk
      elsif ukrainian_common > russian_common
        :ukrainian
      elsif russian_common > ukrainian_common
        :russian
      else
        :unknown
      end
    else
      case linguistic_result.language
      when 'uk', 'ukrainian'
        # Check if it's actually surzhyk
        if surzhyk_score > 0 && russian_common > 0
          :surzhyk
        else
          :ukrainian
        end
      when 'ru', 'russian'
        # Check if it's actually surzhyk
        if surzhyk_score > 0 && ukrainian_common > 0
          :surzhyk
        else
          :russian
        end
      else
        :unknown
      end
    end
  end

  private

  def common_words(text, word_set)
    return 0 if text.strip.empty?

    # Simple tokenization (split by non-word characters)
    words = text.scan(/\b\w+\b/).map(&:downcase)
    (words & word_set).size
  end
end

# Example usage
detector = LanguageDetector.new

comments = [
  "Це український текст. Львів - прекрасне місто.",
  "Это русский текст. Москва - прекрасный город.",
  "Це часок з газети, але тут деякі російські слова.",
  "Это газета, но тут некоторые украинские слова.",
  "Привіт, як справи? Я з Києва."
]

comments.each do |comment|
  language = detector.detect_language(comment)
  puts "Comment: #{comment}"
  puts "Detected: #{language}\n"
end
```

### Explanation:
1. **Gemfile**: Includes the `linguist` gem for language detection.
2. **LanguageDetector class**:
   - Contains sets of characteristic words for Ukrainian, Russian, and Surzhyk.
   - Uses `linguist` for initial language detection.
   - Falls back to word frequency analysis if linguistic detection is inconclusive.
   - Uses Surzhyk indicators (like Ukrainian grammar with Russian words) to detect Surzhyk.
3. **Example usage**: Tests the detector with sample comments in Ukrainian, Russian, and Surzhyk.

This implementation provides a basic approach to language detection. For more accurate results, you might need to:
- Expand the word sets with more characteristic words.
- Use more sophisticated NLP techniques.
- Consider using machine learning models for better accuracy.

# Ukrainian Pluralization in Rails I18n

Here's how to implement Ukrainian pluralization rules in a Rails application.

## Gemfile

```ruby
# Gemfile
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'rails', '~> 7.0.0'  # or your Rails version
gem 'i18n', '~> 1.12.0'  # Rails includes this by default, but we specify for clarity
```

## Implementation

### 1. Create the I18n locale file

Create a file at `config/locales/uk.yml` with the Ukrainian pluralization rules:

```ruby
# config/locales/uk.yml
uk:
  plural:
    keys:
      - one
      - few
      - many
      - other
    rules:
      - rule: "n == 1"
        one: true
        other: false
      - rule: "n % 10 == 2 && n % 100 != 12 && n % 100 != 112"
        few: true
        other: false
      - rule: "n % 10 == 3 && n % 100 != 13 && n % 100 != 113"
        few: true
        other: false
      - rule: "n % 10 == 4 && n % 100 != 14 && n % 100 != 114"
        few: true
        other: false
      - rule: "n % 100 >= 5 && n % 100 <= 20"
        many: true
        other: false
      - rule: "n % 100 >= 25 && n % 100 <= 30"
        many: true
        other: false
      - rule: "n % 100 >= 125 && n % 100 <= 130"
        many: true
        other: false
      - rule: "n % 100 >= 225 && n % 100 <= 230"
        many: true
        other: false
      - rule: "n % 100 >= 325 && n % 100 <= 330"
        many: true
        other: false
      - rule: "n % 100 >= 425 && n % 100 <= 430"
        many: true
        other: false
      - rule: "n % 100 >= 525 && n % 100 <= 530"
        many: true
        other: false
      - rule: "n % 100 >= 625 && n % 100 <= 630"
        many: true
        other: false
      - rule: "n % 10 == 0 || (n % 10 == 5 && n % 100 != 15 && n % 100 != 115) || (n % 10 == 6 && n % 100 != 16 && n % 100 != 116) || (n % 10 == 7 && n % 100 != 17 && n % 100 != 117) || (n % 10 == 8 && n % 100 != 18 && n % 100 != 118) || (n % 10 == 9 && n % 100 != 19 && n % 100 != 119)"
        other: true
        one: false
        few: false
        many: false
```

### 2. Example usage in your application

You can use these pluralization rules in your views, controllers, or models:

```ruby

  @users = User.all
  @message = t('activerecord.models.user.plural', count: @users.count)
end

To detect whether a comment is written in Ukrainian, Russian, or Surzhyk (a mixture of Ukrainian and Russian), we can use a language detection gem. The `language_detector` gem is a good choice, but it might not be as accurate for dialect detection. Another option is to use a more sophisticated NLP library, but for simplicity, we'll use a combination of heuristics and the `language_detector` gem.

Here's the implementation:

### Gemfile
```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'language_detector'
```

Run `bundle install` to install the required gem.

### Implementation
```ruby
require 'language_detector'
require 'set'

# Initialize the language detector
LanguageDetector::Detector.load_profile(:uk)  # Ukrainian
LanguageDetector::Detector.load_profile(:ru)  # Russian

# Common Ukrainian words (excluding Russian)
UKRAINIAN_WORDS = Set.new([
  'україна', 'київ', 'львів', 'харків', 'одержимо', 'герої', 'ми', 'наші',
  'історичний', 'культура', 'традиції', 'держава', 'народ', 'укр', 'українець'
])

# Common Russian words (excluding Ukrainian)
RUSSIAN_WORDS = Set.new([
  'россия', 'москва', 'питер', 'держава', 'народ', 'страна', 'русский', 'рус',
  'наш', 'российский', 'российские', 'московский'
])

# Common Surzhyk words (mixed Ukrainian and Russian)
SURZHYK_WORDS = Set.new([
  'мова', 'язык', 'держава', 'страна', 'народ', 'україна', 'россия', 'грамота',
  'література', 'литература', 'наш', 'ми', 'мы', 'українець', 'русский'
])

def detect_language(text)
  # Convert to lowercase for case-insensitive comparison
  text_down = text.downcase

  # Check for Ukrainian words
  ukrainian_count = (text_down.scan(/(україна|київ|львів|харків|одержимо|герої|ми|наші|історичний|культура|традиції|держава|народ|укр|українець)/) & UKRAINIAN_WORDS).count
  # Check for Russian words
  russian_count = (text_down.scan(/(россия|москва|питер|держава|народ|страна|русский|рус|наш|российский|российские|московский)/) & RUSSIAN_WORDS).count

  # Check for Surzhyk indicators (mixed words)
  surzhyk_count = (text_down.scan(/(мова|язык|держава|страна|народ|україна|россия|грамота|література|литература|наш|ми|мы|українець|русский)/) & SURZHYK_WORDS).count

  # Use language detection for initial guess
  detected = LanguageDetector::Detector.detect(text)

  # Heuristics to determine the language
  if ukrainian_count > russian_count && ukrainian_count > surzhyk_count
    :uk
  elsif russian_count > ukrainian_count && russian_count > surzhyk_count
    :ru
  elsif surzhyk_count >= ukrainian_count && surzhyk_count >= russian_count
    :surzhyk
  else
    # Fallback to language detector
    detected.to_sym
  end
end

# Example usage
text_ukrainian = "Це текст українською мовою, де ми говоримо про Україну."
text_russian = "Это текст на русском языке, где мы говорим о России."
text_surzhyk = "Це текст на суржику, де ми говоримо про країну та народ."

puts "Ukrainian text detected as: #{detect_language(text_ukrainian)}"
puts "Russian text detected as: #{detect_language(text_russian)}"
puts "Surzhyk text detected as: #{detect_language(text_surzhyk)}"
```

### Explanation:
1. **Gemfile**: Includes the `language_detector` gem for basic language detection.
2. **Language Detection**:
   - The `detect_language` method uses a combination of word matching and the `language_detector` gem.
   - Ukrainian, Russian, and Surzhyk words are defined as sets for quick lookup.
   - The method counts occurrences of these words in the input text to determine the most likely language.
3. **Fallback**: If the word counts are inconclusive, it falls back to the `language_detector` gem.

### Notes:
- This is a heuristic approach and may not be 100% accurate, especially for short texts or mixed-language content.
- For more accurate detection, consider using a more advanced NLP library or a machine learning model trained on Ukrainian, Russian, and Surzhyk text.

Here's a Ruby solution for extracting named entities from Ukrainian news articles. This implementation uses the `stanford-nlp` gem for named entity recognition (NER) and `open-uri` for fetching articles.

### Gemfile
```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'stanford-nlp'
gem 'nokogiri'  # For HTML parsing
gem 'open-uri'  # For fetching articles
```

### Implementation
```ruby
require 'stanford-nlp'
require 'nokogiri'
require 'open-uri'

class NewsEntityExtractor
  def initialize
    # Initialize the StanfordNLP processor
    @nlp = StanfordNLP::CoreNLP.new(
      annotators: %w(tok ssplit pos ner lemma),
      language: 'uk'  # Ukrainian language
    )
  end

  # Fetch article content from a URL
  def fetch_article(url)
    html = URI.open(url).read
    doc = Nokogiri::HTML(html)

    # Extract main article text (this selector might need adjustment based on the site)
    doc.at_css('article, .article-content, .news-content').try(:text) || doc.text
  end

  # Extract named entities from text
  def extract_entities(text)
    @nlp.annotate(text).select do |sentence|
      sentence['sentences'].any? do |sent|
        sent['entitymentions'].any? { |entity| %w(PERSON ORG LOCATION).include?(entity['ner']) }
      end
    end
  end

  # Process a news article URL
  def process_article(url)
    text = fetch_article(url)
    entities = extract_entities(text)

    entities.flat_map do |sentence|
      sentence['sentences'].flat_map do |sent|
        sent['entitymentions'].select { |entity| %w(PERSON ORG LOCATION).include?(entity['ner']) }
      end
    end
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0
  extractor = NewsEntityExtractor.new

  # Example Ukrainian news URL (you might need to adjust the URL and selectors)
  article_url = 'https://www.pravda.com.ua/news/'

  begin
    entities = extractor.process_article(article_url)

    puts "Named Entities Found:"
    entities.each do |entity|
      puts "#{entity['text']} - #{entity['ner']}"
    end
  rescue => e
    puts "Error processing article: #{e.message}"
  end
end
```

### Notes:
1. **StanfordNLP Setup**: The `stanford-nlp` gem requires Java. Make sure you have Java installed on your system.

2. **Ukrainian Language Support**: The StanfordNLP processor needs to be properly configured for Ukrainian. You might need to:
   - Download the appropriate language models
   - Configure the processor with the right models

3. **Article Parsing**: The HTML parsing logic (especially the CSS selectors) will need to be adjusted based on the specific news website you're targeting.

4. **Alternative Approach**: If StanfordNLP doesn't work well with Ukrainian, you might consider:
   - Using a Ukrainian-specific NLP library
   - Translating the text to English first (using a gem like `google_translate`)
   - Using a different NER service with Ukrainian support

5. **Error Handling**: The code includes basic error handling, but you might want to expand it for production use.

  end
  comment

class UkrainianKeyboardConverter

  # This is the standard Windows Ukrainian layout (not US International)
  LATIN_TO_UKRAINIAN = {

def normalize_and_determine_operator(phone_number)
  # Видаляємо всі символи, окрім цифр

  else

    profanity_words = @profanity_words.map { |word| Regexp.escape(word) }.join('|')

  PROFANITY_WORDS_FILE = 'profanity_words.yml'

  def initialize
    @profanity_words = load_profanity_words
    @replacement = "****"
  end

  def filter(comment)
    return comment unless comment.is_a?(String)

    scanner = StringScanner.new(comment.downcase)
    result = []

    while scanner.scan(/(?:\w+|.)/) do
      word = scanner.matched
      if @profanity_words.include?(word)
        result << @replacement
      else
        result << word
      end
    end

    result.join

  }.freeze

  def self.convert_latin_to_ukrainian(text)
    text.chars.map do |char|
      LATIN_TO_UKRAINIAN.fetch(char, char)
    end.join
  end

  # Alternative method that uses KOI8-U encoding if the text was encoded that way
  def self.convert_from_koi8_u(text)
    text.force_encoding('KOI8-U').encode('UTF-8')
  end
end

def transliterate(text)
  # Замінюємо кожен символ згідно словника
  text.chars.map do |char|

  .gsub(/t(\w)/i, 'т\1')
  .gsub(/v(\w)/i, 'в\1')
  .gsub(/z(\w)/i, 'з\1')
  # Виправляємо великі літери
  .gsub(/(^|\s)([a-z])/) { |_| Regexp.last_match(1) + Regexp.last_match(2).upcase }
end

)

  rand(100_000..999_999).to_s
end

# Helper method to send SMS

  $twilio_client.messages.create(
    from: ENV['TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER'],
    to: phone_number,
    body: message
  )
end

# Route to initiate verification
post '/start_verification' do
  content_type :json

  # Validate input
  unless params[:phone_number]
    return { error: 'Phone number is required' }.to_json
  end

  phone_number = params[:phone_number]

  # Generate and store verification code
  verification_code = generate_verification_code
  $verification_codes[phone_number] = {
    code: verification_code,
    created_at: Time.now
  }

  # Send SMS
  message = "Your verification code is: #{verification_code}"
  send_sms(phone_number, message)

  { status: 'success', message: 'Verification code sent' }.to_json
end

# Route to verify the code
post '/verify_code' do
  content_type :json

  # Validate input
  unless params[:phone_number] && params[:code]
    return { error: 'Phone number and code are required' }.to_json
  end

  phone_number = params[:phone_number]
  code = params[:code]

  # Check if we have a verification code for this number
  verification_data = $verification_codes[phone_number]

  if verification_data.nil?
    return { error: 'No verification code found for this phone number' }.to_json
  end

  # Check if the code matches and is not expired (5 minutes)
  if verification_data[:code] == code &&
     (Time.now - verification_data[:created_at]) < 300

    # Verification successful - remove the code
    $verification_codes.delete(phone_number)

    { status: 'verified', message: 'Verification successful' }.to_json
  else
    { error: 'Invalid or expired verification code' }.to_json
  end
end

# Ukrainian News Named Entity Extraction

Below is a Ruby implementation for extracting named entities (people, organizations, places) from Ukrainian news articles. The solution uses NLP libraries to handle Ukrainian text.

## Gemfile

```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

# Core NLP processing
gem 'stanford-core-nlp', '~> 5.1.0'

# For handling Ukrainian text
gem 'icu4r'

# For HTTP requests to fetch news articles
gem 'httparty'

# For text processing
gem 'nokogiri'
gem 'unicode_utils'

# For logging
gem 'logger'

# For parallel processing
gem 'parallel'
```

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'stanford-core-nlp'
require 'icu4r'
require 'httparty'
require 'nokogiri'
require 'unicode_utils'
require 'logger'
require 'parallel'

# Configure Stanford CoreNLP
StanfordCoreNLP.java_classpath = 'stanford-corenlp-full-2018-10-05/*'

# Logger configuration
LOGGER = Logger.new($stdout)
LOGGER.level = Logger::INFO

class NewsEntityExtractor
  def initialize
    @properties = {
      'annotators' => 'tokenize, ssplit, pos, lemma, ner',
      'language' => 'uk',
      'parse.model' => 'edu/stanford/nlp/models/lexparser/ukrainianSR.ser.gz',
      'ner.model' => 'edu/stanford/nlp/models/ner/ukrainian.ser.gz',
      'ner.applyFineGrained' => 'false',
      'outputFormat' => 'json'
    }

    @pipeline = StanfordCoreNLP.load_pipeline(@properties)
  end

  def fetch_news_article(url)
    response = HTTParty.get(url)
    response.body
  end

  def extract_article_text(html)
    doc = Nokogiri::HTML(html)
    doc.css('article, .article, .content, .post-body').first&.text ||
      doc.css('p').text
  end

  def clean_text(text)
    # Remove excessive whitespace and normalize
    text.gsub(/\s+/, ' ').strip
  end

  def extract_entities(text)
    document = @pipeline.annotate(text)

    entities = []
    document.each_sentence do |sentence|
      sentence.each_token do |token|
        next unless token.ner_tag

        entity_type = token.ner_tag.downcase
        entity_text = token.word

        # Only process our target entity types
        if ['PERSON', 'ORGANIZATION', 'LOCATION'].include?(entity_type)
          entities << {
            text: entity_text,
            type: entity_type,
            sentence: sentence.text
          }
        end
      end
    end

    # Deduplicate entities
    deduplicated = entities.uniq { |e| e[:text] }

    # Group by type
    {
      people: deduplicated.select { |e| e[:type] == 'PERSON' },
      organizations: deduplicated.select { |e| e[:type] == 'ORGANIZATION' },
      places: deduplicated.select { |e| e[:type] == 'LOCATION' }
    }
  end

  def process_article(url)
    LOGGER.info "Processing article: #{url}"
    begin
      html = fetch_news_article(url)
      text = extract_article_text(html)
      clean_text = clean_text(text)

      if clean_text.strip.empty?
        LOGGER.warn "No text content found in article: #{url}"
        return { url: url, error: 'No text content found' }
      end

      entities = extract_entities(clean_text)

      {
        url: url,
        entities: entities,
        success: true
      }
    rescue StandardError => e
      LOGGER.error "Error processing article #{url}: #{e.message}"
      { url: url, error: e.message, success: false }
    end
  end

  def process_articles(urls)
    Parallel.map(urls, in_threads: 4) do |url|
      process_article(url)
    end
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0
  extractor = NewsEntityExtractor.new

  # Example Ukrainian news URLs
  ukraine_news_urls = [
    'https://www.pravda.com.ua/rus/news/2023/12/15/7433881/',
    'https://www.ukrinform.ua/rubric-ukraine/3663865-za-24-godi-v-ukraini-znaisovili-12-dene-ili-94-a-poranna-stolittia-12.html',
    'https://www.epravda.com.ua/rus/news/2023/12/15/7433881/'
  ]

  results = extractor.process_articles(ukraine_news_urls)

  results.each do |result|
    if result[:success]
      LOGGER.info "Entities from #{result[:url]}"
      result[:entities].each do |type, entities|
        LOGGER.info "#{type.to_s.capitalize}:"
        entities.each { |e| LOGGER.info "  - #{e[:text]} (in: #{e[:sentence]})" }
      end
    else
      LOGGER.error "Failed to process #{result[:url]}: #{result[:error]}"
    end

require 'nokogiri'

require 'stanford-nlp'

class NewsEntityExtractor
  def initialize
    @ner_pipeline = StanfordNLP::Pipeline.new do |config|
      config[:language] = 'uk' # Вказати українську мову (якщо підтримується)
      config[:annotators] = 'tokenize, ssplit, pos, lemma, ner' # Використовуємо NER
    end
  end

  def fetch_article(url)
    URI.open(url) do |response|
      Nokogiri::HTML(response.read)
    end
  rescue StandardError => e
    puts "Помилка завантаження статті: #{e.message}"
    nil
  end

  # Метод для витягнення тексту зі статті (можна адаптувати під конкретні сайти)
  def extract_text(html)
    # Простий парсер - вибираємо всі текстові вузли
    html.text.gsub(/\s+/, ' ').strip
  end

  # Метод для аналізу тексту та витягнення іменованих сутностей
  def extract_entities(text)
    document = @ner_pipeline.annotate(text)
    entities = []

    document[:sentences].each do |sentence|
      sentence[:entities].each do |entity|
        entities << {
          type: entity[:ner],
          text: entity[:text],
          start: entity[:start_char],
          end: entity[:end_char]
        }
      end
    end

    entities
  end

  # Метод для виведення результатів
  def print_entities(entities)
    puts "Виявлені іменовані сутності:"
    entities.each do |entity|
      puts "- Тип: #{entity[:type]}, Текст: '#{entity[:text]}'"
    end
  end

  # Головний метод для обробки URL-статті
  def process_article(url)
    html = fetch_article(url)
    return unless html

    text = extract_text(html)
    entities = extract_entities(text)

    print_entities(entities)
  rescue StandardError => e
    puts "Помилка обробки статті: #{e.message}"
  end
end

# config/initializers/fcm.rb
require 'google/cloud/messaging'
require 'dotenv'

Dotenv.load

class FcmNotifier
  def initialize
    @client = Google::Cloud::Messaging.fcm do |config|
      config.credentials = Google::Cloud::Messaging::Credentials.new(
        server_key: ENV['FCM_SERVER_KEY']
      )
    end
  end

  # Send to a single device
  def send_notification(device_token, title, body, data = {})
    message = Google::Cloud::Messaging::Message.new(
      notification: {
        title: title,
        body: body
      },
      data: data,
      token: device_token
    )

    response = @client.send(message)
    puts "Notification sent to #{device_token}: #{response}"
    response
  end

  # Send to multiple devices
  def send_to_multiple(device_tokens, title, body, data = {})
    device_tokens.each do |token|
      send_notification(token, title, body, data)
    end
  end

  # Send to topic (for iOS and Android)
  def send_to_topic(topic, title, body, data = {})
    message = Google::Cloud::Messaging::Message.new(
      notification: {
        title: title,
        body: body
      },
      data: data,
      topic: topic
    )

    response = @client.send(message)
    puts "Notification sent to topic #{topic}: #{response}"
    response
  end
end

# whatsapp_client.rb
require 'faraday'

require 'dotenv'

Dotenv.load

class WhatsAppClient
  BASE_URL = ENV['WHATSAPP_API_BASE_URL'] || 'https://graph.facebook.com/v18.0'
  PHONE_NUMBER_ID = ENV['WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_PHONE_ID']
  ACCOUNT_ID = ENV['WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_ACCOUNT_ID']
  ACCESS_TOKEN = ENV['WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN']

  def initialize
    @connection = Faraday.new(url: BASE_URL) do |faraday|
      faraday.request :json
      faraday.response :json, content_type: /\bjson$/
      faraday.response :raise_error
      faraday.adapter Faraday.default_adapter
    end
  end

  def send_template_message(phone_number, template_name, language_code, components = [])
    # WhatsApp API endpoint for sending template messages
    url = "#{BASE_URL}/#{PHONE_NUMBER_ID}/messages"

    headers = {
      'Authorization' => "Bearer #{ACCESS_TOKEN}",
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
    }

    payload = {
      messaging_product: 'whatsapp',
      recipient_type: 'individual',
      to: phone_number,
      type: 'template',
      template: {
        name: template_name,
        language: {
          code: language_code
        },
        components: components
      }
    }

    response = @connection.post(url, payload, headers)
    response.body
  rescue Faraday::Error => e
    handle_error(e)
  end

  def get_template_by_name(template_name)
    url = "#{BASE_URL}/#{PHONE_NUMBER_ID}/message_templates?name=#{URI.encode_www_form_component(template_name)}"

    response = @connection.get(url) do |req|
      req.headers['Authorization'] = "Bearer #{ACCESS_TOKEN}"
    end

    response.body
  rescue Faraday::Error => e
    handle_error(e)
  end

  def handle_error(error)
    if error.response
      { error: error.message, response: error.response_body }
    else
      { error: error.message }
    end
  end
end

```ruby
# lib/whatsapp_business_client.rb
require 'faraday'
require 'faraday_middleware'
require 'oj'

class WhatsAppBusinessClient
  BASE_URL = 'https://graph.facebook.com/v18.0'.freeze

  def initialize(access_token)
    @access_token = access_token
    @phone_number_id = ENV['WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID']
    raise 'WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID environment variable is required' unless @phone_number_id
  end

  def send_template_message(to: nil, template: nil, language: nil, components: [])
    body = {
      messaging_product: 'whatsapp',
      recipient_type: 'individual',
      to: to,
      type: 'template',
      template: {
        name: template,
        language: language,
        components: components
      }
    }.compact

    response = connection.post("https://graph.facebook.com/v18.0/#{@phone_number_id}/messages", body)

    if response.success?
      Oj.load(response.body)
    else
      raise "WhatsApp API error: #{response.status}: #{response.body}"
    end
  end

  private

  def connection
    Faraday.new(url: BASE_URL) do |f|
      f.request :json
      f.response :json
      f.response :logger if ENV['DEBUG'] == 'true'
      f.adapter Faraday.default_adapter
    end.tap do |conn|
      conn.headers['Authorization'] = "Bearer #{@access_token}"
      conn.headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json'
    end
  end
end
```

## Gemfile

First, let's create a Gemfile that includes all the necessary gems:

```ruby
# Gemfile
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'google-cloud-firebase'
gem 'rest-client' # For making HTTP requests
gem 'json' # For JSON handling
```

## Implementation

Here's the Ruby implementation for sending push notifications to both Android and iOS devices through Firebase Cloud Messaging:

```ruby
# app/services/fcm_notification_sender.rb
require 'google/cloud/firebase'
require 'json'

class FCMNotificationSender
  def initialize(credentials_path = 'path/to/service-account-key.json')
    @firebase = Google::Cloud::Firebase.new(credentials_path: credentials_path)
  end

  # Send a notification to a specific device
  def send_to_device(device_token, title, body, data = nil, android_channel_id = nil)
    message = build_message(device_token, title, body, data, android_channel_id)
    response = @firebase.messaging.send(message)
    response
  end

  # Send a notification to multiple devices (device group or topic)
  def send_to_multiple(device_tokens, title, body, data = nil, android_channel_id = nil)
    if device_tokens.is_a?(Array)
      # For multiple device tokens
      message = build_message(device_tokens, title, body, data, android_channel_id)
      message.topic = nil # Ensure not using topic mode
    else
      # For topics
      message = build_message(nil, title, body, data, android_channel_id)
      message.topic = device_tokens
    end

    response = @firebase.messaging.send(message)
    response
  end

  private

  def build_message(device_tokens, title, body, data, android_channel_id)
    message = Google::Cloud::Firebase::Messaging::Message.new

    if device_tokens.is_a?(Array)
      message.token = device_tokens
    elsif device_tokens
      message.token = [device_tokens]
    end

    if title || body
      notification = Google::Cloud::Firebase::Messaging::Notification.new
      notification.title = title if title
      notification.body = body if body
      message.notification = notification
    end

    if data
      if data.is_a?(Hash)
        message.data = data
      else
        raise ArgumentError, "Data must be a Hash"
      end
    end

    if android_channel_id
      message.android = Google::Cloud::Firebase::Messaging::AndroidConfig.new
      message.android.fcm_options = Google::Cloud::Firebase::Messaging::AndroidFcmOptions.new
      message.android.fcm_options.analytic_properties = { 'channel_id' => android_channel_id }
    end

    message
  end
end
```

Here's how you would use the FCMNotificationSender class:

```ruby

LOGGER.level = Logger::INFO

# Create bot instance
BOT = Discordrb::Bot.new(token: ENV['DISCORD_TOKEN'])

# Deployment notification command
BOT.command(:deploy, description: "Post a deployment notification", usage: "!deploy <environment> <version> [message]") do |event, environment, version, *message_parts|
  unless %w[production staging development].include?(environment)
    event.respond("❌ Invalid environment. Must be one of: production, staging, development")
    return
  end

  message = message_parts.join(" ") || "No additional details provided"

        value: environment.capitalize,
        inline: true
      },
      {
        name: "Version",
        value: version,
        inline: true
      }
    ],
    timestamp: Time.now
  )

  event.channel.send_embed(embed) do |embed|
    embed.add_field(name: "Message", value: message, inline: false)
  end

  LOGGER.info("Deployment notification sent by #{event.user.username} for #{environment}")
end

# Slash command: ping
BOT.command(:ping, description: "Responds with Pong!") do |event|
  event.respond("Pong! 🏓")
  LOGGER.info("Ping command used by #{event.user.username}")
end

# Slash command: serverinfo
BOT.command(:serverinfo, description: "Displays information about the server") do |event|
  guild = event.guild
  owner = guild.owner
  roles = guild.roles.size
  channels = guild.channels.size

  embed = Discordrb::Webhooks::Embed.new(
    title: "Server Information",
    color: 0x0072ff, # Blue
    fields: [
      { name: "Name", value: guild.name, inline: true },
      { name: "Owner", value: owner.username, inline: true },
      { name: "Created At", value: guild.created_at.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), inline: true },
      { name: "Member Count", value: guild.members.size, inline: true },
      { name: "Role Count", value: roles, inline: true },
      { name: "Channel Count", value: channels, inline: true }
    ],
    thumbnail: guild.icon_url
  )

  event.respond(embed: embed)
  LOGGER.info("Serverinfo command used by #{event.user.username}")
end

# Error handling
BOT.ready do |event|
  LOGGER.info("Bot is online! Logged in as #{event.bot.profile.username}")
end

BOT.error do |event, error|
  LOGGER.error("Error occurred: #{error.message}")
  event.respond("An error occurred. Please try again later.") if event.respondable?
end

# Start the bot
BOT.run
```

Here's a complete solution for sending an SMS through the Vonage (formerly Nexmo) API and tracking delivery receipts in Ruby. The solution includes a `Gemfile` and the necessary implementation.

### Implementation

1. First, create a `.env` file in your project root to store your Vonage API credentials:
```
VONAGE_API_KEY=your_api_key
VONAGE_API_SECRET=your_api_secret
```

2. Here's the Ruby implementation:

```ruby
require 'vonage'
require 'dotenv/load'

# Configuration
Vonage.api_key = ENV['VONAGE_API_KEY']
Vonage.api_secret = ENV['VONAGE_API_SECRET']

class SMSClient
  def initialize
    @client = Vonage::SMS.new
  end

  def send_sms(to, from, text, reference = nil)
    response = @client.send_request(
      from: from,
      to: to,
      text: text,
      reference: reference || generate_reference
    )

    if response.success?
      { status: 'success', message_id: response.message_id, reference: response.reference }
    else
      { status: 'error', error: response.error_text }
    end
  rescue Vonage::Error => e
    { status: 'error', error: e.message }
  end

  def generate_reference
    "#{(0...8).map { (65 + rand(26)).chr }.join}"
  end

  # Track the status of a message using the message_id or reference
  def get_message_status(message_id, reference = nil)
    response = @client.get_message_status(
      message_id: message_id,
      reference: reference
    )

    if response.success?
      {
        status: 'success',
        message_status: response.data['messages'].first['status'],
        created_at: response.data['messages'].first['created_at'],
        updated_at: response.data['messages'].first['updated_at']
      }
    else
      { status: 'error', error: response.error_text }
    end
  rescue Vonage::Error => e
    { status: 'error', error: e.message }
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0
  client = SMSClient.new

  # Send an SMS
  result = client.send_sms(
    to: 'RECIPIENT_PHONE_NUMBER',  # e.g., '447700900000'
    from: 'YOUR_VONAGE_NUMBER',    # e.g., '441234567890'
    text: 'Hello from Vonage! This is a test message.'
  )

  puts "SMS send result: #{result}"

  # Check delivery status (after some delay)
  if result[:status] == 'success'
    sleep(5) # Wait a few seconds for delivery status to update
    status_result = client.get_message_status(result[:message_id])
    puts "Delivery status: #{status_result}"
  end
end
```

```

2. Run the example:

```

### Key Features

1. **SMS Sending**: Sends SMS messages through the Vonage API
2. **Delivery Tracking**: Provides a method to check the delivery status
3. **Error Handling**: Includes proper error handling for API requests
4. **Reference Management**: Automatically generates a reference for tracking
5. **Environment Configuration**: Uses environment variables for secure credential management

### Notes

- Make sure to:

# Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) Push Notifications in Ruby

Here's a complete solution for sending push notifications to Android and iOS devices through Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM).

## Gemfile

```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'fcm' # Official Firebase Cloud Messaging gem for Ruby
```

Run `bundle install` after creating this file.

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'fcm'

# Configuration class to manage FCM settings
class FCMConfig
  def self.server_key
    ENV['FCM_SERVER_KEY'] || 'your-firebase-server-key'
  end

  def self.project_id
    ENV['FCM_PROJECT_ID'] || 'your-firebase-project-id'
  end
end

# Service class for sending push notifications
class FCMNotificationService
  def initialize
    @fcm = FCM.new(FCMConfig.server_key)
  end

  # Send notification to a single device
  def send_notification_to_device(registration_id, title, body, data = {})
    options = {
      notification: {
        title: title,
        body: body
      },
      data: data,
      registration_ids: [registration_id]
    }

    response = @fcm.send(options)
    response
  end

  # Send notification to multiple devices
  def send_notification_to_devices(registration_ids, title, body, data = {})
    options = {
      notification: {
        title: title,
        body: body
      },
      data: data,
      registration_ids: registration_ids
    }

    response = @fcm.send(options)
    response
  end

  # Send notification to a topic
  def send_notification_to_topic(topic, title, body, data = {})
    options = {
      notification: {
        title: title,
        body: body
      },
      data: data,
      to: "/topics/#{topic}"
    }

    response = @fcm.send(options)
    response
  end

  # Send notification with custom targeting
  def send_custom_notification(condition, title, body, data = {})
    options = {
      notification: {
        title: title,
        body: body
      },
      data: data,
      condition: condition # Example: "'topic1' in topics || 'topic2' in topics"
    }

    response = @fcm.send(options)
    response
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0
  # Initialize the service
  notification_service = FCMNotificationService.new

  # Example 1: Send to a single device
  android_device_token = "your-android-device-token"
  response = notification_service.send_notification_to_device(
    android_device_token,
    "Hello from Ruby!",
    "This is a test notification sent from a Ruby application",
    { custom_data: "value123" }
  )
  puts "Single device notification response: #{response.inspect}"

  # Example 2: Send to multiple devices
  device_tokens = [
    "android-device-token-1",
    "ios-device-token-1",
    "android-device-token-2"
  ]
  response = notification_service.send_notification_to_devices(
    device_tokens,
    "Broadcast Message",
    "This notification goes to multiple devices",
    { category: "news" }
  )
  puts "Multiple devices notification response: #{response.inspect}"

  # Example 3: Send to a topic
  response = notification_service.send_notification_to_topic(
    "news_updates",
    "Breaking News",
    "Important news update for subscribers",
    { news_id: "12345" }
  )
  puts "Topic notification response: #{response.inspect}

  # Example 4: Send with custom condition
  response = notification_service.send_custom_notification(
    "'news_updates' in topics || 'alerts' in topics",
    "Urgent Update",
    "This is an urgent message for all subscribers",
    { priority: "high" }
  )
  puts "Custom condition notification response: #{response.inspect}"
end
```

## Setup Instructions

1. Add the `fcm` gem to your Gemfile as shown above
2. Run `bundle install`
3. Get your Firebase server key and project ID from the Firebase Console
4. Set them as environment variables or replace the placeholders in the code
5. Ensure your app has the Firebase SDK properly configured for both Android and iOS

# lib/whatsapp_business_client.rb
require 'faraday'
require 'json'
require 'request_store'

class WhatsAppBusinessClient
  BASE_URL = 'https://graph.facebook.com/v18.0'

  def initialize(access_token, phone_number_id, api_version: 'v18.0')
    @access_token = access_token
    @phone_number_id = phone_number_id
    @api_version = api_version

    setup_faraday
  end

  def send_template_message(recipient_phone_number, template_name, language_code = 'en_US', components = [])
    url = "#{BASE_URL}/#{@api_version}/#{@phone_number_id}/messages"

    payload = {
      messaging_product: 'whatsapp',
      recipient_type: 'individual',
      to: format_phone_number(recipient_phone_number),
      type: 'template',
      template: {
        name: template_name,
        language: {
          code: language_code
        }
      }
    }

    add_components_to_payload(payload, components) if components.any?

    response = connection.post(url) do |req|
      req.body = payload.to_json
      req.headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json'
    end

    parse_response(response)
  end

  private

  def setup_faraday
    @connection = Faraday.new(url: BASE_URL) do |f|
      f.request :json
      f.response :json
      f.response :raise_error
      f.adapter Faraday.default_adapter
    end
  end

  def connection
    @connection
  end

  def format_phone_number(phone_number)
    # Remove any non-digit characters except leading +
    formatted = phone_number.gsub(/[^\d+]/, '')
    # Ensure the correct format (e.g., +14155238888)
    formatted
  end

  def add_components_to_payload(payload, components)
    template = payload[:template]
    template[:components] = components
  end

  def parse_response(response)
    if response.success?
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      raise "WhatsApp API error: #{response.status} - #{response.body}"
    end
  end
end
```

Here's a complete solution for sending SMS through the Vonage (formerly Nexmo) API and tracking delivery receipts:

## Implementation

First, create a `config` directory and add a `.env` file (add this to your `.gitignore`):

```

VONAGE_API_SECRET=your_api_secret
VONAGE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH=path/to/private/key
VONAGE_APPLICATION_ID=your_application_id
```

Then create the main implementation file (e.g., `vonage_sms.rb`):

```ruby
require 'vonage'
require 'json'
require 'dotenv/load'

class VonageSMS
  def initialize
    # Configure Vonage client
    @client = Vonage::Client.new(
      application_id: ENV['VONAGE_APPLICATION_ID'],
      private_key: File.read(ENV['VONAGE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH']),
      api_key: ENV['VONAGE_API_KEY'],
      api_secret: ENV['VONAGE_API_SECRET']
    )
  end

  # Send SMS and get delivery receipt reference
  def send_sms(to, from, text)
    response = @client.sms.send(
      from: from,
      to: to,
      text: text,
      type: 'unicode' # For international characters
    )

    if response.successful?
      {
        message_id: response.messages.first['message-id'],
        to: to,
        from: from,
        status: response.messages.first['status'],
        status_code: response.code
      }
    else
      {
        error: response.error_text,
        status_code: response.code
      }
    end
  end

  # Check delivery receipt status
  def check_delivery_status(message_id)
    delivery_receipt = @client.sms.dr(message_id)

    if delivery_receipt.successful?
      delivery_receipt.messages.first
    else
      {
        error: delivery_receipt.error_text,
        status_code: delivery_receipt.code
      }
    end
  end

  # Set up delivery receipt webhook (for asynchronous notifications)
  def setup_webhook(url)
    @client.sms.webhooks.create(
      url: url,
      events: ['delivered', 'failed', 'buffered']
    )
  end
end

# Example usage
if __FILE__ == $0
  sms = VonageSMS.new

  # Send SMS
  result = sms.send_sms(
    to: 'recipient_phone_number', # e.g., '15551234567'
    from: 'your_vonage_number',  # e.g., '15559876543'
    text: 'Hello from Vonage! Your message has been sent.'
  )

  puts "SMS sent with message ID: #{result[:message_id]}"
  puts "Status: #{result[:status]}"

  # Check delivery status (you might want to do this asynchronously in production)
  sleep(5) # Wait a few seconds for delivery status to update
  delivery_status = sms.check_delivery_status(result[:message_id])
  puts "Delivery status: #{delivery_status.inspect}"

  # To set up a webhook for real-time delivery notifications:
  # sms.setup_webhook('https://yourserver.com/vonage/webhook')
end
```

## Important Notes

1. **Authentication**: Vonage offers multiple authentication methods. The example uses:
   - API Key/Secret (for basic operations)
   - Application ID with private key (for more secure operations)

2. **Webhooks**: For production use, set up a webhook endpoint to receive delivery receipts in real-time rather than polling.

      from: from_number || ENV['VONAGE_DEFAULT_FROM'],
      text: message
    }

    response = @client.sms.send(params)

    }

    { error: e.message }
  end

  # Перевірка статусу доставки
  def check_delivery_status(message_id)
    response = @client.sms.delivery_receipt(message_id)
    response.body
  rescue StandardError => e
    { error: e.message }
  end
end

# Ruby Implementation for Sending SMS via Kyivstar Business Messaging API

Here's a complete Ruby implementation for sending SMS through the Kyivstar business messaging API.

## Gemfile

```ruby
# Gemfile
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'httparty', '~> 0.20'
gem 'dotenv', '~> 2.8'
```

## Implementation

```ruby
# sms_service.rb
require 'httparty'
require 'dotenv'
Dotenv.load

class KyivstarSMSService
  include HTTParty

  def initialize
    @api_key = ENV['KYIVSTAR_API_KEY'] || raise('Kyivstar API key not configured')
    @api_url = 'https://api.kyivstar.ua/api/sms/v1'
  end

  # Send a single SMS
  def send_sms(phone_number, message, sender_id = nil)
    options = {
      query: {
        api_key: @api_key,
        phone: normalize_phone_number(phone_number),
        text: message,
        sender: sender_id
      }
    }

    response = self.class.get("#{@api_url}/send", options)

    if response.success?
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      raise "Failed to send SMS: #{response.body}"
    end
  end

  # Check SMS balance
  def check_balance
    options = {
      query: {
        api_key: @api_key
      }
    }

    response = self.class.get("#{@api_url}/balance", options)

    if response.success?
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      raise "Failed to check balance: #{response.body}"
    end
  end

  private

  # Normalize phone number to international format
  def normalize_phone_number(phone)
    # Remove all non-digit characters
    cleaned = phone.gsub(/[^\d]/, '')

    # If starts with 0, add country code (380 for Ukraine)
    cleaned.start_with?('0') ? "38#{cleaned}" : cleaned
  end
end
```

    'Hello from Ruby! This is a test message.',
    'MyApp'       # Optional sender ID
  )

  puts "SMS sent successfully:"
  puts response

  # Check balance
  balance = sms_service.check_balance
  puts "\nCurrent balance:"
  puts balance

rescue => e

Here's a complete solution to send SMS through the Ukrainian provider SMS-fly, including a Gemfile and implementation code.

## Gemfile

## Implementation

```ruby
# sms_fly.rb
require 'httparty'
require 'json'

# Configuration (you can use a config file or environment variables)
class SMSFlyConfig
  attr_reader :api_url, :login, :password

  def initialize
    @api_url = 'https://api.smsfly.com/api/v2/sms/send'
    @login = ENV['SMSFLY_LOGIN'] || 'your_login'
    @password = ENV['SMSFLY_PASSWORD'] || 'your_password'
  end
end

# Main SMS sender class
class SMSFly
  include HTTParty
  base_uri 'https://api.smsfly.com'

  def initialize(config = SMSFlyConfig.new)
    @config = config
  end

  def send_sms(phone, text, sender = nil, flash = false, valid_until = nil)
    headers = {
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
    }

    body = {
      'login' => @config.login,
      'password' => @config.password,
      'phones' => [format_phone(phone)],
      'text' => text,
      'sender' => sender,
      'flash' => flash,
      'valid_until' => valid_until
    }.compact

    response = self.class.post(
      '/api/v2/sms/send',
      headers: headers,
      body: body.to_json
    )

    process_response(response)
  end

  private

  def format_phone(phone)
    # Remove all non-digit characters
    phone.gsub(/[^\d+]/, '').sub(/^\+?380/, '380')
  end

  def process_response(response)
    if response.success?
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      raise "SMS send failed: #{response.body}"
    end
  end
end
```

require 'httparty'

  include HTTParty

  # Базовий URL для API Київстара
  base_uri 'https://api.kyivstar.ua/'

  # Клас для обробки помилок
  class ApiError < StandardError; end

  # Ініціалізація з параметрами API
  def initialize(api_key, from_number = nil, logger: nil)
    @api_key = api_key
    @from_number = from_number
    @logger = logger || Logger.new($stdout)
  end

  def send_sms(to_number, message)
    @logger.info("Спроба відправки SMS на номер #{to_number}")

    # Формуємо тіло запиту
    body = {
      key: @api_key,
      from: @from_number,
      to: to_number,
      text: message
    }.to_json

    # Налаштовуємо заголовки
    headers = {
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
    }

    # Виконуємо POST-запит
    response = self.class.post(
      '/business-messages/v1/sms',
      body: body,
      headers: headers
    )

    # Обробляємо відповідь
    if response.success?

      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      error_message = "Помилка при відправці SMS: #{response.code} - #{response.body}"
      @logger.error(error_message)
      raise ApiError, error_message
    end
  rescue StandardError => e
    @logger.error("Виникла помилка: #{e.message}")
    raise ApiError, e.message
  end
end

  include HTTParty
  base_uri 'https://api.smsfly.com'

    @api_key = ENV['SMF_API_KEY']

    options = {
      query: {
        api_key: @api_key,
        signature: @signature,
        phone: phone,
        message: message,
        sender: sender
      }
    }

    self.class.get('/send/', options)
  end

  # Check SMS status
  # @param sms_id [String] ID of the SMS to check
  # @return [Hash] Response from SMS-fly API

    options = {
      query: {
        api_key: @api_key,
        signature: @signature,
        id: sms_id
      }
    }

    self.class.get('/status/', options)
  end

  # @return [Hash] Response from SMS-fly API
  def get_balance
    options = {
      query: {
        api_key: @api_key,
        signature: @signature
      }
    }

    self.class.get('/balance/', options)
  end

```ruby
# lib/kyivstar_sms.rb
require 'httparty'
require 'dotenv'
require 'json'

class KyivstarSMS
  include HTTParty

  # Базовый URL API
  BASE_URI = 'https://api.kievstar.ua/business_messages/v1'.freeze

  # Инициализация с учетными данными
  def initialize
    Dotenv.load
    @username = ENV['KIYVSTAR_USERNAME']
    @password = ENV['KIYVSTAR_PASSWORD']
    @api_key = ENV['KIYVSTAR_API_KEY']
  end

  # Отправить SMS
  def send_sms(phone_number, message)
    # Авторизация
    auth_token = authenticate

    # Подготовка данных для запроса
    headers = {
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
      'Authorization' => "Bearer #{auth_token}"
    }

    body = {
      to: format_phone_number(phone_number),
      text: message,
      sender: ENV['KIYVSTAR_SENDER_ID'] || 'Kyivstar'
    }.to_json

    # Выполнение запроса
    response = self.class.post(
      "#{BASE_URI}/messages/sms",
      body: body,
      headers: headers
    )

    handle_response(response)
  end

  # Авторизация и получение токена
  def authenticate
    auth_response = self.class.post(
      "#{BASE_URI}/auth/token",
      body: {
        username: @username,
        password: @password,
        api_key: @api_key
      }.to_json,
      headers: { 'Content-Type' => 'application/json' }
    )

    if auth_response.success?
      JSON.parse(auth_response.body)['access_token']
    else
      raise "Authentication failed: #{auth_response.body}"
    end
  end

  # Форматирование номера телефона
  def format_phone_number(phone)
    # Удаляем все нецифровые символы
    phone = phone.gsub(/[^0-9]/, '')

    # Добавляем код страны, если его нет
    unless phone.start_with?('380')
      phone = "380#{phone}"
    end

    # Возвращаем номер в формате +380XXXXXXXXXX
    "+#{phone}"
  end

  # Обработка ответа от API
  def handle_response(response)
    if response.success?
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      raise "SMS sending failed: #{response.body}"
    end
  end
end

# lib/sms_fly_client.rb
require 'httparty'
require 'dotenv'

class SmsFlyClient
  include HTTParty

  # Initialize with API credentials
  def initialize
    Dotenv.load
    @auth_token = ENV['SMS_FLY_AUTH_TOKEN'] || raise('SMS_FLY_AUTH_TOKEN is required')
    @sender_name = ENV['SMS_FLY_SENDER_NAME'] # Optional
    base_uri 'https://api.sms-fly.com'
  end

  # Send a single SMS
  def send_sms(phone, message, sender = nil)
    sender ||= @sender_name

    options = {
      query: {
        token: @auth_token,
        phones: format_phone_numbers(phone),
        text: message,
        sender: sender
      },
      headers: {
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
      }
    }

    response = self.class.post('/api/send', body: options[:query].to_json, options)

    if response.success?
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      raise "SMS-fly API error: #{response.body}"
    end
  end

  # Send multiple SMS messages
  def send_bulk_sms(phone_messages)
    # phone_messages format: { "+380671234567" => "message 1", "+380677654321" => "message 2" }
    options = {
      query: {
        token: @auth_token,
        phones: format_phone_numbers(phone_messages.keys.join(', ')),
        text: phone_messages.values.join("\n"),
        sender: @sender_name
      },
      headers: {
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
      }
    }

    response = self.class.post('/api/send', body: options[:query].to_json, options)

    if response.success?
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      raise "SMS-fly API error: #{response.body}"
    end
  end

  # Format phone numbers for API
  def format_phone_numbers(phone_numbers)
    # If single phone, convert to string
    phone_numbers = phone_numbers.to_s unless phone_numbers.is_a?(String)

    # Remove all non-digit characters except leading +
    phone_numbers.gsub(/[^\d+]/, '')
  end

  # Check balance
  def check_balance
    response = self.class.get('/api/balance', query: { token: @auth_token })

    if response.success?
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      raise "SMS-fly API error: #{response.body}"
    end
  end
end

# sms_fly_client.rb
require 'httparty'
require 'json'

class SmsFlyClient
  include HTTParty
  base_uri 'https://api.sms-fly.com/api'

  def initialize(api_key, sender_id = nil)
    @options = {
      query: {
        key: api_key
      }
    }

    @options[:query][:sender] = sender_id if sender_id.present?
  end

  # Надсилання SMS
  def send_sms(phone, message, country_code = '380')
    response = self.class.post(
      '/send',
      body: {
        phones: format_phone_number(phone, country_code),
        text: message
      }.to_json,
      headers: {
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
      }.merge(@options)
    )

    parse_response(response)
  end

  # Форматування номера телефону
  def format_phone_number(phone, country_code)
    # Прибирання всіх нецифрових символів
    phone = phone.gsub(/[^\d]/, '')

    # Якщо номер без коду країни, додаємо його
    unless phone.start_with?(country_code)
      phone = "#{country_code}#{phone}"
    end

    phone
  end

  private

  # Обробка відповіді від API
  def parse_response(response)
    if response.success?
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      raise "SMS-fly API error: #{response.body}"
    end
  end
end

## Implementation

```ruby
# lib/unisender_client.rb
require 'httparty'
require 'json'

class UnisenderClient
  include HTTParty
  base_uri 'api.unisender.com'

  # Initialize with API credentials
  def initialize(api_key, sender_name: nil, sender_email: nil, sender_company: nil)
    @options = {
      query: {
        api_key: api_key
      },
      headers: {
        'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
        'Accept' => 'application/json'
      }
    }

    # Optional sender information (for transactional emails)
    @sender_info = {
      sender_name: sender_name,
      sender_email: sender_email,
      sender_company: sender_company
    }.compact
  end

  # Send a transactional email
  def send_email(recipient_email, subject, body, fields = {})
    email_fields = {
      email: recipient_email,
      subject: subject,
      body: body
    }.merge(@sender_info).merge(fields)

    response = self.class.post(
      '/objects/9a2dd6f1749c10c6353319101d0553d8/', # Transactional email endpoint
      body: email_fields.to_json,
      query: @options[:query],
      headers: @options[:headers]
    )

    handle_response(response)
  end

  # Send an SMS message
  def send_sms(phone_number, message)
    sms_fields = {
      phone: phone_number,
      text: message
    }.merge(@sender_info)

    response = self.class.post(
      '/objects/9a2dd6f1749c10c6353319101d0553d8/', # SMS endpoint
      body: sms_fields.to_json,
      query: @options[:query],
      headers: @options[:headers]
    )

    handle_response(response)
  end

  private

  # Handle API response
  def handle_response(response)
    if response.success?
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      raise "Unisender API error: #{response.code} - #{response.body}"
    end
  end
end

require 'httparty'
require 'json'
require 'logger'
require 'dotenv/load'

class UniOne::Client
  include HTTParty
  base_uri 'https://api.unione.com.ua/'

  # Initialize the client with API credentials
  def initialize
    @logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
    @logger.level = Logger::INFO
    @api_key = ENV['UNI_ONE_API_KEY'] || raise('UNI_ONE_API_KEY environment variable not set')
    @api_secret = ENV['UNI_ONE_API_SECRET'] || raise('UNI_ONE_API_SECRET environment variable not set')
  end

  # Send a transactional SMS message
  def send_sms(phone_number, message, sender = nil, priority: 'normal')
    request_body = {
      api_key: @api_key,
      api_secret: @api_secret,
      recipient: phone_number,
      message: message,
      sender: sender,
      priority: priority
    }.to_json

    response = self.class.post(
      '/sms/send',
      body: request_body,
      headers: { 'Content-Type' => 'application/json' }
    )

    handle_response(response)
  end

  # Check the balance of the account
  def get_balance
    request_body = {
      api_key: @api_key,
      api_secret: @api_secret
    }.to_json

    response = self.class.post(
      '/balance',
      body: request_body,
      headers: { 'Content-Type' => 'application/json' }
    )

    handle_response(response)
  end

  private

  def handle_response(response)
    @logger.info("UniOne API Response: #{response.body}")

    if response.success?
      parsed_response = JSON.parse(response.body)
      { success: true, data: parsed_response }
    else
      { success: false, error: response.body }
    end
  end
end

class AirRaidMapFetcher
  # This URL is an example. In a real implementation, you would use the official
  # Ukrainian government or emergency services source for air-raid alerts.
  SOURCE_URL = 'https://example.com/ukraine-air-raids'.freeze

  def self.fetch_latest_map
    response = HTTParty.get(SOURCE_URL)
    raise "Failed to fetch data: #{response.code}" unless response.success?

    # Parse the response - this would need to be adapted based on the actual source
    doc = Nokogiri::HTML(response.body)

    # Example parsing - adjust based on actual source structure
    map_image = doc.at_xpath('//div[@class="map-container"]//img')
    timestamp_element = doc.at_xpath('//div[@class="timestamp"]')

    if map_image && timestamp_element
      map_url = map_image['src']
      timestamp = timestamp_element.text.strip

      # Ensure the URL is absolute
      if map_url.start_with?('http')
        [map_url, timestamp]
      else
        [URI.join(SOURCE_URL, map_url).to_s, timestamp]
      end
    else
      nil
    end
  rescue StandardError => e
    raise "Error fetching air-raid map: #{e.message}"
  end
end

## Implementation

```ruby
require 'httparty'
require 'dotenv'
require 'logger'

class DiiaPushNotification
  include HTTParty
  base_uri 'https://api.diia.gov.ua/v1/notifications'

  def initialize
    Dotenv.load('.env') if File.exists?('.env')
    @auth_token = ENV['DIIA_API_KEY']
    @logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
    @logger.level = Logger::INFO
  end

  # Send push notification to a single user
  # @param user_id [String] The Diia user ID
  # @param title [String] Notification title
  # @param body [String] Notification body
  # @param data [Hash] Optional additional data payload
  # @return [Hash] API response
  def send_notification(user_id, title, body, data = {})
    validate_inputs(user_id, title, body)

    headers = {
      'Authorization' => "Bearer #{@auth_token}",
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json'
    }

    payload = {
      user_id: user_id,
      title: title,
      body: body,
      data: data
    }

    @logger.info("Sending notification to user #{user_id}")

    response = self.class.post('/push', body: payload.to_json, headers: headers)

    if response.success?
      @logger.info("Notification sent successfully")
      response.parsed_response
    else
      @logger.error("Failed to send notification: #{response.body}")
      raise "Diia API Error: #{response.code} - #{response.message}"
    end
  rescue => e
    @logger.error("Error sending notification: #{e.message}")
    raise
  end

  # Send notifications to multiple users
  # @param user_ids [Array<String>] Array of Diia user IDs
  # @param title [String] Notification title
  # @param body [String] Notification body
  # @param data [Hash] Optional additional data payload
  # @return [Array<Hash>] Array of API responses
  def send_bulk_notifications(user_ids, title, body, data = {})
    validate_inputs(user_ids.first, title, body)
    user_ids.each { |id| validate_inputs(id, title, body) }

    responses = []

    user_ids.each do |user_id|
      begin
        response = send_notification(user_id, title, body, data)
        responses << response
      rescue => e
        @logger.error("Failed to send notification to user #{user_id}: #{e.message}")
        responses << { error: e.message, user_id: user_id }
      end
    end

    responses
  end

  private

  def validate_inputs(*args)
    args.each do |arg|
      if arg.blank?
        raise ArgumentError, "All parameters must be provided and non-empty"
      end
    end

    unless @auth_token
      raise RuntimeError, "Diia API key not configured. Set DIIA_API_KEY in environment."
    end
  end
end
```

Here's a complete implementation for sending push notifications through the Diia partner API, including a Gemfile and the main implementation code.

## Gemfile

gem 'httparty', '~> 0.20.0'

gem 'dotenv', '~> 2.8'
```

## Implementation

```ruby
# lib/diia_notification_service.rb
require 'httparty'
require 'jwt'
require 'dotenv'
require 'securerandom'

class DiiaNotificationService
  include HTTParty

  def initialize
    Dotenv.load
    @base_url = ENV['DIIA_API_BASE_URL'] || 'https://api.partner.diia.gov.ua'
    @api_key = ENV['DIIA_API_KEY']
    @api_secret = ENV['DIIA_API_SECRET']
    @app_id = ENV['DIIA_APP_ID']
    @issuer = ENV['DIIA_ISSUER'] || 'partner-service'
    @audience = ENV['DIIA_AUDIENCE'] || 'diia-api'
  end

  def send_notification(user_id, message, data = {})
    # Generate JWT token
    token = generate_jwt_token

    # Prepare headers
    headers = {
      'Authorization' => "Bearer #{token}",
      'Content-Type' => 'application/json',
      'X-Request-ID' => SecureRandom.uuid
    }

    # Prepare payload
    payload = {
      user_id: user_id,
      message: message,
      data: data,
      notification_type: 'push',
      timestamp: Time.now.iso8601
    }

    # Make the API request
    response = self.class.post(
      "#{@base_url}/v2/notifications/push",
      body: payload.to_json,
      headers: headers
    )

    handle_response(response)
  end

  private

  def generate_jwt_token
    payload = {
      iss: @issuer,
      aud: @audience,
      iat: Time.now.to_i,
      exp: (Time.now + 3600).to_i,
      app_id: @app_id
    }

    JWT.encode(payload, @api_secret, 'HS256')
  end

  def handle_response(response)
    case response.code
    when 200..299
      JSON.parse(response.body)
    else
      error_data = JSON.parse(response.body) rescue {}
      raise DiiaNotificationError.new(
        "Failed to send notification: #{error_data['message'] || response.body}",
        error_data
      )
    end
  end
end

class DiiaNotificationError < StandardError
  attr_reader :error_data

  def initialize(message, error_data = {})
    super(message)
    @error_data = error_data
  end
end
```

        account: @account_id,
        caller_id: caller_id,
        phone: customer_phone,
        text: message_text
      },
      headers: {
        'X-API-Key' => @api_key,
        'X-API-Secret' => @api_secret
      }
    }

    response = self.class.post('/text2call', options)

    if response.success?
      { success: true, response: response.parsed_response }
    else
